steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Observe student-led surface operations without prompting; safety intervention means further training is needed. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Observe an independent departure and traffic scan; give only task/route instructions. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Sight picture, climb, level flight and descent
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Recognizes the changing sight picture, coordinates pitch and power and levels with timely coaching; initial-flight assistance is expected. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Describe the outside attitude and cross-check the instruments. 2. Hold straight flight with coordinated rudder. 3. Establish the briefed climb airspeed and level at the assigned altitude. 4. Establish a descent, then restore level flight. 5. State what pitch and power changed.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the changing sight picture, coordinates pitch and power and levels with timely coaching; initial-flight assistance is expected.
errors: Chasing the vertical-speed indication → return eyes to the horizon and make one small pitch correction.
Ball displaced during a power change → add the appropriate rudder while keeping wings level.
steps.stop: Restore ordinary cruise if traffic, turbulence or workload prevents an outside scan; instructor takes control before an unsafe altitude or airspeed develops.
steps.reference: AFH: basic flight maneuvers; PHAK: flight controls and instruments

steps.title: Coordinated turns to headings
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains a coordinated turn, identifies altitude drift and rolls out smoothly with decreasing instructor assistance. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear toward the turn. 2. Enter the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture. 4. Anticipate rollout to the chosen heading. 5. Re-trim only when stable and reverse direction after another clearing scan.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains a coordinated turn, identifies altitude drift and rolls out smoothly with decreasing instructor assistance.
errors: Staring at the heading instrument → use it briefly and return to the outside reference.
Using rudder alone to hurry the rollout → reduce bank with coordinated aileron and rudder.
steps.stop: Roll wings level and discontinue if the turn is uncoordinated, traffic appears or the learner loses the altitude/airspeed picture.
steps.reference: AFH: turns; PHAK: adverse yaw and coordination

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the recovery altitude. 2. Set the briefed configuration and slow-flight airspeed. 3. Trim and hold heading/altitude. 4. Make gentle coordinated turns both ways. 5. Recover to cruise using the POH sequence; explain the increasing angle of attack and control pressures.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for unexpected stall warning, a loss of coordination, an unsafe altitude trend or the briefed recovery floor. No intentional spin entry.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Private ACS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Private ACS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Private ACS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Recognize an equipment failure and choose a safe action
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Prioritizes aircraft control, chooses the correct checklist and reaches a defensible landing/diversion decision without random switch changes. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Identify the abnormal indication. 2. Keep flying and state the immediate risk. 3. Apply only approved memory actions when applicable, then use the checklist. 4. Reassess systems, weather and landing options. 5. Tell the instructor/ATC what help is needed.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Prioritizes aircraft control, chooses the correct checklist and reaches a defensible landing/diversion decision without random switch changes.
errors: Treating the indication before controlling the airplane → restore control, then diagnose.
Resetting a breaker or moving a control without authority → consult the aircraft checklist and identify the consequence first.
steps.stop: End the simulation immediately for a real abnormality, distraction from traffic/terrain or any effect on essential equipment.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency procedures; POH: systems and abnormal checklists

steps.title: Simulated engine failure and emergency approach
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains glide control, selects a reachable site early and manages checklist/communications without losing the landing plan. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Establish the POH glide condition. 2. Select a reachable suitable site and plan the approach. 3. Perform approved checklist actions or verbalize unsafe-to-simulate actions. 4. Brief occupants and communications. 5. Evaluate whether the site remains reachable, then recover at the briefed gate.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains glide control, selects a reachable site early and manages checklist/communications without losing the landing plan.
errors: Searching indefinitely for the perfect field → select a suitable reachable option and refine it.
Trying to stretch the glide → maintain the POH glide condition and revise the landing plan.
steps.stop: Recover with power at the prebriefed safe altitude/position or earlier for traffic, terrain, a poor glide plan or aircraft concerns. No surprise engine shutdown or off-airport touchdown.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency approach; Private ACS: Emergency Approach and Landing; POH

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Assess an independent arrival and landing; provide safety intervention if needed and record it. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.

steps.title: Recognize an equipment failure and choose a safe action

Look for this task-specific result: Prioritizes aircraft control, chooses the correct checklist and reaches a defensible landing/diversion decision without random switch changes. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Identify the abnormal indication. 2. Keep flying and state the immediate risk. 3. Apply only approved memory actions when applicable, then use the checklist. 4. Reassess systems, weather and landing options. 5. Tell the instructor/ATC what help is needed.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Prioritizes aircraft control, chooses the correct checklist and reaches a defensible landing/diversion decision without random switch changes.
errors: Treating the indication before controlling the airplane → restore control, then diagnose.
Resetting a breaker or moving a control without authority → consult the aircraft checklist and identify the consequence first.
steps.stop: End the simulation immediately for a real abnormality, distraction from traffic/terrain or any effect on essential equipment.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency procedures; POH: systems and abnormal checklists

steps.title: Simulated engine failure and emergency approach

steps.student: 1. Establish the POH glide condition. 2. Select a reachable suitable site and plan the approach. 3. Perform approved checklist actions or verbalize unsafe-to-simulate actions. 4. steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.

errors: Searching indefinitely for the perfect field → select a suitable reachable option and refine it.

Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.

steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

debrief: Ask the student to reconstruct one control/decision sequence and identify the earliest cue of the largest error.
Compare the first and last attempt using observable aircraft control and decisions; separate assisted practice from independent evidence.

Use the POH walkaround and fuel/oil checks. Assess defects instead of assuming that a checklist tick means airworthy.

steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Have the student brief and fly the departure, diagnosing any drift/airspeed issue after a safe climb. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Short-field takeoff and landing
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use POH performance, actual runway conditions and a selected obstacle/aiming point. Demonstrate the approved takeoff setup, obstacle-clearance climb and transition. On return show stabilized approach speed, precise touchdown and approved stopping technique.
steps.student: 1. Calculate usable runway and margins. 2. Apply the POH short-field takeoff procedure. 3. Track centerline and transition only after obstacle clearance. 4. Fly a stable short-field approach at the approved speed. 5. Touch down at the selected point within the applicable lesson/ACS tolerance and stop with directional control.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one student takeoff–landing pair on introduction; two student pairs on review if the runway/pattern supports them.
steps.success: Uses performance data and approved procedures, clears the simulated obstacle and controls touchdown/stopping without chasing a spot unsafely.
errors: Rotating early to improve distance → use the POH procedure and required control speed.
Pitching down to hit the spot → go around when the approach cannot remain stable.
steps.stop: Reject or go around for performance margin, unstable speed, obstacle-clearance uncertainty or poor alignment. Simulate a field condition on a suitable runway rather than using an unsafe short strip.
steps.reference: AFH: short-field takeoffs and landings; Private ACS: short-field tasks; POH

steps.title: Soft-field takeoff and landing
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Explain how to unload the nosewheel and preserve momentum using the POH technique. Demonstrate the ground-effect transition without an early climb at insufficient airspeed. On landing show energy management and protection of the landing gear.
steps.student: 1. Brief the approved configuration and simulated surface. 2. Maintain the required nosewheel unloading and directional control during the takeoff roll. 3. Accelerate safely in ground effect as prescribed. 4. Transition to the approved climb. 5. Fly a stable soft-field approach and protect the gear through touchdown and roll.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one student takeoff–landing pair on introduction; two student pairs on review when safe.
steps.success: Maintains control and momentum, avoids premature climb and manages touchdown without dropping the nosewheel.
errors: Pulling out of ground effect before acceleration → lower the pitch appropriately and follow the POH transition.
Trying to hold the nose up beyond control margin → prioritize directional control and aircraft limits.
steps.stop: Stop the simulation for inadequate surface/runway suitability or go around for an unstable approach. Use actual soft surfaces only when approved and suitable.
steps.reference: AFH: soft-field takeoffs and landings; Private ACS: soft-field tasks; POH

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Clear the area, identify configuration limits and explain the selected slow-flight condition. Reduce power while maintaining altitude, configure in the POH sequence and coordinate added power. Show gentle turns and a deliberate return to cruise.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the recovery altitude. 2. Set the briefed configuration and slow-flight airspeed. 3. Trim and hold heading/altitude. 4. Make gentle coordinated turns both ways. 5. Recover to cruise using the POH sequence; explain the increasing angle of attack and control pressures.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for unexpected stall warning, a loss of coordination, an unsafe altitude trend or the briefed recovery floor. No intentional spin entry.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Private ACS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: From a safe altitude, show an approach-type full stall with coordinated controls. Identify the first warning and the full-stall indication, then reduce angle of attack, add approved power and clean up in the POH sequence. Contrast the entry with and without flaps.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One entry with flaps and one without on introduction; on review add one briefed turning entry only after straight entries are safe.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Private ACS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Demonstrate the approved departure configuration and controlled pitch-up at the briefed power. Show the rudder required as speed decreases. At the full stall, reduce angle of attack, maintain coordination and restore a safe climb according to the POH.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One straight entry, then the other approved configuration or a shallow turning entry on a review lesson; never rush the reset.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Private ACS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

Use the POH walkaround and fuel/oil checks. Assess defects instead of assuming that a checklist tick means airworthy.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Have the student lead the start/taxi checks; coach only a diagnosed error after stopping safely. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit

For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Navigate by landmarks and magnetic compass

Compare planned and actual time/fuel. Demonstrate a concise position report or Flight Service contact when useful, without letting communications replace lookout.
steps.student: 1. Orient the chart and identify two independent position clues. 2. Fly the planned heading with wind correction. 3. Mark actual checkpoint time and revise ETA/fuel. 4. Scan weather and airspace ahead. 5. Explain the next landmark and landing alternative; make the assigned radio contact at a low-workload time.
steps.repetitions: At least three checkpoint fixes and two time/fuel updates; use the source route distances rather than a generic local circuit.
steps.success: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan.
errors: Mistaking one similar feature for the checkpoint → verify with a second independent landmark.
Ignoring time/fuel after a wind change → update groundspeed, ETA and reserves at the next checkpoint.
steps.stop: Divert or terminate the exercise for deteriorating weather, uncertain position, unsafe fuel margin or airspace risk; GPS may be used by the instructor for safety without replacing the assigned visual-navigation exercise.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation; AFH: cross-country flight; current charts, Chart Supplement and AIM

steps.title: Arrive, land and depart at an unfamiliar airport
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Before arrival, review current runway, pattern, traffic and taxi information. Show how to identify the airport/runway visually, make proper non-towered reports or follow a clearance, then stop at a safe place to review departure information.
steps.student: 1. Confirm destination position, runway/wind, published pattern and landing performance. 2. Establish radio awareness and visually identify traffic. 3. Join the correct pattern and fly a stable approach. 4. Land, clear and complete checks before heads-down taxi work. 5. Review departure/taxi routing before taking off again.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival–landing–departure at each required destination; do not omit a source-required airport to meet the clock.
steps.success: Finds the correct airport/runway, integrates safely with traffic and handles taxi/departure without instructor navigation rescue.
errors: Descending toward a guessed airport → remain safe and verify the airport before committing.
Programming or folding charts while crossing a runway → stop at a safe location and perform the task there.
steps.stop: Go around or divert if airport identity, runway suitability, traffic or weather is uncertain; obtain any required clearance before entering controlled movement/runway areas.
steps.reference: AIM: airport operations; current Chart Supplement, airport diagram and POH

Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.

errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.

steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure

Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Observe student-led surface operations without prompting; safety intervention means further training is needed. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Observe an independent departure and traffic scan; give only task/route instructions. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Short-field takeoff and landing
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Uses performance data and approved procedures, clears the simulated obstacle and controls touchdown/stopping without chasing a spot unsafely. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Calculate usable runway and margins. 2. Apply the POH short-field takeoff procedure. 3. Track centerline and transition only after obstacle clearance. 4. Fly a stable short-field approach at the approved speed. 5. Touch down at the selected point within the applicable lesson/ACS tolerance and stop with directional control.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Uses performance data and approved procedures, clears the simulated obstacle and controls touchdown/stopping without chasing a spot unsafely.
errors: Rotating early to improve distance → use the POH procedure and required control speed.
Pitching down to hit the spot → go around when the approach cannot remain stable.
steps.stop: Reject or go around for performance margin, unstable speed, obstacle-clearance uncertainty or poor alignment. Simulate a field condition on a suitable runway rather than using an unsafe short strip.
steps.reference: AFH: short-field takeoffs and landings; Private ACS: short-field tasks; POH

steps.title: Soft-field takeoff and landing
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains control and momentum, avoids premature climb and manages touchdown without dropping the nosewheel. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Brief the approved configuration and simulated surface. 2. Maintain the required nosewheel unloading and directional control during the takeoff roll. 3. Accelerate safely in ground effect as prescribed. 4. Transition to the approved climb. 5. Fly a stable soft-field approach and protect the gear through touchdown and roll.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains control and momentum, avoids premature climb and manages touchdown without dropping the nosewheel.
errors: Pulling out of ground effect before acceleration → lower the pitch appropriately and follow the POH transition.
Trying to hold the nose up beyond control margin → prioritize directional control and aircraft limits.
steps.stop: Stop the simulation for inadequate surface/runway suitability or go around for an unstable approach. Use actual soft surfaces only when approved and suitable.
steps.reference: AFH: soft-field takeoffs and landings; Private ACS: soft-field tasks; POH

steps.title: Navigate by landmarks and magnetic compass
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Orient the chart and identify two independent position clues. 2. Fly the planned heading with wind correction. 3. Mark actual checkpoint time and revise ETA/fuel. 4. Scan weather and airspace ahead. 5. Explain the next landmark and landing alternative; make the assigned radio contact at a low-workload time.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan.
errors: Mistaking one similar feature for the checkpoint → verify with a second independent landmark.
Ignoring time/fuel after a wind change → update groundspeed, ETA and reserves at the next checkpoint.
steps.stop: Divert or terminate the exercise for deteriorating weather, uncertain position, unsafe fuel margin or airspace risk; GPS may be used by the instructor for safety without replacing the assigned visual-navigation exercise.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation; AFH: cross-country flight; current charts, Chart Supplement and AIM

steps.title: Choose and fly a diversion
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Chooses early, keeps flying while planning and selects an alternative with safe fuel, terrain and weather margins. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. State the reason to abandon the original plan. 2. Choose a reachable suitable airport. 3. Estimate heading, distance, time and fuel. 4. Check terrain, airspace, weather and runway information. 5. Fly toward it, refine the estimate and explain the new decision gates.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Chooses early, keeps flying while planning and selects an alternative with safe fuel, terrain and weather margins.
errors: Choosing the nearest symbol without checking suitability → verify runway, weather and airport status.
Continuing the old course while calculating → establish a safe interim heading and workload plan.
steps.stop: End the scenario and provide needed assistance if actual position, weather, terrain or fuel margin is threatened. Do not continue toward a fictitious hazard.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation and aeronautical decision-making; Private ACS: Diversion

steps.title: Recover an uncertain position
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes loss of confidence, asks for help early and re-establishes position without compromising control, fuel or airspace. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Admit uncertainty promptly. 2. Maintain control and a safe altitude/course. 3. Check last known position, elapsed time and fuel. 4. Use appropriate navigation/ATC assistance to establish position. 5. Choose a safe landing plan rather than wandering.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes loss of confidence, asks for help early and re-establishes position without compromising control, fuel or airspace.
errors: Continuing random turns while searching → stabilize the airplane and work from the last known fix.
Delaying a radio request through embarrassment → state uncertainty and request assistance early.
steps.stop: Stop any simulation before actual uncertainty occurs; for a real lost condition, prioritize safety and obtain assistance. Never intentionally get lost on solo.
steps.reference: PHAK: lost procedures; AIM: assistance and communications

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Assess an independent arrival and landing; provide safety intervention if needed and record it. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

Compare the first and last attempt using observable aircraft control and decisions; separate assisted practice from independent evidence.
Record actual flight/instrument time, route and full-stop counts as applicable outside this app. Agree on the next specific exercise and any carry-forward gate.
preflightGuide: Student checks actual aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading and fuel; instructor verifies suitability before approving movement.
Use the POH walkaround and fuel/oil checks. Assess defects instead of assuming that a checklist tick means airworthy.

lessons.title: Day cross-country: dead reckoning and 30-minute instrument introduction
lessons.summary: Teach predictions from heading/time/wind and introduce instrument control during a VFR cross-country. Preserve the 30-minute instrument subset inside the 90-minute flight target.
briefing: Use the actual aircraft POH/AFM and supplements to agree on speeds, configuration limits, takeoff/landing margins and safe recovery boundaries. Confirm weather, airspace, fuel, personal readiness and a return/diversion plan.
Agree on positive control transfer, who maintains the traffic scan and which simulations are permitted. No intentional spins, surprise engine shutdowns or unsafe low-altitude emergency simulations.

Preview today’s ordered flight blocks: Dead reckoning and in-flight prediction; Basic instrument control under a view-limiting device; Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery; VOR navigation and radar/ATC services when available; GPS route, nearest airport and safe automation.

Bring current charts, Chart Supplement/airport diagrams, a weather/NOTAM briefing, route/heading/time/fuel log and alternatives. Check each source-required distance/airport/landing against the actual route; calculated flight duration and reserves decide the booking length.

Brief view-limiter control transfers and instructor lookout. Instrument minutes are inside the flight target, not additional time. Count actual time flown solely by reference to instruments and restore visual flight immediately when safety requires it.
prerequisites: Complete prerequisite ground preparation and demonstrate safe control before adding the next maneuver.
Use the previous flight’s unresolved items to decide whether this mission is ready to begin.
Aircraft instruments are serviceable; a qualified instructor provides lookout/control supervision for view-limited VFR training.
objectives: Teach predictions from heading/time/wind and introduce instrument control during a VFR cross-country. Preserve the 30-minute instrument subset inside the 90-minute flight target.
Explain the setup, fly the assigned exercise, diagnose the largest error and demonstrate a corrected repeat when the budget safely permits.
lessons.timingNote: Thirty instrument minutes overlap the flight target. VOR and autopilot exercises depend on installed, approved equipment; absent equipment is conditional, not an accomplished task.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Have the student lead the start/taxi checks; coach only a diagnosed error after stopping safely. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Have the student brief and fly the departure, diagnosing any drift/airspeed issue after a safe climb. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Dead reckoning and in-flight prediction
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show how the planned course, wind correction, groundspeed and leg time produce a predicted position. At the next visual checkpoint compare prediction with observation, then revise the remaining leg time and fuel estimate.
steps.student: 1. Record departure/checkpoint time. 2. Fly the calculated heading. 3. Predict when and where the next checkpoint should appear. 4. Verify with pilotage and revise wind/groundspeed. 5. Recompute ETA and fuel for the next leg.
steps.repetitions: Two predicted checkpoints and two independent checks of the prediction.
steps.success: Uses heading and elapsed time to predict position and notices a discrepancy before it becomes a lost-position problem.
errors: Recalculating heads-down for too long → write only essentials and pause calculation while controlling/looking outside.
Accepting a predicted fix without visual confirmation → compare with two ground features.
steps.stop: Suspend calculation for traffic, workload, worsening weather or position uncertainty; aviate and use an appropriate navigation/ATC safety resource.
steps.reference: PHAK: dead reckoning and wind correction; Private ACS: Navigation

steps.title: Basic instrument control under a view-limiting device
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Establish instructor lookout and a positive control transfer before applying the view limiter. Demonstrate attitude-led straight flight, heading changes, constant-airspeed climbs/descents and level-offs. Explain a short cross-check and small corrections; this is VFR training with a safety lookout.
steps.student: 1. Accept the view limiter only after control/communication agreement. 2. Stabilize straight-and-level flight using the instruments. 3. Fly assigned heading changes. 4. Climb and descend at the assigned airspeed and level off. 5. Recover normal visual flight when instructed.
steps.repetitions: Two heading changes each way plus one climb and one descent with level-offs; count only actual view-limited instrument time.
steps.success: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively.
errors: Fixating on one instrument → cross-check attitude, performance and supporting instruments.
Making large alternating corrections → return to the known attitude/power and make a small correction.
steps.stop: Remove the view limiter or transfer control immediately for traffic, turbulence, spatial disorientation or unsafe control; instructor retains outside vigilance. No actual IMC without appropriate qualifications/clearance.
steps.reference: AFH: basic instrument control; Private ACS: Basic Instrument Maneuvers

steps.title: Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Agree on control transfers and modest, aircraft-approved setup boundaries. Demonstrate recognition of a nose-high or nose-low instrument picture and the POH/FAA recovery priorities. The instructor establishes the attitude and maintains traffic/terrain clearance.
steps.student: 1. Identify nose-high or nose-low from the instrument cross-check. 2. Apply the appropriate power, pitch and bank recovery sequence. 3. Avoid excess load or airspeed. 4. Re-establish stable flight. 5. Explain the cue that made the attitude clear.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated and one student recovery for each attitude on introduction; one student recovery each way on review/check.
steps.success: Recognizes the attitude correctly and restores controlled flight without pulling through excessive bank or exceeding aircraft limits.
errors: Treating a nose-low/high-bank condition by pulling first → use the correct bank/pitch recovery sequence.
Using a single instrument without cross-check → verify the attitude with the supporting indications.
steps.stop: Instructor takes control immediately for incorrect recovery, excessive speed/load, disorientation or an approaching safe-altitude boundary; no extreme attitudes or intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: unusual attitudes; Private ACS: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes; POH

steps.title: VOR navigation and radar/ATC services when available
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: If equipped and supported by a usable signal, show tuning, identification, course selection and sensing. Demonstrate an intercept and tracking correction. Brief when radar/flight-following assistance helps and how to request it without surrendering VFR responsibility.
steps.student: 1. Verify the facility and usable signal. 2. Set the desired course and interpret TO/FROM/sensing. 3. Intercept with a reasonable angle. 4. Track with wind correction and cross-check position visually. 5. Make the assigned radar-service request when appropriate.
steps.repetitions: One intercept and a tracked segment; one concise ATC service request or a parked rehearsal if service is unavailable.
steps.success: Identifies and interprets the aid correctly, tracks without chasing the needle and keeps VFR terrain/weather responsibility.
errors: Tracking without checking identification → identify the signal before using it.
Turning the wrong way from reverse sensing → recheck course and TO/FROM before intercepting.
steps.stop: Stop the navigation exercise for unreliable signal, unsafe course, weather/terrain conflict or excessive heads-down time. Mark unavailable equipment as not applicable, not as demonstrated.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation systems; AIM: VOR and radar services

steps.title: GPS route, nearest airport and safe automation
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show the installed unit’s approved operating method for checking the active route, sequencing and nearest-airport page. Compare database information with current charts and airport suitability. If an autopilot is installed, demonstrate mode/annunciation checks and immediate manual override using its supplement.
steps.student: 1. Verify the active waypoint/route against the chart. 2. Confirm mode and sequencing. 3. Use nearest to find options, then check runway/weather/fuel suitability. 4. If approved and equipped, engage a briefed autopilot mode, monitor it and disengage manually. 5. Keep a visual position cross-check.
steps.repetitions: One route verification, one nearest-airport choice and one monitored automation engage/disengage cycle if equipped.
steps.success: Understands what the installed unit is commanding, chooses a suitable option rather than merely the closest airport and can return promptly to manual control.
errors: Following the magenta line without checking the waypoint → verify the active leg against the planned course.
Assuming an armed mode is active → read the actual annunciation and monitor the flight path.
steps.stop: Disengage automation and fly manually for unexpected behavior, mode uncertainty or unsafe path; discontinue programming for high workload. Use only aircraft-approved equipment procedures.
steps.reference: Installed avionics/autopilot supplement; PHAK: navigation; Private ACS: Navigation Systems

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation

steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.

steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

Explain a short cross-check and small corrections; this is VFR training with a safety lookout.
steps.student: 1. Accept the view limiter only after control/communication agreement. 2. Stabilize straight-and-level flight using the instruments. 3. Fly assigned heading changes. 4. Climb and descend at the assigned airspeed and level off. 5. Recover normal visual flight when instructed.
steps.repetitions: Two heading changes each way plus one climb and one descent with level-offs; count only actual view-limited instrument time.
steps.success: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively.
errors: Fixating on one instrument → cross-check attitude, performance and supporting instruments.
Making large alternating corrections → return to the known attitude/power and make a small correction.
steps.stop: Remove the view limiter or transfer control immediately for traffic, turbulence, spatial disorientation or unsafe control; instructor retains outside vigilance. No actual IMC without appropriate qualifications/clearance.
steps.reference: AFH: basic instrument control; Private ACS: Basic Instrument Maneuvers

steps.title: Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Agree on control transfers and modest, aircraft-approved setup boundaries. Demonstrate recognition of a nose-high or nose-low instrument picture and the POH/FAA recovery priorities. The instructor establishes the attitude and maintains traffic/terrain clearance.
steps.student: 1. Identify nose-high or nose-low from the instrument cross-check. 2. Apply the appropriate power, pitch and bank recovery sequence. 3. Avoid excess load or airspeed. 4. Re-establish stable flight. 5. Explain the cue that made the attitude clear.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated and one student recovery for each attitude on introduction; one student recovery each way on review/check.
steps.success: Recognizes the attitude correctly and restores controlled flight without pulling through excessive bank or exceeding aircraft limits.
errors: Treating a nose-low/high-bank condition by pulling first → use the correct bank/pitch recovery sequence.
Using a single instrument without cross-check → verify the attitude with the supporting indications.
steps.stop: Instructor takes control immediately for incorrect recovery, excessive speed/load, disorientation or an approaching safe-altitude boundary; no extreme attitudes or intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: unusual attitudes; Private ACS: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes; POH

errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.

steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.

errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.

steps.success: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively.
errors: Fixating on one instrument → cross-check attitude, performance and supporting instruments.

steps.stop: Remove the view limiter or transfer control immediately for traffic, turbulence, spatial disorientation or unsafe control; instructor retains outside vigilance. No actual IMC without appropriate qualifications/clearance.
steps.reference: AFH: basic instrument control; Private ACS: Basic Instrument Maneuvers

steps.repetitions: One demonstrated and one student recovery for each attitude on introduction; one student recovery each way on review/check.

errors: Treating a nose-low/high-bank condition by pulling first → use the correct bank/pitch recovery sequence.

steps.stop: Instructor takes control immediately for incorrect recovery, excessive speed/load, disorientation or an approaching safe-altitude boundary; no extreme attitudes or intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: unusual attitudes; Private ACS: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes; POH

steps.title: Short-field takeoff and landing
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use POH performance, actual runway conditions and a selected obstacle/aiming point. steps.student: 1. Calculate usable runway and margins. 2. Apply the POH short-field takeoff procedure. 3. Track centerline and transition only after obstacle clearance. 4. Fly a stable short-field approach at the approved speed. 5. Touch down at the selected point within the applicable lesson/ACS tolerance and stop with directional control.

steps.success: Uses performance data and approved procedures, clears the simulated obstacle and controls touchdown/stopping without chasing a spot unsafely.
errors: Rotating early to improve distance → use the POH procedure and required control speed.
Pitching down to hit the spot → go around when the approach cannot remain stable.
steps.stop: Reject or go around for performance margin, unstable speed, obstacle-clearance uncertainty or poor alignment. Simulate a field condition on a suitable runway rather than using an unsafe short strip.
steps.reference: AFH: short-field takeoffs and landings; Private ACS: short-field tasks; POH

steps.title: Soft-field takeoff and landing
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Explain how to unload the nosewheel and preserve momentum using the POH technique. Demonstrate the ground-effect transition without an early climb at insufficient airspeed. On landing show energy management and protection of the landing gear.
steps.student: 1. Brief the approved configuration and simulated surface. 2. Maintain the required nosewheel unloading and directional control during the takeoff roll. 3. Accelerate safely in ground effect as prescribed. 4. Transition to the approved climb. 5. Fly a stable soft-field approach and protect the gear through touchdown and roll.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one student takeoff–landing pair on introduction; two student pairs on review when safe.
steps.success: Maintains control and momentum, avoids premature climb and manages touchdown without dropping the nosewheel.
errors: Pulling out of ground effect before acceleration → lower the pitch appropriately and follow the POH transition.
Trying to hold the nose up beyond control margin → prioritize directional control and aircraft limits.
steps.stop: Stop the simulation for inadequate surface/runway suitability or go around for an unstable approach. Use actual soft surfaces only when approved and suitable.
steps.reference: AFH: soft-field takeoffs and landings; Private ACS: soft-field tasks; POH

errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
