steps.title: Steep turns in both directions
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current ACS tolerances. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose altitude, airspeed and rollout reference. 2. Establish the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture and cross-check altitude. 4. Complete the turn, roll out and stabilize. 5. Repeat in the other direction after clearing.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current ACS tolerances.
errors: Trying to correct altitude with bank alone → restore the briefed bank and make a small pitch/power correction.
Looking only inside → return to the outside pitch reference and make short instrument cross-checks.
steps.stop: Roll out if bank, load, airspeed or altitude approaches an aircraft limit or safe practice boundary; never chase a tolerance through unsafe control inputs.
steps.reference: AFH: steep turns; Private ACS: Steep Turns

steps.title: Rectangular course: wind correction by leg
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains safe altitude and reasonably uniform spacing, predicts drift and changes bank smoothly rather than skidding the turn. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and establish the briefed entry. 2. Hold parallel ground tracks with wind correction. 3. Change bank smoothly through each corner to preserve spacing. 4. Call the wind correction on each leg. 5. Exit without descending or tightening toward obstacles.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains safe altitude and reasonably uniform spacing, predicts drift and changes bank smoothly rather than skidding the turn.
errors: Turning too late on the fast downwind corner → anticipate the corner and use an appropriate coordinated bank.
Looking continuously at the field → alternate the reference with traffic, horizon and altitude scans.
steps.stop: Exit toward a safe area for traffic, inadequate obstacle clearance, excessive bank or an unstable altitude trend.
steps.reference: AFH: rectangular course; Private ACS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: S-turns across a road
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Crosses the reference with wings approximately level, varies bank with wind and preserves altitude and coordination. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and approach the reference as briefed. 2. Begin a coordinated turn that compensates for the wind. 3. Cross wings level and reverse the turn. 4. Adjust bank to create the second comparable arc. 5. Exit and describe the strongest drift correction.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Crosses the reference with wings approximately level, varies bank with wind and preserves altitude and coordination.
errors: Holding one bank all the way around → anticipate changing groundspeed and vary bank.
Rushing the reversal with rudder → level the wings at the reference, then enter the opposite bank together.
steps.stop: Exit if bank/altitude trend is unsafe or the chosen road has traffic/obstructions that compromise the practice area; maintain legal clearances.
steps.reference: AFH: S-turns; Private ACS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: Turns around a point
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Holds a consistent radius using coordinated bank changes, with safe altitude and a sustained traffic scan. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose a safe radius and altitude. 2. Enter as briefed. 3. Adjust bank to maintain the ground radius. 4. Keep the ball centered and scan outside. 5. Exit after a full circuit and predict corrections for a second direction.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Holds a consistent radius using coordinated bank changes, with safe altitude and a sustained traffic scan.
errors: Tightening toward the point when blown inward → reduce bank and re-establish the planned radius.
Fixating on the point → scan the horizon and traffic, then check the ground reference briefly.
steps.stop: Leave the maneuver if the required bank exceeds the practice limit, an escape route is compromised or traffic/terrain clearance becomes uncertain.
steps.reference: AFH: turns around a point; Private ACS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the recovery altitude. 2. Set the briefed configuration and slow-flight airspeed. 3. Trim and hold heading/altitude. 4. Make gentle coordinated turns both ways. 5. Recover to cruise using the POH sequence; explain the increasing angle of attack and control pressures.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for unexpected stall warning, a loss of coordination, an unsafe altitude trend or the briefed recovery floor. No intentional spin entry.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Private ACS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Private ACS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Private ACS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Basic instrument control under a view-limiting device
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Accept the view limiter only after control/communication agreement. 2. Stabilize straight-and-level flight using the instruments. 3. Fly assigned heading changes. 4. Climb and descend at the assigned airspeed and level off. 5. Recover normal visual flight when instructed.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively.
errors: Fixating on one instrument → cross-check attitude, performance and supporting instruments.
Making large alternating corrections → return to the known attitude/power and make a small correction.
steps.stop: Remove the view limiter or transfer control immediately for traffic, turbulence, spatial disorientation or unsafe control; instructor retains outside vigilance. No actual IMC without appropriate qualifications/clearance.
steps.reference: AFH: basic instrument control; Private ACS: Basic Instrument Maneuvers

steps.title: Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes the attitude correctly and restores controlled flight without pulling through excessive bank or exceeding aircraft limits. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Identify nose-high or nose-low from the instrument cross-check. 2. Apply the appropriate power, pitch and bank recovery sequence. 3. Avoid excess load or airspeed. 4. Re-establish stable flight. 5. Explain the cue that made the attitude clear.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the attitude correctly and restores controlled flight without pulling through excessive bank or exceeding aircraft limits.
errors: Treating a nose-low/high-bank condition by pulling first → use the correct bank/pitch recovery sequence.
Using a single instrument without cross-check → verify the attitude with the supporting indications.
steps.stop: Instructor takes control immediately for incorrect recovery, excessive speed/load, disorientation or an approaching safe-altitude boundary; no extreme attitudes or intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: unusual attitudes; Private ACS: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes; POH

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Assess an independent arrival and landing; provide safety intervention if needed and record it. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

completion: All required tasks are observed or explicitly finished in continued training; safe preparation, traffic awareness and control take priority over the nominal time.
The instructor evaluates the actual student performance and records any assistance or remaining deficiency before advancing the lesson.

Demonstrate applicable current Private ACS knowledge, risk management and skill without coaching. A missing task or safety intervention prevents a complete assessment; this guide grants no certificate or school examining authority.

Confirm experience, tests, endorsements and the required preparation within the applicable regulatory period separately from this mock/readiness result. Review and correct knowledge-test deficiency areas before recommendation.
debrief: Ask the student to reconstruct one control/decision sequence and identify the earliest cue of the largest error.
Compare the first and last attempt using observable aircraft control and decisions; separate assisted practice from independent evidence.
Record actual flight/instrument time, route and full-stop counts as applicable outside this app. Agree on the next specific exercise and any carry-forward gate.
preflightGuide: Student checks actual aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading and fuel; instructor verifies suitability before approving movement.
Use the POH walkaround and fuel/oil checks. Assess defects instead of assuming that a checklist tick means airworthy.
Set seats/restraints, controls, radios/charts and loose items; give an aircraft-specific passenger/control-transfer briefing. Stage-appropriate independence is assessed here.

lessons.applicability: Single-engine airplane, Part 61 adaptation. Confirm speeds, power, configuration, maneuver limitations, recovery altitudes and runway performance from the actual POH/AFM and installed supplements with the CFI before flight. The times are planning allocations; safe operation and demonstrated proficiency govern continuation.
lessons.title: Final remedial flight and instrument experience check
lessons.summary: Use the previous assessment to choose targeted corrections, then reconcile actual instrument experience. The source broad task list cannot receive adequate repetitions inside 72 minutes with 30 minutes under the view limiter.
briefing: Use the actual aircraft POH/AFM and supplements to agree on speeds, configuration limits, takeoff/landing margins and safe recovery boundaries. Confirm weather, airspace, fuel, personal readiness and a return/diversion plan.
Agree on positive control transfer, who maintains the traffic scan and which simulations are permitted. No intentional spins, surprise engine shutdowns or unsafe low-altitude emergency simulations.

Preview today’s ordered flight blocks: Basic instrument control under a view-limiting device; Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery; Steep turns in both directions; Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit.

Explain angle of attack, warning/full-stall cues, coordination and the conditions that lead from a stall to a spin. Discuss the aircraft-approved recovery; this flight demonstrates stall prevention/recovery, not intentional spins.

Brief view-limiter control transfers and instructor lookout. Instrument minutes are inside the flight target, not additional time. Count actual time flown solely by reference to instruments and restore visual flight immediately when safety requires it.
prerequisites: Complete prerequisite ground preparation and demonstrate safe control before adding the next maneuver.
Use the previous flight’s unresolved items to decide whether this mission is ready to begin.
Aircraft instruments are serviceable; a qualified instructor provides lookout/control supervision for view-limited VFR training.
objectives: Use the previous assessment to choose targeted corrections, then reconcile actual instrument experience. The source broad task list cannot receive adequate repetitions inside 72 minutes with 30 minutes under the view limiter.
Explain the setup, fly the assigned exercise, diagnose the largest error and demonstrate a corrected repeat when the budget safely permits.
lessons.timingNote: Choose the highest-priority 12-minute visual remediation block instead of assuming this entire source list is mastered. The shown default is steep turns plus slow flight. Extend/repeat to remedy any other deficiency and verify at least three actual instrument-training hours for the Part 61 airplane requirement.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Have the student lead the start/taxi checks; coach only a diagnosed error after stopping safely. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Have the student brief and fly the departure, diagnosing any drift/airspeed issue after a safe climb. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Basic instrument control under a view-limiting device
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Establish instructor lookout and a positive control transfer before applying the view limiter. Demonstrate attitude-led straight flight, heading changes, constant-airspeed climbs/descents and level-offs. Explain a short cross-check and small corrections; this is VFR training with a safety lookout.
steps.student: 1. Accept the view limiter only after control/communication agreement. 2. Stabilize straight-and-level flight using the instruments. 3. Fly assigned heading changes. 4. Climb and descend at the assigned airspeed and level off. 5. Recover normal visual flight when instructed.
steps.repetitions: Two heading changes each way plus one climb and one descent with level-offs; count only actual view-limited instrument time.
steps.success: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively.
errors: Fixating on one instrument → cross-check attitude, performance and supporting instruments.
Making large alternating corrections → return to the known attitude/power and make a small correction.
steps.stop: Remove the view limiter or transfer control immediately for traffic, turbulence, spatial disorientation or unsafe control; instructor retains outside vigilance. No actual IMC without appropriate qualifications/clearance.
steps.reference: AFH: basic instrument control; Private ACS: Basic Instrument Maneuvers

steps.title: Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Agree on control transfers and modest, aircraft-approved setup boundaries. Demonstrate recognition of a nose-high or nose-low instrument picture and the POH/FAA recovery priorities. The instructor establishes the attitude and maintains traffic/terrain clearance.
steps.student: 1. Identify nose-high or nose-low from the instrument cross-check. 2. Apply the appropriate power, pitch and bank recovery sequence. 3. Avoid excess load or airspeed. 4. Re-establish stable flight. 5. Explain the cue that made the attitude clear.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated and one student recovery for each attitude on introduction; one student recovery each way on review/check.
steps.success: Recognizes the attitude correctly and restores controlled flight without pulling through excessive bank or exceeding aircraft limits.
errors: Treating a nose-low/high-bank condition by pulling first → use the correct bank/pitch recovery sequence.
Using a single instrument without cross-check → verify the attitude with the supporting indications.
steps.stop: Instructor takes control immediately for incorrect recovery, excessive speed/load, disorientation or an approaching safe-altitude boundary; no extreme attitudes or intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: unusual attitudes; Private ACS: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes; POH

steps.title: Steep turns in both directions
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Show clearing, the current Private ACS bank target, the added back pressure/power as needed and an outside reference that reveals altitude drift. Demonstrate the rollout and a complete reset before changing direction.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose altitude, airspeed and rollout reference. 2. Establish the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture and cross-check altitude. 4. Complete the turn, roll out and stabilize. 5. Repeat in the other direction after clearing.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration followed by one student turn each way on introduction; two student turns each way on review if safe and unrushed.
steps.success: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current ACS tolerances.
errors: Trying to correct altitude with bank alone → restore the briefed bank and make a small pitch/power correction.
Looking only inside → return to the outside pitch reference and make short instrument cross-checks.

steps.reference: AFH: steep turns; Private ACS: Steep Turns

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Clear the area, identify configuration limits and explain the selected slow-flight condition. Reduce power while maintaining altitude, configure in the POH sequence and coordinate added power. Show gentle turns and a deliberate return to cruise.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the recovery altitude. 2. Set the briefed configuration and slow-flight airspeed. 3. Trim and hold heading/altitude. 4. Make gentle coordinated turns both ways. 5. Recover to cruise using the POH sequence; explain the increasing angle of attack and control pressures.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for unexpected stall warning, a loss of coordination, an unsafe altitude trend or the briefed recovery floor. No intentional spin entry.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Private ACS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.

Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.

Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.

Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.

Simulated engine failure and emergency approach: not allocated adequate practice in this target flight. Add a safe dedicated block or another flight before declaring the source lesson complete.
VOR navigation and radar/ATC services when available: not allocated adequate practice in this target flight. Add a safe dedicated block or another flight before declaring the source lesson complete.
If a required task is unobserved, unsafe or below the lesson gate, extend/continue training or assessment. Complete and verify it before progressing; elapsed minutes never substitute for proficiency.
completion: All required tasks are observed or explicitly finished in continued training; safe preparation, traffic awareness and control take priority over the nominal time.
The instructor evaluates the actual student performance and records any assistance or remaining deficiency before advancing the lesson.

Student leads the setup and control with decreasing assistance, recognizes deviations and shows a corrected repeat. Final-stage proficiency is judged against the current Private ACS, using the actual aircraft references.

Reconcile at least three actual hours of instrument training under the Part 61 single-engine-airplane experience requirement, plus any unresolved assessment task. Do not add overlapping instrument time again to flight totals.
debrief: Ask the student to reconstruct one control/decision sequence and identify the earliest cue of the largest error.
Compare the first and last attempt using observable aircraft control and decisions; separate assisted practice from independent evidence.
Record actual flight/instrument time, route and full-stop counts as applicable outside this app. Agree on the next specific exercise and any carry-forward gate.
preflightGuide: Student checks actual aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading and fuel; instructor verifies suitability before approving movement.
Use the POH walkaround and fuel/oil checks. Assess defects instead of assuming that a checklist tick means airworthy.
Set seats/restraints, controls, radios/charts and loose items; give an aircraft-specific passenger/control-transfer briefing. Stage-appropriate independence is assessed here.

preparation.title: Current Private Pilot Airplane ACS: knowledge, risk and skill review

lessons.applicability: Single-engine airplane, Part 61 adaptation. Confirm speeds, power, configuration, maneuver limitations, recovery altitudes and runway performance from the actual POH/AFM and installed supplements with the CFI before flight. The times are planning allocations; safe operation and demonstrated proficiency govern continuation.
lessons.title: Final Part 61 readiness assessment
lessons.summary: Use a complete current-ACS plan of action, the knowledge-test deficiency areas and independent performance evidence. This adaptation is a readiness assessment, not issuance of a pilot certificate or a school graduation authorization.
briefing: Use the actual aircraft POH/AFM and supplements to agree on speeds, configuration limits, takeoff/landing margins and safe recovery boundaries. Confirm weather, airspace, fuel, personal readiness and a return/diversion plan.
Agree on positive control transfer, who maintains the traffic scan and which simulations are permitted. No intentional spins, surprise engine shutdowns or unsafe low-altitude emergency simulations.

Preview today’s ordered flight blocks: Navigate by landmarks and magnetic compass; Choose and fly a diversion; Recover an uncertain position; Steep turns in both directions; Rectangular course: wind correction by leg; S-turns across a road; Turns around a point; Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit; Full power-off stalls: approach scenario; Full power-on stalls: departure scenario; Basic instrument control under a view-limiting device; Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery.

Explain angle of attack, warning/full-stall cues, coordination and the conditions that lead from a stall to a spin. Discuss the aircraft-approved recovery; this flight demonstrates stall prevention/recovery, not intentional spins.

State the assessment rules before starting: no coaching during the attempt, safety intervention is documented, and unobserved/unsafe tasks require more training or a continued assessment. Use current ACS standards where applicable; Stage I uses the solo-readiness gate.

Use the parked oral to assess certificates/endorsements, airworthiness, current weather, aircraft performance/systems, airspace and human factors. Include airport signs/markings/lighting and emergency/survival equipment where in scope. Final assessments also cover the planned cross-country, night preparation and knowledge-test deficiency codes.

Brief view-limiter control transfers and instructor lookout. Instrument minutes are inside the flight target, not additional time. Count actual time flown solely by reference to instruments and restore visual flight immediately when safety requires it.
prerequisites: Complete prerequisite ground preparation and demonstrate safe control before adding the next maneuver.
Use the previous flight’s unresolved items to decide whether this mission is ready to begin.
Finish required training and prepare an assessor plan of action. Identify prior deficiencies and unobserved tasks before the assessment.
Aircraft instruments are serviceable; a qualified instructor provides lookout/control supervision for view-limited VFR training.
objectives: Use a complete current-ACS plan of action, the knowledge-test deficiency areas and independent performance evidence. This adaptation is a readiness assessment, not issuance of a pilot certificate or a school graduation authorization.
Show independent preparation, control, hazard recognition and safe decisions; record safety interventions and tasks not observed.
lessons.timingNote: The 120-minute target may need a continued assessment for the full ACS scope. Instrument time is an 18-minute overlapping subset. Do not issue a practical-test recommendation until the required tasks, knowledge-test deficiencies, experience and endorsements have all been satisfied.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Observe student-led surface operations without prompting; safety intervention means further training is needed. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Observe an independent departure and traffic scan; give only task/route instructions. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Navigate by landmarks and magnetic compass
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Orient the chart and identify two independent position clues. 2. Fly the planned heading with wind correction. 3. Mark actual checkpoint time and revise ETA/fuel. 4. Scan weather and airspace ahead. 5. Explain the next landmark and landing alternative; make the assigned radio contact at a low-workload time.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan.
errors: Mistaking one similar feature for the checkpoint → verify with a second independent landmark.
Ignoring time/fuel after a wind change → update groundspeed, ETA and reserves at the next checkpoint.
steps.stop: Divert or terminate the exercise for deteriorating weather, uncertain position, unsafe fuel margin or airspace risk; GPS may be used by the instructor for safety without replacing the assigned visual-navigation exercise.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation; AFH: cross-country flight; current charts, Chart Supplement and AIM

steps.title: Choose and fly a diversion
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Chooses early, keeps flying while planning and selects an alternative with safe fuel, terrain and weather margins. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. State the reason to abandon the original plan. 2. Choose a reachable suitable airport. 3. Estimate heading, distance, time and fuel. 4. Check terrain, airspace, weather and runway information. 5. Fly toward it, refine the estimate and explain the new decision gates.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Chooses early, keeps flying while planning and selects an alternative with safe fuel, terrain and weather margins.
errors: Choosing the nearest symbol without checking suitability → verify runway, weather and airport status.
Continuing the old course while calculating → establish a safe interim heading and workload plan.
steps.stop: End the scenario and provide needed assistance if actual position, weather, terrain or fuel margin is threatened. Do not continue toward a fictitious hazard.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation and aeronautical decision-making; Private ACS: Diversion

steps.title: Recover an uncertain position
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes loss of confidence, asks for help early and re-establishes position without compromising control, fuel or airspace. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Admit uncertainty promptly. 2. Maintain control and a safe altitude/course. 3. Check last known position, elapsed time and fuel. 4. Use appropriate navigation/ATC assistance to establish position. 5. Choose a safe landing plan rather than wandering.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes loss of confidence, asks for help early and re-establishes position without compromising control, fuel or airspace.
errors: Continuing random turns while searching → stabilize the airplane and work from the last known fix.
Delaying a radio request through embarrassment → state uncertainty and request assistance early.
steps.stop: Stop any simulation before actual uncertainty occurs; for a real lost condition, prioritize safety and obtain assistance. Never intentionally get lost on solo.
steps.reference: PHAK: lost procedures; AIM: assistance and communications

steps.title: Steep turns in both directions
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current ACS tolerances. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose altitude, airspeed and rollout reference. 2. Establish the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture and cross-check altitude. 4. Complete the turn, roll out and stabilize. 5. Repeat in the other direction after clearing.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current ACS tolerances.
errors: Trying to correct altitude with bank alone → restore the briefed bank and make a small pitch/power correction.
Looking only inside → return to the outside pitch reference and make short instrument cross-checks.
steps.stop: Roll out if bank, load, airspeed or altitude approaches an aircraft limit or safe practice boundary; never chase a tolerance through unsafe control inputs.
steps.reference: AFH: steep turns; Private ACS: Steep Turns

steps.title: Rectangular course: wind correction by leg
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains safe altitude and reasonably uniform spacing, predicts drift and changes bank smoothly rather than skidding the turn. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and establish the briefed entry. 2. Hold parallel ground tracks with wind correction. 3. Change bank smoothly through each corner to preserve spacing. 4. Call the wind correction on each leg. 5. Exit without descending or tightening toward obstacles.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains safe altitude and reasonably uniform spacing, predicts drift and changes bank smoothly rather than skidding the turn.
errors: Turning too late on the fast downwind corner → anticipate the corner and use an appropriate coordinated bank.
Looking continuously at the field → alternate the reference with traffic, horizon and altitude scans.
steps.stop: Exit toward a safe area for traffic, inadequate obstacle clearance, excessive bank or an unstable altitude trend.
steps.reference: AFH: rectangular course; Private ACS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: S-turns across a road
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Crosses the reference with wings approximately level, varies bank with wind and preserves altitude and coordination. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and approach the reference as briefed. 2. Begin a coordinated turn that compensates for the wind. 3. Cross wings level and reverse the turn. 4. Adjust bank to create the second comparable arc. 5. Exit and describe the strongest drift correction.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Crosses the reference with wings approximately level, varies bank with wind and preserves altitude and coordination.
errors: Holding one bank all the way around → anticipate changing groundspeed and vary bank.
Rushing the reversal with rudder → level the wings at the reference, then enter the opposite bank together.
steps.stop: Exit if bank/altitude trend is unsafe or the chosen road has traffic/obstructions that compromise the practice area; maintain legal clearances.
steps.reference: AFH: S-turns; Private ACS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: Turns around a point
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Holds a consistent radius using coordinated bank changes, with safe altitude and a sustained traffic scan. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose a safe radius and altitude. 2. Enter as briefed. 3. Adjust bank to maintain the ground radius. 4. Keep the ball centered and scan outside. 5. Exit after a full circuit and predict corrections for a second direction.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Holds a consistent radius using coordinated bank changes, with safe altitude and a sustained traffic scan.
errors: Tightening toward the point when blown inward → reduce bank and re-establish the planned radius.
Fixating on the point → scan the horizon and traffic, then check the ground reference briefly.
steps.stop: Leave the maneuver if the required bank exceeds the practice limit, an escape route is compromised or traffic/terrain clearance becomes uncertain.
steps.reference: AFH: turns around a point; Private ACS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the recovery altitude. 2. Set the briefed configuration and slow-flight airspeed. 3. Trim and hold heading/altitude. 4. Make gentle coordinated turns both ways. 5. Recover to cruise using the POH sequence; explain the increasing angle of attack and control pressures.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes reduced control effectiveness, stays coordinated and exits promptly when asked; use the current ACS condition for advanced assessment, not obsolete continuous-warning technique.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for unexpected stall warning, a loss of coordination, an unsafe altitude trend or the briefed recovery floor. No intentional spin entry.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Private ACS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Private ACS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Private ACS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Basic instrument control under a view-limiting device
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Accept the view limiter only after control/communication agreement. 2. Stabilize straight-and-level flight using the instruments. 3. Fly assigned heading changes. 4. Climb and descend at the assigned airspeed and level off. 5. Recover normal visual flight when instructed.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Controls the airplane by reference to instruments with the assistance appropriate to this lesson, uses small corrections and transfers control positively.
errors: Fixating on one instrument → cross-check attitude, performance and supporting instruments.
Making large alternating corrections → return to the known attitude/power and make a small correction.
steps.stop: Remove the view limiter or transfer control immediately for traffic, turbulence, spatial disorientation or unsafe control; instructor retains outside vigilance. No actual IMC without appropriate qualifications/clearance.
steps.reference: AFH: basic instrument control; Private ACS: Basic Instrument Maneuvers

steps.title: Instrument unusual-attitude recognition and recovery
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes the attitude correctly and restores controlled flight without pulling through excessive bank or exceeding aircraft limits. Apply the current ACS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Identify nose-high or nose-low from the instrument cross-check. 2. Apply the appropriate power, pitch and bank recovery sequence. 3. Avoid excess load or airspeed. 4. Re-establish stable flight. 5. Explain the cue that made the attitude clear.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the attitude correctly and restores controlled flight without pulling through excessive bank or exceeding aircraft limits.
errors: Treating a nose-low/high-bank condition by pulling first → use the correct bank/pitch recovery sequence.
Using a single instrument without cross-check → verify the attitude with the supporting indications.
steps.stop: Instructor takes control immediately for incorrect recovery, excessive speed/load, disorientation or an approaching safe-altitude boundary; no extreme attitudes or intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: unusual attitudes; Private ACS: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes; POH

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Assess an independent arrival and landing; provide safety intervention if needed and record it. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

If a required task is unobserved, unsafe or below the lesson gate, extend/continue training or assessment. Complete and verify it before progressing; elapsed minutes never substitute for proficiency.
completion: All required tasks are observed or explicitly finished in continued training; safe preparation, traffic awareness and control take priority over the nominal time.
The instructor evaluates the actual student performance and records any assistance or remaining deficiency before advancing the lesson.

Demonstrate applicable current Private ACS knowledge, risk management and skill without coaching. A missing task or safety intervention prevents a complete assessment; this guide grants no certificate or school examining authority.

Confirm experience, tests, endorsements and the required preparation within the applicable regulatory period separately from this mock/readiness result. Review and correct knowledge-test deficiency areas before recommendation.
debrief: Ask the student to reconstruct one control/decision sequence and identify the earliest cue of the largest error.
Compare the first and last attempt using observable aircraft control and decisions; separate assisted practice from independent evidence.
Record actual flight/instrument time, route and full-stop counts as applicable outside this app. Agree on the next specific exercise and any carry-forward gate.
preflightGuide: Student checks actual aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading and fuel; instructor verifies suitability before approving movement.
Use the POH walkaround and fuel/oil checks. Assess defects instead of assuming that a checklist tick means airworthy.
Set seats/restraints, controls, radios/charts and loose items; give an aircraft-specific passenger/control-transfer briefing. Stage-appropriate independence is assessed here.

lessons.title: First flight: control, trim and the traffic pattern
lessons.summary: Introduce the airplane as a controllable system. Build an outside sight picture and positive control transfer; the instructor still demonstrates and assists takeoff and landing.
objectives: Introduce the airplane as a controllable system. Build an outside sight picture and positive control transfer; the instructor still demonstrates and assists takeoff and landing.
Use safe setup/control, recognize the earliest error cue and show a corrected repeat or independent assessment evidence appropriate to the lesson.
prerequisites: Complete the prerequisite ground preparation and resolve unsafe/deficient items from the preceding flight.
Have the instructor verify actual aircraft eligibility, operational limits and current Sport privileges/endorsements for the proposed mission.
briefing: Check the actual aircraft eligibility, limitations and installed supplements with current Sport privileges/endorsements. Select POH speeds/configurations, weather/crosswind limits, runway margins, fuel, practice area and safe recovery boundaries before movement.

Agree on positive control transfer, instructor lookout and authorized simulations. Keep aircraft control, traffic and terrain ahead of discussion; no intentional spins, surprise shutdowns or hazardous low-altitude failures.
Preview the ordered exercises: Sight picture, climb, level flight and descent; Airspeed changes and trim; Coordinated turns to headings.
preflightGuide: Review aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading, fuel and current Sport aircraft/operation eligibility. Instructor verifies suitability and authorization.
Use the actual POH/AFM walkaround, fuel/oil and defect assessment. Set seats/restraints/controls, secure loose items and prepare charts/radios.
Give the aircraft-specific passenger/positive-control-transfer briefing; on solo review the specific mission and ground contact plan before release.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Model each action and explain it before the learner attempts it. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Demonstrate the outside references and coach control inputs; retain responsibility for the landing/takeoff outcome. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Sight picture, climb, level flight and descent
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: At a safe cruise altitude, point out the horizon position for level flight. Show how a small pitch change moves the horizon, then coordinate power for a climb. Anticipate level-off, set cruise power and trim. Show a descent and level-off in the same order.
steps.student: 1. Describe the outside attitude and cross-check the instruments. 2. Hold straight flight with coordinated rudder. 3. Establish the briefed climb airspeed and level at the assigned altitude. 4. Establish a descent, then restore level flight. 5. State what pitch and power changed.
steps.repetitions: One instructor sequence, then two student climb–level–descent sequences; use smaller changes if the learner is overloaded.
steps.success: Recognizes the changing sight picture, coordinates pitch and power and levels with timely coaching; initial-flight assistance is expected.
errors: Chasing the vertical-speed indication → return eyes to the horizon and make one small pitch correction.
Ball displaced during a power change → add the appropriate rudder while keeping wings level.
steps.stop: Restore ordinary cruise if traffic, turbulence or workload prevents an outside scan; instructor takes control before an unsafe altitude or airspeed develops.
steps.reference: AFH: basic flight maneuvers; PHAK: flight controls and instruments

steps.title: Airspeed changes and trim
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show cruise-to-low-cruise airspeed by setting power, holding altitude with pitch and trimming only after the attitude is established. Reverse the sequence to cruise and demonstrate how trim relieves force without setting the flight path.
steps.student: 1. Choose the assigned airspeed and configuration within the POH limits. 2. Change power while holding altitude. 3. Stabilize the attitude, then trim. 4. Return to cruise. 5. Explain which control establishes attitude and which relieves pressure.
steps.repetitions: Two complete speed transitions, with one hands-light trim check after stabilization.
steps.success: Controls altitude through a speed change, avoids chasing trim and verifies the airplane stays stable when control pressure is relaxed.
errors: Using trim as the primary pitch control → establish attitude with the elevator before trimming.
Adding power without compensating pitch → anticipate the attitude change and recheck altitude.
steps.stop: Leave the exercise before stall warning, a configuration limit or an unsafe altitude trend; use the recovery already taught rather than continuing a speed target.
steps.reference: AFH: straight-and-level flight, transitions and trim

steps.title: Coordinated turns to headings
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show clearing, an outside bank reference and coordinated rudder. Compare a shallow turn with a medium-bank turn, then show leading the rollout to capture a heading without skidding.
steps.student: 1. Clear toward the turn. 2. Enter the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture. 4. Anticipate rollout to the chosen heading. 5. Re-trim only when stable and reverse direction after another clearing scan.
steps.repetitions: Two turns in each direction, using different heading changes and one deliberate rollout correction.
steps.success: Maintains a coordinated turn, identifies altitude drift and rolls out smoothly with decreasing instructor assistance.
errors: Staring at the heading instrument → use it briefly and return to the outside reference.
Using rudder alone to hurry the rollout → reduce bank with coordinated aileron and rudder.
steps.stop: Roll wings level and discontinue if the turn is uncoordinated, traffic appears or the learner loses the altitude/airspeed picture.
steps.reference: AFH: turns; PHAK: adverse yaw and coordination

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Demonstrate the pattern, aiming picture, flare and directional control, then allow only the participation the learner can safely manage. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
Student performs preparation/start/taxi checks and elementary control with appropriate instructor help; independent landing proficiency is not expected.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.
Name the next corrected exercise and verify every unfinished source requirement before moving on.
