steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Use the currently effective Sport airplane PTS task, which specifies the near-stall condition at which another increase in angle of attack/load or reduction in power would produce an immediate stall. Clear, choose a safe recovery floor that permits completion at or above the PTS minimum of 1,500 feet AGL, and follow all aircraft limitations. Demonstrate coordinated straight flight, gentle turns, climb and descent with the requested approved configurations, then recover to cruise. This Sport task differs from the private-certificate slow-flight condition.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Recognize and recover at the first stall indication
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Demonstrate one approach-type and one departure-type entry in the approved aircraft configuration. steps.student: 1. Clear, set the configuration and verify the recovery floor. 2. Enter the instructor-briefed approach scenario. 3. Call the first stall cue and begin recovery immediately. 4. Re-establish stable flight. 5. Repeat for a departure scenario, staying coordinated throughout.
steps.repetitions: One instructor example of each entry; one student recovery of each if readiness and altitude allow.
steps.success: Names the warning cues and reduces angle of attack without delay; assisted recovery is acceptable on the introduction lesson.
errors: Trying to climb out by pulling → reduce angle of attack first, then apply approved power.
Applying aileron aggressively with yaw present → restore coordination and follow the POH stall recovery.
steps.stop: Instructor intervenes before an uncoordinated stall or spin tendency; recover by the agreed altitude. This lesson does not authorize intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: stall recognition and prevention; POH: stall recovery

Preview the ordered exercises: Airspeed changes and trim; Constant-airspeed and constant-rate altitude changes; Coordinated turns to headings; Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit; Recognize and recover at the first stall indication.

Explain angle of attack, stall warning/full-stall cues, yaw and spin prevention. This Sport PTS slow-flight condition is near an immediate stall, unlike Private ACS slow flight. Choose enough altitude to finish slow-flight/stall tasks above the applicable current PTS minimum and any higher aircraft/terrain safety floor.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Have the student lead the start/taxi checks; coach only a diagnosed error after stopping safely. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Have the student brief and fly the departure, diagnosing any drift/airspeed issue after a safe climb. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Airspeed changes and trim
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show cruise-to-low-cruise airspeed by setting power, holding altitude with pitch and trimming only after the attitude is established. Reverse the sequence to cruise and demonstrate how trim relieves force without setting the flight path.
steps.student: 1. Choose the assigned airspeed and configuration within the POH limits. 2. Change power while holding altitude. 3. Stabilize the attitude, then trim. 4. Return to cruise. 5. Explain which control establishes attitude and which relieves pressure.
steps.repetitions: Two complete speed transitions, with one hands-light trim check after stabilization.
steps.success: Controls altitude through a speed change, avoids chasing trim and verifies the airplane stays stable when control pressure is relaxed.
errors: Using trim as the primary pitch control → establish attitude with the elevator before trimming.
Adding power without compensating pitch → anticipate the attitude change and recheck altitude.
steps.stop: Leave the exercise before stall warning, a configuration limit or an unsafe altitude trend; use the recovery already taught rather than continuing a speed target.
steps.reference: AFH: straight-and-level flight, transitions and trim

steps.title: Constant-airspeed climbs, descents and altitude captures
steps.instructor: Demonstrate aircraft-appropriate pitch/power for a constant-airspeed climb and descent, with an anticipated level-off. Explain the difference between establishing airspeed and chasing vertical rate. Keep this lesson on airspeed control; selected-rate climbs/descents are introduced in Lesson 11.
steps.student: 1. Brief the altitude and POH/assigned airspeed. 2. Establish the constant-airspeed climb with coordinated controls. 3. Lead the level-off and set cruise/trim. 4. Repeat in a constant-airspeed descent. 5. Explain the pitch/power correction used when speed drifted.
steps.repetitions: Two climb–level–descent sequences at constant airspeed, with a safe reset and one diagnosed correction.
steps.success: Selects the proper pitch/power combination, anticipates level-off and corrects a trend before it becomes a large deviation.
errors: Fixating on rate while airspeed decays → restore a safe pitch/airspeed and reduce the rate target.
Leveling late → announce the approaching altitude and begin the transition earlier.
steps.stop: Level off or restore cruise if assigned airspace, terrain clearance or an airspeed/configuration limit would be approached.
steps.reference: AFH: climbs and descents; PHAK: instruments

steps.title: Coordinated turns to headings
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show clearing, an outside bank reference and coordinated rudder. Compare a shallow turn with a medium-bank turn, then show leading the rollout to capture a heading without skidding.
steps.student: 1. Clear toward the turn. 2. Enter the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture. 4. Anticipate rollout to the chosen heading. 5. Re-trim only when stable and reverse direction after another clearing scan.
steps.repetitions: Two turns in each direction, using different heading changes and one deliberate rollout correction.
steps.success: Maintains a coordinated turn, identifies altitude drift and rolls out smoothly with decreasing instructor assistance.
errors: Staring at the heading instrument → use it briefly and return to the outside reference.
Using rudder alone to hurry the rollout → reduce bank with coordinated aileron and rudder.
steps.stop: Roll wings level and discontinue if the turn is uncoordinated, traffic appears or the learner loses the altitude/airspeed picture.
steps.reference: AFH: turns; PHAK: adverse yaw and coordination

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use the currently effective Sport airplane PTS task, which specifies the near-stall condition at which another increase in angle of attack/load or reduction in power would produce an immediate stall. Clear, choose a safe recovery floor that permits completion at or above the PTS minimum of 1,500 feet AGL, and follow all aircraft limitations. Demonstrate coordinated straight flight, gentle turns, climb and descent with the requested approved configurations, then recover to cruise. This Sport task differs from the private-certificate slow-flight condition.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Recognize and recover at the first stall indication
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Demonstrate one approach-type and one departure-type entry in the approved aircraft configuration. Name the cues as they appear. Recover at the first stall indication by reducing angle of attack and using the POH recovery sequence; do not continue to a full stall in this exercise.
steps.student: 1. Clear, set the configuration and verify the recovery floor. 2. Enter the instructor-briefed approach scenario. 3. Call the first stall cue and begin recovery immediately. 4. Re-establish stable flight. 5. Repeat for a departure scenario, staying coordinated throughout.
steps.repetitions: One instructor example of each entry; one student recovery of each if readiness and altitude allow.
steps.success: Names the warning cues and reduces angle of attack without delay; assisted recovery is acceptable on the introduction lesson.
errors: Trying to climb out by pulling → reduce angle of attack first, then apply approved power.
Applying aileron aggressively with yaw present → restore coordination and follow the POH stall recovery.
steps.stop: Instructor intervenes before an uncoordinated stall or spin tendency; recover by the agreed altitude. This lesson does not authorize intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: stall recognition and prevention; POH: stall recovery

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

carryForward: Recognize and recover at the first stall indication: no adequate dedicated block is assigned in this target flight. Add/extend a safe training or assessment block before declaring the source lesson complete.
An unobserved, unsafe or below-standard source requirement must be completed in continued training/assessment before progress; the target duration grants no completion credit.
completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: From a safe altitude, show an approach-type full stall with coordinated controls. Identify the first warning and the full-stall indication, then reduce angle of attack, add approved power and clean up in the POH sequence. Contrast the entry with and without flaps.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One entry with flaps and one without on introduction; on review add one briefed turning entry only after straight entries are safe.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Demonstrate the approved departure configuration and controlled pitch-up at the briefed power. Show the rudder required as speed decreases. At the full stall, reduce angle of attack, maintain coordination and restore a safe climb according to the POH.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry. The source introduction is without flaps; use that approved configuration rather than adding a flap configuration the lesson has not assigned.
steps.repetitions: One straight entry, then the other approved configuration or a shallow turning entry on a review lesson; never rush the reset.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

Demonstrate the rollout and a complete reset before changing direction.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose altitude, airspeed and rollout reference. 2. Establish the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture and cross-check altitude. 4. Complete the turn, roll out and stabilize. 5. Repeat in the other direction after clearing.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration followed by one student turn each way on introduction; two student turns each way on review if safe and unrushed.
steps.success: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current Sport PTS tolerances.
errors: Trying to correct altitude with bank alone → restore the briefed bank and make a small pitch/power correction.
Looking only inside → return to the outside pitch reference and make short instrument cross-checks.
steps.stop: Roll out if bank, load, airspeed or altitude approaches an aircraft limit or safe practice boundary; never chase a tolerance through unsafe control inputs.

prerequisites: Complete the prerequisite ground preparation and resolve unsafe/deficient items from the preceding flight.
Have the instructor verify actual aircraft eligibility, operational limits and current Sport privileges/endorsements for the proposed mission.
briefing: Check the actual aircraft eligibility, limitations and installed supplements with current Sport privileges/endorsements. Select POH speeds/configurations, weather/crosswind limits, runway margins, fuel, practice area and safe recovery boundaries before movement.

Agree on positive control transfer, instructor lookout and authorized simulations. Keep aircraft control, traffic and terrain ahead of discussion; no intentional spins, surprise shutdowns or hazardous low-altitude failures.

Preview the ordered exercises: Constant-airspeed and constant-rate altitude changes; Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit; Steep turns in both directions; Full power-off stalls: approach scenario; Full power-on stalls: departure scenario.

Explain angle of attack, stall warning/full-stall cues, yaw and spin prevention. This Sport PTS slow-flight condition is near an immediate stall, unlike Private ACS slow flight. Choose enough altitude to finish slow-flight/stall tasks above the applicable current PTS minimum and any higher aircraft/terrain safety floor.
preflightGuide: Review aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading, fuel and current Sport aircraft/operation eligibility. Instructor verifies suitability and authorization.
Use the actual POH/AFM walkaround, fuel/oil and defect assessment. Set seats/restraints/controls, secure loose items and prepare charts/radios.
Give the aircraft-specific passenger/positive-control-transfer briefing; on solo review the specific mission and ground contact plan before release.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Have the student lead the start/taxi checks; coach only a diagnosed error after stopping safely. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Have the student brief and fly the departure, diagnosing any drift/airspeed issue after a safe climb. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Selected-rate climbs and descents
steps.instructor: Introduce a selected vertical-rate climb/descent using aircraft-appropriate pitch/power while protecting airspeed. Demonstrate how to avoid chasing a lagging rate indication and how to anticipate level-off. Return control for both directions and require a small, stable correction.
steps.student: 1. Brief the rate, altitude and safe airspeed range. 2. Establish the selected-rate climb. 3. Cross-check airspeed/attitude with rate and altitude. 4. Lead the level-off. 5. Repeat in descent and explain when a rate target must be abandoned for airspeed/safety.
steps.repetitions: One instructor example, then one student selected-rate climb and one descent with level-offs.
steps.success: Selects the proper pitch/power combination, anticipates level-off and corrects a trend before it becomes a large deviation.
errors: Fixating on rate while airspeed decays → restore a safe pitch/airspeed and reduce the rate target.
Leveling late → announce the approaching altitude and begin the transition earlier.
steps.stop: Level off or restore cruise if assigned airspace, terrain clearance or an airspeed/configuration limit would be approached.
steps.reference: AFH: climbs and descents; PHAK: instruments

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use the currently effective Sport airplane PTS task, which specifies the near-stall condition at which another increase in angle of attack/load or reduction in power would produce an immediate stall. Clear, choose a safe recovery floor that permits completion at or above the PTS minimum of 1,500 feet AGL, and follow all aircraft limitations. Demonstrate coordinated straight flight, gentle turns, climb and descent with the requested approved configurations, then recover to cruise. This Sport task differs from the private-certificate slow-flight condition.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Steep turns in both directions
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Show clearing, the current Sport PTS bank target, the added back pressure/power as needed and an outside reference that reveals altitude drift. Demonstrate the rollout and a complete reset before changing direction.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose altitude, airspeed and rollout reference. 2. Establish the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture and cross-check altitude. 4. Complete the turn, roll out and stabilize. 5. Repeat in the other direction after clearing.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration followed by one student turn each way on introduction; two student turns each way on review if safe and unrushed.
steps.success: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current Sport PTS tolerances.
errors: Trying to correct altitude with bank alone → restore the briefed bank and make a small pitch/power correction.
Looking only inside → return to the outside pitch reference and make short instrument cross-checks.
steps.stop: Roll out if bank, load, airspeed or altitude approaches an aircraft limit or safe practice boundary; never chase a tolerance through unsafe control inputs.
steps.reference: AFH: steep turns; Sport PTS: Steep Turns

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: From a safe altitude, show an approach-type full stall with coordinated controls. Identify the first warning and the full-stall indication, then reduce angle of attack, add approved power and clean up in the POH sequence. Contrast the entry with and without flaps.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One entry with flaps and one without on introduction; on review add one briefed turning entry only after straight entries are safe.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Demonstrate the approved departure configuration and controlled pitch-up at the briefed power. Show the rudder required as speed decreases. At the full stall, reduce angle of attack, maintain coordination and restore a safe climb according to the POH.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One straight entry, then the other approved configuration or a shallow turning entry on a review lesson; never rush the reset.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.

steps.title: Read the wind before ground-reference maneuvers
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Use a road or field boundary to compare heading with actual ground track. Show how groundspeed changes around a point and why the bank changes through a maneuver. Select a legal, clear practice area with escape options.
steps.student: 1. Identify wind direction from available evidence. 2. Compare heading and ground track on two headings. 3. Explain where groundspeed and required bank will be greatest. 4. Select the reference, practice altitude and emergency options before maneuvering.
steps.repetitions: Two short wind comparisons, then a verbal prediction before the first ground-reference entry.
steps.success: Predicts drift and varying groundspeed and chooses a reference that permits safe, legal maneuvering.
errors: Assuming heading equals track → compare the airplane with a fixed ground feature.
Selecting a feature near people or obstacles → choose another area before descending.
steps.stop: Do not enter if terrain, obstructions, populated areas, airspace or traffic cannot support safe practice at the chosen altitude.
steps.reference: AFH: ground-reference maneuvers; PHAK: wind correction

steps.title: Rectangular course: wind correction by leg
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Demonstrate downwind entry, planned lateral spacing and changing bank through each corner. Point out crab on crosswind legs and the difference between heading and track; keep the selected altitude and an outside scan.
steps.student: 1. Clear and establish the briefed entry. 2. Hold parallel ground tracks with wind correction. 3. Change bank smoothly through each corner to preserve spacing. 4. Call the wind correction on each leg. 5. Exit without descending or tightening toward obstacles.
steps.repetitions: One instructor circuit and one student circuit on introduction; two student circuits on review if time allows.
steps.success: Maintains safe altitude and reasonably uniform spacing, predicts drift and changes bank smoothly rather than skidding the turn.
errors: Turning too late on the fast downwind corner → anticipate the corner and use an appropriate coordinated bank.
Looking continuously at the field → alternate the reference with traffic, horizon and altitude scans.
steps.stop: Exit toward a safe area for traffic, inadequate obstacle clearance, excessive bank or an unstable altitude trend.
steps.reference: AFH: rectangular course; Sport PTS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: S-turns across a road
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show a suitable reference line, an entry perpendicular to it and changing bank with groundspeed. Demonstrate a wings-level crossing before reversing the turn; explain why equal-looking ground arcs need unequal banks.
steps.student: 1. Clear and approach the reference as briefed. 2. Begin a coordinated turn that compensates for the wind. 3. Cross wings level and reverse the turn. 4. Adjust bank to create the second comparable arc. 5. Exit and describe the strongest drift correction.
steps.repetitions: One paired S-turn demonstration and one student pair on introduction; two student pairs on review.
steps.success: Crosses the reference with wings approximately level, varies bank with wind and preserves altitude and coordination.
errors: Holding one bank all the way around → anticipate changing groundspeed and vary bank.
Rushing the reversal with rudder → level the wings at the reference, then enter the opposite bank together.
steps.stop: Exit if bank/altitude trend is unsafe or the chosen road has traffic/obstructions that compromise the practice area; maintain legal clearances.
steps.reference: AFH: S-turns; Sport PTS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: Turns around a point
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Select a visible point with clear surrounding airspace. Demonstrate entry and variable bank to hold a constant radius as groundspeed changes. Explain the steepest-bank sector and the need to retain an escape route.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose a safe radius and altitude. 2. Enter as briefed. 3. Adjust bank to maintain the ground radius. 4. Keep the ball centered and scan outside. 5. Exit after a full circuit and predict corrections for a second direction.
steps.repetitions: One instructor circuit and one student circuit on introduction; one student circuit each way on review.
steps.success: Holds a consistent radius using coordinated bank changes, with safe altitude and a sustained traffic scan.
errors: Tightening toward the point when blown inward → reduce bank and re-establish the planned radius.
Fixating on the point → scan the horizon and traffic, then check the ground reference briefly.
steps.stop: Leave the maneuver if the required bank exceeds the practice limit, an escape route is compromised or traffic/terrain clearance becomes uncertain.
steps.reference: AFH: turns around a point; Sport PTS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

lessons.applicability: Single-engine-land airplane Sport pathway, using the current 2026 course portal’s October 2025 syllabus and currently effective FAA-S-8081-29B PTS. Check aircraft eligibility under current §61.316 and all privileges/limitations/endorsements in Part 61; the source’s older LSA shorthand does not establish current eligibility. lessons.title: Wind-track and maneuver consolidation
lessons.summary: Review rectangle/S-turn ground tracks, both full-stall types, slow flight and steep turns. Revisit turns around a point if the source completion requirement has not already been demonstrated.
objectives: Review rectangle/S-turn ground tracks, both full-stall types, slow flight and steep turns. Revisit turns around a point if the source completion requirement has not already been demonstrated.
Use safe setup/control, recognize the earliest error cue and show a corrected repeat or independent assessment evidence appropriate to the lesson.
prerequisites: Complete the prerequisite ground preparation and resolve unsafe/deficient items from the preceding flight.
Have the instructor verify actual aircraft eligibility, operational limits and current Sport privileges/endorsements for the proposed mission.
briefing: Check the actual aircraft eligibility, limitations and installed supplements with current Sport privileges/endorsements. Select POH speeds/configurations, weather/crosswind limits, runway margins, fuel, practice area and safe recovery boundaries before movement.

Agree on positive control transfer, instructor lookout and authorized simulations. Keep aircraft control, traffic and terrain ahead of discussion; no intentional spins, surprise shutdowns or hazardous low-altitude failures.

Preview the ordered exercises: Rectangular course: wind correction by leg; S-turns across a road; Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit; Full power-off stalls: approach scenario; Full power-on stalls: departure scenario.

Explain angle of attack, stall warning/full-stall cues, yaw and spin prevention. This Sport PTS slow-flight condition is near an immediate stall, unlike Private ACS slow flight. Choose enough altitude to finish slow-flight/stall tasks above the applicable current PTS minimum and any higher aircraft/terrain safety floor.
preflightGuide: Review aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading, fuel and current Sport aircraft/operation eligibility. Instructor verifies suitability and authorization.
Use the actual POH/AFM walkaround, fuel/oil and defect assessment. Set seats/restraints/controls, secure loose items and prepare charts/radios.
Give the aircraft-specific passenger/positive-control-transfer briefing; on solo review the specific mission and ground contact plan before release.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Have the student lead the start/taxi checks; coach only a diagnosed error after stopping safely. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Have the student brief and fly the departure, diagnosing any drift/airspeed issue after a safe climb. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Rectangular course: wind correction by leg
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Demonstrate downwind entry, planned lateral spacing and changing bank through each corner. Point out crab on crosswind legs and the difference between heading and track; keep the selected altitude and an outside scan.
steps.student: 1. Clear and establish the briefed entry. 2. Hold parallel ground tracks with wind correction. 3. Change bank smoothly through each corner to preserve spacing. 4. Call the wind correction on each leg. 5. Exit without descending or tightening toward obstacles.
steps.repetitions: One instructor circuit and one student circuit on introduction; two student circuits on review if time allows.
steps.success: Maintains safe altitude and reasonably uniform spacing, predicts drift and changes bank smoothly rather than skidding the turn.
errors: Turning too late on the fast downwind corner → anticipate the corner and use an appropriate coordinated bank.
Looking continuously at the field → alternate the reference with traffic, horizon and altitude scans.
steps.stop: Exit toward a safe area for traffic, inadequate obstacle clearance, excessive bank or an unstable altitude trend.
steps.reference: AFH: rectangular course; Sport PTS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: S-turns across a road
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Show a suitable reference line, an entry perpendicular to it and changing bank with groundspeed. Demonstrate a wings-level crossing before reversing the turn; explain why equal-looking ground arcs need unequal banks.
steps.student: 1. Clear and approach the reference as briefed. 2. Begin a coordinated turn that compensates for the wind. 3. Cross wings level and reverse the turn. 4. Adjust bank to create the second comparable arc. 5. Exit and describe the strongest drift correction.
steps.repetitions: One paired S-turn demonstration and one student pair on introduction; two student pairs on review.
steps.success: Crosses the reference with wings approximately level, varies bank with wind and preserves altitude and coordination.
errors: Holding one bank all the way around → anticipate changing groundspeed and vary bank.
Rushing the reversal with rudder → level the wings at the reference, then enter the opposite bank together.
steps.stop: Exit if bank/altitude trend is unsafe or the chosen road has traffic/obstructions that compromise the practice area; maintain legal clearances.
steps.reference: AFH: S-turns; Sport PTS: Ground Reference Maneuvers

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use the currently effective Sport airplane PTS task, which specifies the near-stall condition at which another increase in angle of attack/load or reduction in power would produce an immediate stall. Clear, choose a safe recovery floor that permits completion at or above the PTS minimum of 1,500 feet AGL, and follow all aircraft limitations. Demonstrate coordinated straight flight, gentle turns, climb and descent with the requested approved configurations, then recover to cruise. This Sport task differs from the private-certificate slow-flight condition.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: From a safe altitude, show an approach-type full stall with coordinated controls. Identify the first warning and the full-stall indication, then reduce angle of attack, add approved power and clean up in the POH sequence. Contrast the entry with and without flaps.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One entry with flaps and one without on introduction; on review add one briefed turning entry only after straight entries are safe.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Demonstrate the approved departure configuration and controlled pitch-up at the briefed power. Show the rudder required as speed decreases. At the full stall, reduce angle of attack, maintain coordination and restore a safe climb according to the POH.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One straight entry, then the other approved configuration or a shallow turning entry on a review lesson; never rush the reset.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

carryForward: Steep turns in both directions: no adequate dedicated block is assigned in this target flight. Add/extend a safe training or assessment block before declaring the source lesson complete.
Turns around a point: no adequate dedicated block is assigned in this target flight. Add/extend a safe training or assessment block before declaring the source lesson complete.

The source completion text also expects turns around a point, although that task is absent from this lesson’s content checklist. Confirm prior evidence or schedule a dedicated turn-around-point review before completion.
completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.
Name the next corrected exercise and verify every unfinished source requirement before moving on.

steps.title: Rejected-takeoff decision and controlled simulation
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Before moving, brief rejection triggers, runway remaining and the aircraft stopping procedure. Demonstrate a reject only in an instructor-selected, prebriefed low-risk condition with adequate runway; otherwise use a stopped/verbal scenario and schedule the flight task later.
steps.student: 1. State what would require rejection before the roll. 2. Keep directional control during the authorized simulation. 3. Reduce power and stop using the POH procedure. 4. Communicate and clear the runway when safe. 5. Explain why continuing would be unsafe.
steps.repetitions: One coached decision rehearsal and, only when suitable, one prebriefed controlled reject. No unannounced high-speed abort.
steps.success: Recognizes a rejection trigger promptly and preserves runway alignment while stopping with adequate margin.
errors: Continuing because the instructor has not spoken → act on the briefed rejection trigger.
Braking aggressively while drifting → maintain directional control and apply the approved stopping procedure.
steps.stop: Do not simulate if runway, traffic, contamination or aircraft condition reduces stopping margin. A verbal rehearsal does not count as a completed flight task.
steps.reference: AFH: takeoffs and emergency procedures; aircraft POH

steps.title: Recognize an equipment failure and choose a safe action
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Use a verbal or approved simulated indication, such as an electrical or instrument fault. Show how to preserve aircraft control, confirm the indication, use the correct checklist and decide whether to land or divert. Do not disable essential equipment.
steps.student: 1. Identify the abnormal indication. 2. Keep flying and state the immediate risk. 3. Apply only approved memory actions when applicable, then use the checklist. 4. Reassess systems, weather and landing options. 5. Tell the instructor/ATC what help is needed.
steps.repetitions: Two contrasting verbal scenarios, one with a land-soon decision and one requiring checklist diagnosis.
steps.success: Prioritizes aircraft control, chooses the correct checklist and reaches a defensible landing/diversion decision without random switch changes.
errors: Treating the indication before controlling the airplane → restore control, then diagnose.
Resetting a breaker or moving a control without authority → consult the aircraft checklist and identify the consequence first.
steps.stop: End the simulation immediately for a real abnormality, distraction from traffic/terrain or any effect on essential equipment.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency procedures; POH: systems and abnormal checklists

steps.title: Simulated engine failure and emergency approach
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Brief how the simulation will start, the minimum recovery condition and who controls power. Demonstrate airspeed, landing-site choice and a plan to the site. Use checklist/communications only after control and the landing plan are established.
steps.student: 1. Establish the POH glide condition. 2. Select a reachable suitable site and plan the approach. 3. Perform approved checklist actions or verbalize unsafe-to-simulate actions. 4. Brief occupants and communications. 5. Evaluate whether the site remains reachable, then recover at the briefed gate.
steps.repetitions: One instructor example on introduction and one student scenario; repeat with a different site only with sufficient altitude and time.
steps.success: Maintains glide control, selects a reachable site early and manages checklist/communications without losing the landing plan.
errors: Searching indefinitely for the perfect field → select a suitable reachable option and refine it.
Trying to stretch the glide → maintain the POH glide condition and revise the landing plan.
steps.stop: Recover with power at the prebriefed safe altitude/position or earlier for traffic, terrain, a poor glide plan or aircraft concerns. No surprise engine shutdown or off-airport touchdown.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency approach; Sport PTS: Emergency Approach and Landing; POH

steps.title: Go-around from a rejected landing
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Brief the unstable-approach gate and demonstrate an early decision to go around. Show approved power, pitch, configuration changes and runway/traffic tracking. Explain why cleaning up before a safe climb can increase sink.
steps.student: 1. Identify the assigned unstable-approach cue. 2. Announce and initiate the go-around promptly. 3. Apply approved power and establish the climb attitude. 4. Change configuration in the POH sequence. 5. Maintain runway/traffic separation and communicate when workload allows.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration on introduction and one student go-around; on review one planned and one student-initiated decision when safe.
steps.success: Makes the decision early, controls yaw/pitch and transitions to a safe climb without premature configuration changes.
errors: Waiting to see whether the landing improves → use the briefed gate and commit to a go-around.
Retracting flaps while still descending → establish the approved climb and configuration sequence.
steps.stop: Instructor intervenes for a stall tendency, conflict or runway misalignment; do not manufacture an unsafe approach to create a go-around.
steps.reference: AFH: approaches and go-arounds; Sport PTS: Go-Around/Rejected Landing

lessons.title: Crosswind control, slips and no-flap landing
lessons.summary: Compare crab and sideslip methods, distinguish sideslip from forward slip and practice an approved no-flap approach. Weather and aircraft restrictions decide which methods are demonstrated.
objectives: Compare crab and sideslip methods, distinguish sideslip from forward slip and practice an approved no-flap approach. Weather and aircraft restrictions decide which methods are demonstrated.
Use safe setup/control, recognize the earliest error cue and show a corrected repeat or independent assessment evidence appropriate to the lesson.
prerequisites: Complete the prerequisite ground preparation and resolve unsafe/deficient items from the preceding flight.
Have the instructor verify actual aircraft eligibility, operational limits and current Sport privileges/endorsements for the proposed mission.
briefing: Check the actual aircraft eligibility, limitations and installed supplements with current Sport privileges/endorsements. Select POH speeds/configurations, weather/crosswind limits, runway margins, fuel, practice area and safe recovery boundaries before movement.

Preview the ordered exercises: Crosswind takeoff, crab and sideslip landing; Sideslip and forward slip: distinct purposes; Forward slip to a stabilized landing; Landing without flaps.
