steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Have the student lead the start/taxi checks; coach only a diagnosed error after stopping safely. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Have the student brief and fly the departure, diagnosing any drift/airspeed issue after a safe climb. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Crosswind takeoff, crab and sideslip landing
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show the wind correction on taxi, takeoff roll and climb. In the pattern compare a crab on approach with a sideslip that aligns the longitudinal axis at touchdown. Explain which method/transition the aircraft permits and the crosswind limits selected for this lesson.
steps.student: 1. Identify wind and select the briefed technique. 2. Hold runway alignment during takeoff with coordinated controls. 3. Correct drift in the climb. 4. Fly a stabilized approach. 5. Remove drift and align the airplane using the approved method; go around if control margin is inadequate.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated circuit and one student circuit on introduction; add a second student landing only within weather and time limits.
steps.success: Maintains centerline, manages drift and lands aligned without side loading; new crosswind technique may require assistance.
errors: Holding a fixed correction as airspeed changes → adjust control continuously for the changing effectiveness.
Touching down while drifting or crabbed beyond aircraft guidance → go around and reset the approach.
steps.stop: Go around for excessive drift, misalignment, gusts or inadequate control margin. Use aircraft, instructor and endorsement limits; a published demonstrated crosswind is not automatically a legal operating limit.
steps.reference: AFH: crosswind takeoffs and landings; POH

steps.title: Sideslip and forward slip: distinct purposes
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: At a safe altitude, demonstrate a sideslip to correct drift while tracking a line, then a forward slip to increase descent with a chosen track. Show approved configuration and indications; compare control inputs and how to return smoothly to coordinated flight.
steps.student: 1. Verify the aircraft permits the selected slip/configuration. 2. Establish a briefed sideslip and state its drift-control purpose. 3. Return to coordinated flight. 4. Establish a forward slip while holding the planned ground track. 5. Recover before the briefed altitude and explain the difference.
steps.repetitions: One instructor example and one student entry of each slip; later approach application requires a separate stabilized-landing exercise.
steps.success: Distinguishes drift correction from descent control, stays within aircraft limits and recovers without abrupt yaw or pitch changes.
errors: Skidding instead of slipping → reduce the control input and have the instructor restore the correct combination.
Trusting an affected airspeed indication without context → use the POH cautions and the briefed pitch/configuration.
steps.stop: Discontinue for an aircraft restriction, unapproved flap configuration, unstable speed/track or inadequate recovery height. No slip outside POH guidance.
steps.reference: AFH: slips; POH: operating limitations and approved procedures

steps.title: Forward slip to a stabilized landing
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show when a forward slip can correct excess height on an otherwise safe approach. Establish the approved slip/configuration, preserve the planned track and remove the slip early enough to judge a stabilized touchdown.
steps.student: 1. Identify excess height and confirm the slip is appropriate. 2. Apply the approved forward-slip technique. 3. Hold the landing track and monitor the POH airspeed cautions. 4. Recover to the required landing alignment. 5. Land only if the final approach is stable; otherwise go around.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated approach on introduction and one student approach; do not repeatedly salvage an unstable approach.
steps.success: Uses the slip deliberately, exits smoothly and chooses a go-around if a normal safe touchdown is no longer assured.
errors: Slipping merely to rescue a rushed approach → go around and rebuild the pattern.
Recovering the slip too late → use the prebriefed stabilization gate and restore alignment earlier.
steps.stop: Go around for unapproved configuration, excessive sink/drift, uncertainty about airspeed or failure to stabilize before the aircraft/instructor gate.
steps.reference: AFH: forward slip to landing; Sport PTS: Forward Slip to a Landing; POH

steps.title: Landing without flaps
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Brief the aircraft-approved no-flap approach speed, runway performance and altered sight picture. Demonstrate planning the pattern for the lower drag and avoiding a late, steep correction.
steps.student: 1. Confirm no-flap performance and runway margin from the POH. 2. Set the approved approach configuration and speed. 3. Judge the higher energy and adjusted descent path. 4. Stabilize and align the aircraft. 5. Land or go around before excess speed/height threatens runway margin.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration on introduction and one student no-flap landing when runway and traffic permit.
steps.success: Plans the approach early, controls energy and touches down with adequate runway remaining without forcing the airplane onto the runway.
errors: Using the usual flap-landing picture and arriving fast → adjust pattern and energy earlier.
Diving to the aiming point → go around and plan a stable descent.
steps.stop: Go around if approach energy, alignment or remaining runway becomes uncertain; do not simulate a flap failure by creating an actual system fault.
steps.reference: AFH: no-flap approach; POH: configuration and landing performance

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

carryForward: Rejected-takeoff decision and controlled simulation: no adequate dedicated block is assigned in this target flight. Add/extend a safe training or assessment block before declaring the source lesson complete.
Go-around from a rejected landing: no adequate dedicated block is assigned in this target flight. Add/extend a safe training or assessment block before declaring the source lesson complete.
completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
Student explains the new exercise and performs its sequence with the assistance appropriate to introduction, followed by a corrected repeat when safe.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.
Name the next corrected exercise and verify every unfinished source requirement before moving on.

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use the currently effective Sport airplane PTS task, which specifies the near-stall condition at which another increase in angle of attack/load or reduction in power would produce an immediate stall. Clear, choose a safe recovery floor that permits completion at or above the PTS minimum of 1,500 feet AGL, and follow all aircraft limitations. Demonstrate coordinated straight flight, gentle turns, climb and descent with the requested approved configurations, then recover to cruise. This Sport task differs from the private-certificate slow-flight condition.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: From a safe altitude, show an approach-type full stall with coordinated controls. Identify the first warning and the full-stall indication, then reduce angle of attack, add approved power and clean up in the POH sequence. Contrast the entry with and without flaps.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One entry with flaps and one without on introduction; on review add one briefed turning entry only after straight entries are safe.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Demonstrate the approved departure configuration and controlled pitch-up at the briefed power. Show the rudder required as speed decreases. At the full stall, reduce angle of attack, maintain coordination and restore a safe climb according to the POH.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One straight entry, then the other approved configuration or a shallow turning entry on a review lesson; never rush the reset.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

Use safe setup/control, recognize the earliest error cue and show a corrected repeat or independent assessment evidence appropriate to the lesson.

Have the instructor verify actual aircraft eligibility, operational limits and current Sport privileges/endorsements for the proposed mission.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Observe student-led surface operations without prompting; safety intervention means further training is needed. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Observe an independent departure and traffic scan; give only task/route instructions. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Crosswind takeoff, crab and sideslip landing
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains centerline, manages drift and lands aligned without side loading; new crosswind technique may require assistance. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Identify wind and select the briefed technique. 2. Hold runway alignment during takeoff with coordinated controls. 3. Correct drift in the climb. 4. Fly a stabilized approach. 5. Remove drift and align the airplane using the approved method; go around if control margin is inadequate.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains centerline, manages drift and lands aligned without side loading; new crosswind technique may require assistance.
errors: Holding a fixed correction as airspeed changes → adjust control continuously for the changing effectiveness.
Touching down while drifting or crabbed beyond aircraft guidance → go around and reset the approach.
steps.stop: Go around for excessive drift, misalignment, gusts or inadequate control margin. Use aircraft, instructor and endorsement limits; a published demonstrated crosswind is not automatically a legal operating limit.
steps.reference: AFH: crosswind takeoffs and landings; POH

steps.title: Forward slip to a stabilized landing
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Uses the slip deliberately, exits smoothly and chooses a go-around if a normal safe touchdown is no longer assured. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Identify excess height and confirm the slip is appropriate. 2. Apply the approved forward-slip technique. 3. Hold the landing track and monitor the POH airspeed cautions. 4. Recover to the required landing alignment. 5. Land only if the final approach is stable; otherwise go around.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Uses the slip deliberately, exits smoothly and chooses a go-around if a normal safe touchdown is no longer assured.
errors: Slipping merely to rescue a rushed approach → go around and rebuild the pattern.
Recovering the slip too late → use the prebriefed stabilization gate and restore alignment earlier.
steps.stop: Go around for unapproved configuration, excessive sink/drift, uncertainty about airspeed or failure to stabilize before the aircraft/instructor gate.
steps.reference: AFH: forward slip to landing; Sport PTS: Forward Slip to a Landing; POH

steps.title: Landing without flaps
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Plans the approach early, controls energy and touches down with adequate runway remaining without forcing the airplane onto the runway. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Confirm no-flap performance and runway margin from the POH. 2. Set the approved approach configuration and speed. 3. Judge the higher energy and adjusted descent path. 4. Stabilize and align the aircraft. 5. Land or go around before excess speed/height threatens runway margin.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Plans the approach early, controls energy and touches down with adequate runway remaining without forcing the airplane onto the runway.
errors: Using the usual flap-landing picture and arriving fast → adjust pattern and energy earlier.
Diving to the aiming point → go around and plan a stable descent.
steps.stop: Go around if approach energy, alignment or remaining runway becomes uncertain; do not simulate a flap failure by creating an actual system fault.
steps.reference: AFH: no-flap approach; POH: configuration and landing performance

steps.title: Go-around from a rejected landing
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Makes the decision early, controls yaw/pitch and transitions to a safe climb without premature configuration changes. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Identify the assigned unstable-approach cue. 2. Announce and initiate the go-around promptly. 3. Apply approved power and establish the climb attitude. 4. Change configuration in the POH sequence. 5. Maintain runway/traffic separation and communicate when workload allows.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Makes the decision early, controls yaw/pitch and transitions to a safe climb without premature configuration changes.
errors: Waiting to see whether the landing improves → use the briefed gate and commit to a go-around.
Retracting flaps while still descending → establish the approved climb and configuration sequence.
steps.stop: Instructor intervenes for a stall tendency, conflict or runway misalignment; do not manufacture an unsafe approach to create a go-around.
steps.reference: AFH: approaches and go-arounds; Sport PTS: Go-Around/Rejected Landing

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Assess an independent arrival and landing; provide safety intervention if needed and record it. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.

Solo readiness requires satisfactory presolo knowledge/corrections, required logged training and consistently safe patterns, landing control and emergency decisions in the intended aircraft. Further coaching to prevent an unsafe outcome means further dual training.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.
Name the next corrected exercise and verify every unfinished source requirement before moving on.

steps.title: Sight picture, climb, level flight and descent
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Recognizes the changing sight picture, coordinates pitch and power and levels with timely coaching; initial-flight assistance is expected. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Describe the outside attitude and cross-check the instruments. 2. Hold straight flight with coordinated rudder. 3. Establish the briefed climb airspeed and level at the assigned altitude. 4. Establish a descent, then restore level flight. 5. State what pitch and power changed.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the changing sight picture, coordinates pitch and power and levels with timely coaching; initial-flight assistance is expected.
errors: Chasing the vertical-speed indication → return eyes to the horizon and make one small pitch correction.
Ball displaced during a power change → add the appropriate rudder while keeping wings level.
steps.stop: Restore ordinary cruise if traffic, turbulence or workload prevents an outside scan; instructor takes control before an unsafe altitude or airspeed develops.
steps.reference: AFH: basic flight maneuvers; PHAK: flight controls and instruments

steps.title: Coordinated turns to headings
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains a coordinated turn, identifies altitude drift and rolls out smoothly with decreasing instructor assistance. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear toward the turn. 2. Enter the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture. 4. Anticipate rollout to the chosen heading. 5. Re-trim only when stable and reverse direction after another clearing scan.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains a coordinated turn, identifies altitude drift and rolls out smoothly with decreasing instructor assistance.
errors: Staring at the heading instrument → use it briefly and return to the outside reference.
Using rudder alone to hurry the rollout → reduce bank with coordinated aileron and rudder.
steps.stop: Roll wings level and discontinue if the turn is uncoordinated, traffic appears or the learner loses the altitude/airspeed picture.
steps.reference: AFH: turns; PHAK: adverse yaw and coordination

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Recognize an equipment failure and choose a safe action
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Prioritizes aircraft control, chooses the correct checklist and reaches a defensible landing/diversion decision without random switch changes. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.
steps.student: 1. Identify the abnormal indication. 2. Keep flying and state the immediate risk. 3. Apply only approved memory actions when applicable, then use the checklist. 4. Reassess systems, weather and landing options. 5. Tell the instructor/ATC what help is needed.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Prioritizes aircraft control, chooses the correct checklist and reaches a defensible landing/diversion decision without random switch changes.
errors: Treating the indication before controlling the airplane → restore control, then diagnose.
Resetting a breaker or moving a control without authority → consult the aircraft checklist and identify the consequence first.
steps.stop: End the simulation immediately for a real abnormality, distraction from traffic/terrain or any effect on essential equipment.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency procedures; POH: systems and abnormal checklists

steps.title: Simulated engine failure and emergency approach
steps.instructor: Before flight, assign the setup and recovery/termination gate. Observe without coaching and judge this task-specific result: Maintains glide control, selects a reachable site early and manages checklist/communications without losing the landing plan. Intervene for safety, document the assistance and return the task to dual training; a later demonstration is a separate training attempt.

errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.

steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.

Have the instructor verify actual aircraft eligibility, operational limits and current Sport privileges/endorsements for the proposed mission.
Prepare an independent plan of action and identify required tasks not yet safely demonstrated.
briefing: Check the actual aircraft eligibility, limitations and installed supplements with current Sport privileges/endorsements. Select POH speeds/configurations, weather/crosswind limits, runway margins, fuel, practice area and safe recovery boundaries before movement.

Choose enough altitude to finish slow-flight/stall tasks above the applicable current PTS minimum and any higher aircraft/terrain safety floor.

State the assessment rules: no coaching during the independent attempt, safety intervention is documented, and all unobserved/deficient required tasks need continued training or assessment. Stage I determines safe solo readiness; the final check uses the current Sport PTS.

Use the parked oral to assess certificates/eligibility, maintenance/airworthiness records, actual aircraft systems/servicing, checklists, weather, performance and solo limitations. Observe preflight duties rather than accepting memorized answers.

Use the actual POH/AFM walkaround, fuel/oil and defect assessment. Set seats/restraints/controls, secure loose items and prepare charts/radios.
Give the aircraft-specific passenger/positive-control-transfer briefing; on solo review the specific mission and ground contact plan before release.
lessons.timingNote: The source provides 90 flight minutes and 90 discussion minutes. Schedule the go-around assessment in an extended/continued flight if it cannot be observed safely during the complete pattern sequence; all required tasks must be complete before solo release.

steps.instructor: Observe student-led surface operations without prompting; safety intervention means further training is needed. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.

errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit

Look for this task-specific result: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.

Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.

errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario

Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.

steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

Look for this task-specific result: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.

errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.

steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.

errors: Treating the indication before controlling the airplane → restore control, then diagnose.

steps.stop: End the simulation immediately for a real abnormality, distraction from traffic/terrain or any effect on essential equipment.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency procedures; POH: systems and abnormal checklists

Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: SOLO · Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Ground supervision: observe the authorized departure if practical and retain the agreed contact plan. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: SOLO · Supervised traffic-pattern circuits
steps.instructor: Before departure, verify prior dual demonstration and proficiency, then authorize this exact task, location, repetitions and weather limits. Review the student’s setup and stop criteria using the aircraft references. Remain available under the agreed supervision/contact plan. No in-flight instructor demonstration or new-task training is possible; missing proficiency means another dual lesson before release.
steps.student: 1. Fly only the released pattern/runway in the briefed weather. 2. Make required calls and maintain separation. 3. Use the normal approved takeoff and landing technique, with wind correction only within the endorsement limits. 4. Go around whenever unstable. 5. End the circuits early if traffic, weather, workload or fuel changes.
steps.repetitions: Perform only the prebriefed authorized repetitions within the allotted block. Skip a task rather than exceed weather, proficiency, endorsement or fuel limits.
steps.success: Maintains centerline, manages drift and lands aligned without side loading; new crosswind technique may require assistance.
errors: Holding a fixed correction as airspeed changes → adjust control continuously for the changing effectiveness.
Touching down while drifting or crabbed beyond aircraft guidance → go around and reset the approach.
steps.stop: Go around for excessive drift, misalignment, gusts or inadequate control margin. Use aircraft, instructor and endorsement limits; a published demonstrated crosswind is not automatically a legal operating limit.
steps.reference: AFH: crosswind takeoffs and landings; POH

steps.title: SOLO · Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Ground supervision: remain reachable, monitor the agreed return window and accept an early return/go-around without pressure to finish repetitions. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: SOLO · Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Ground supervision: meet/debrief after shutdown and verify the actual route, landing counts and any difficulty before another authorization. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
The instructor separately makes the parked solo release; the student then safely completes authorized supervised solo patterns. The dual portion alone does not complete Stage I.
debrief: Reconstruct actual route/circuits, full-stop counts and any weather/traffic/authorization change.
Discuss any go-around, return, diversion or request for help; rehearse the response before the next solo authorization.
Confirm aircraft securing and actual experience with the instructor, then decide the next specific authorized mission.

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use the currently effective Sport airplane PTS task, which specifies the near-stall condition at which another increase in angle of attack/load or reduction in power would produce an immediate stall. Clear, choose a safe recovery floor that permits completion at or above the PTS minimum of 1,500 feet AGL, and follow all aircraft limitations. Demonstrate coordinated straight flight, gentle turns, climb and descent with the requested approved configurations, then recover to cruise. This Sport task differs from the private-certificate slow-flight condition.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One entry, two shallow turns and one recovery; repeat the entry only after identifying the largest error.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: From a safe altitude, show an approach-type full stall with coordinated controls. Identify the first warning and the full-stall indication, then reduce angle of attack, add approved power and clean up in the POH sequence. Contrast the entry with and without flaps.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One entry with flaps and one without on introduction; on review add one briefed turning entry only after straight entries are safe.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Demonstrate the approved departure configuration and controlled pitch-up at the briefed power. Show the rudder required as speed decreases. At the full stall, reduce angle of attack, maintain coordination and restore a safe climb according to the POH.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One straight entry, then the other approved configuration or a shallow turning entry on a review lesson; never rush the reset.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure

Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

carryForward: Forward slip to a stabilized landing: no adequate dedicated block is assigned in this target flight. Add/extend a safe training or assessment block before declaring the source lesson complete.
completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.

debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.

Compare planned and actual time/fuel. Demonstrate a concise position report or Flight Service contact when useful, without letting communications replace lookout.
steps.student: 1. Orient the chart and identify two independent position clues. 2. Fly the planned heading with wind correction. 3. Mark actual checkpoint time and revise ETA/fuel. 4. Scan weather and airspace ahead. 5. Explain the next landmark and landing alternative; make the assigned radio contact at a low-workload time.
steps.repetitions: At least three checkpoint fixes and two time/fuel updates; use the source route distances rather than a generic local circuit.
steps.success: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan.
errors: Mistaking one similar feature for the checkpoint → verify with a second independent landmark.
Ignoring time/fuel after a wind change → update groundspeed, ETA and reserves at the next checkpoint.
steps.stop: Divert or terminate the exercise for deteriorating weather, uncertain position, unsafe fuel margin or airspace risk; GPS may be used by the instructor for safety without replacing the assigned visual-navigation exercise.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation; AFH: cross-country flight; current charts, Chart Supplement and AIM

steps.title: Arrive, land and depart at an unfamiliar airport
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Before arrival, review current runway, pattern, traffic and taxi information. Show how to identify the airport/runway visually, make proper non-towered reports or follow a clearance, then stop at a safe place to review departure information.
steps.student: 1. Confirm destination position, runway/wind, published pattern and landing performance. 2. Establish radio awareness and visually identify traffic. 3. Join the correct pattern and fly a stable approach. 4. Land, clear and complete checks before heads-down taxi work. 5. Review departure/taxi routing before taking off again.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival–landing–departure at each required destination; do not omit a source-required airport to meet the clock.
steps.success: Finds the correct airport/runway, integrates safely with traffic and handles taxi/departure without instructor navigation rescue.
errors: Descending toward a guessed airport → remain safe and verify the airport before committing.
Programming or folding charts while crossing a runway → stop at a safe location and perform the task there.
steps.stop: Go around or divert if airport identity, runway suitability, traffic or weather is uncertain; obtain any required clearance before entering controlled movement/runway areas.
steps.reference: AIM: airport operations; current Chart Supplement, airport diagram and POH

steps.title: Recover an uncertain position
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Use an agreed simulated uncertainty while retaining a known safe position. Show stabilizing the airplane, using time/heading/landmarks, identifying a safe navigation aid and requesting assistance early. Discuss climb only when weather, terrain and airspace permit.
steps.student: 1. Admit uncertainty promptly. 2. Maintain control and a safe altitude/course. 3. Check last known position, elapsed time and fuel. 4. Use appropriate navigation/ATC assistance to establish position. 5. Choose a safe landing plan rather than wandering.
steps.repetitions: One deliberate position-recovery exercise with a clear ending fix; solo lessons rehearse this before departure and use it only for real uncertainty.
steps.success: Recognizes loss of confidence, asks for help early and re-establishes position without compromising control, fuel or airspace.
errors: Continuing random turns while searching → stabilize the airplane and work from the last known fix.
Delaying a radio request through embarrassment → state uncertainty and request assistance early.
steps.stop: Stop any simulation before actual uncertainty occurs; for a real lost condition, prioritize safety and obtain assistance. Never intentionally get lost on solo.
steps.reference: PHAK: lost procedures; AIM: assistance and communications

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
Student explains the new exercise and performs its sequence with the assistance appropriate to introduction, followed by a corrected repeat when safe.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.
Name the next corrected exercise and verify every unfinished source requirement before moving on.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Ground supervision: before release verify current solo authority, route/area, weather, fuel, aircraft condition and contact/return plan. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit

steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Show how the planned course, wind correction, groundspeed and leg time produce a predicted position. At the next visual checkpoint compare prediction with observation, then revise the remaining leg time and fuel estimate.
