errors: Recalculating heads-down for too long → write only essentials and pause calculation while controlling/looking outside.
Accepting a predicted fix without visual confirmation → compare with two ground features.
steps.stop: Suspend calculation for traffic, workload, worsening weather or position uncertainty; aviate and use an appropriate navigation/ATC safety resource.
steps.reference: PHAK: dead reckoning and wind correction; Sport PTS: Navigation

steps.title: Arrive, land and depart at an unfamiliar airport
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Before arrival, review current runway, pattern, traffic and taxi information. Show how to identify the airport/runway visually, make proper non-towered reports or follow a clearance, then stop at a safe place to review departure information.
steps.student: 1. Confirm destination position, runway/wind, published pattern and landing performance. 2. Establish radio awareness and visually identify traffic. 3. Join the correct pattern and fly a stable approach. 4. Land, clear and complete checks before heads-down taxi work. 5. Review departure/taxi routing before taking off again.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival–landing–departure at each required destination; do not omit a source-required airport to meet the clock.
steps.success: Finds the correct airport/runway, integrates safely with traffic and handles taxi/departure without instructor navigation rescue.
errors: Descending toward a guessed airport → remain safe and verify the airport before committing.
Programming or folding charts while crossing a runway → stop at a safe location and perform the task there.
steps.stop: Go around or divert if airport identity, runway suitability, traffic or weather is uncertain; obtain any required clearance before entering controlled movement/runway areas.
steps.reference: AIM: airport operations; current Chart Supplement, airport diagram and POH

steps.title: Recover an uncertain position
steps.instructor: Observe the first attempt without continuous prompting. After a safe reset, give one diagnosis, show the correction if needed and require another attempt: Use an agreed simulated uncertainty while retaining a known safe position. Show stabilizing the airplane, using time/heading/landmarks, identifying a safe navigation aid and requesting assistance early. Discuss climb only when weather, terrain and airspace permit.
steps.student: 1. Admit uncertainty promptly. 2. Maintain control and a safe altitude/course. 3. Check last known position, elapsed time and fuel. 4. Use appropriate navigation/ATC assistance to establish position. 5. Choose a safe landing plan rather than wandering.
steps.repetitions: One deliberate position-recovery exercise with a clear ending fix; solo lessons rehearse this before departure and use it only for real uncertainty.
steps.success: Recognizes loss of confidence, asks for help early and re-establishes position without compromising control, fuel or airspace.
errors: Continuing random turns while searching → stabilize the airplane and work from the last known fix.
Delaying a radio request through embarrassment → state uncertainty and request assistance early.
steps.stop: Stop any simulation before actual uncertainty occurs; for a real lost condition, prioritize safety and obtain assistance. Never intentionally get lost on solo.
steps.reference: PHAK: lost procedures; AIM: assistance and communications

steps.title: Emergency descent: controlled escape from an urgent hazard
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Brief a simulated smoke/fire or other urgent descent need using the POH procedure. Verify clear airspace, terrain and recovery altitude. Demonstrate approved configuration, bank, airspeed and checklist priorities without exceeding any limitation.
steps.student: 1. State the simulated hazard and approved immediate actions. 2. Clear the descent path. 3. Establish the POH emergency-descent procedure. 4. Monitor airspeed, load and terrain. 5. Recover by the briefed safe altitude and decide where to land.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration on introduction and one student descent if recovery margin is ample; one independently flown scenario on assessment.
steps.success: Uses the correct aircraft procedure, descends promptly within limits and retains terrain/traffic awareness through recovery.
errors: Treating maximum descent rate as the only goal → prioritize aircraft limits and terrain clearance.
Missing the recovery altitude while checking a list → keep the descent path and altitude in the scan.
steps.stop: Recover earlier than planned if traffic, terrain, speed/load or weather is unfavorable. No real system disabling or descent toward an unsafe floor.
steps.reference: AFH: emergency descents; Sport PTS: Emergency Descent; POH

steps.title: Choose and fly a diversion
steps.instructor: Demonstrate with an explicit control transfer, then coach the student: Present a briefed weather, fuel or destination problem without creating a real hazard. Show selecting a suitable alternative, estimating heading/time/fuel, checking terrain/airspace and changing the flight plan or informing ATC as appropriate.
steps.student: 1. State the reason to abandon the original plan. 2. Choose a reachable suitable airport. 3. Estimate heading, distance, time and fuel. 4. Check terrain, airspace, weather and runway information. 5. Fly toward it, refine the estimate and explain the new decision gates.
steps.repetitions: One complete diversion decision and two position/ETA updates along the new course.
steps.success: Chooses early, keeps flying while planning and selects an alternative with safe fuel, terrain and weather margins.
errors: Choosing the nearest symbol without checking suitability → verify runway, weather and airport status.
Continuing the old course while calculating → establish a safe interim heading and workload plan.
steps.stop: End the scenario and provide needed assistance if actual position, weather, terrain or fuel margin is threatened. Do not continue toward a fictitious hazard.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation and aeronautical decision-making; Sport PTS: Diversion

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Let the student brief and fly the arrival; diagnose one energy or alignment issue only after a safe landing/reset. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

completion: Complete all required tasks safely, including any named unfinished work in continued training; preserve actual aircraft/traffic/weather/fuel margins.
Evaluate actual control, decisions and assistance level rather than elapsed minutes. Use the applicable current Sport PTS and Part 61 gate; early instruction is not a final practical-test result.
Reconcile at least two actual hours of qualifying dual cross-country training from the full experience record; do not infer it solely from this 120-minute allocation.
debrief: Ask for the earliest error/decision cue, then compare the first and final attempt with actual control and assistance evidence.
Reconcile actual flight/solo/cross-country time and full-stop counts in the appropriate records outside this temporary guide.
Name the next corrected exercise and verify every unfinished source requirement before moving on.

steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.

steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and confirm the aircraft configuration and safe recovery floor. 2. Establish the instructor-briefed current Sport PTS slow-flight condition. 3. Hold heading/altitude with coordinated controls and trim. 4. Make briefed gentle turns, a climb and a descent without exceeding control margin. 5. Recover to ordinary flight in the POH sequence; explain the effect of angle of attack, load and power.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains the agreed near-stall condition, coordination and safe recovery margin with lesson-appropriate assistance. At the final Sport PTS assessment, use the current specified altitude/heading/airspeed/bank tolerances rather than applying Private Pilot ACS criteria.
errors: Bank increasing while the ball moves off center → reduce bank and coordinate rudder before continuing.
Retracting flaps abruptly → use the approved sequence and manage the resulting pitch/sink change.
steps.stop: Recover for an actual stall, loss of coordination, unsafe altitude trend, aircraft restriction or the prebriefed floor. A warning cue expected in the agreed near-stall condition is assessed in context; unexpected deterioration requires recovery. Complete the task no lower than the current Sport PTS minimum, and use a higher floor when safety/POH requires it. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: slow flight; Sport PTS: Slow Flight

steps.title: Full power-off stalls: approach scenario
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and brief the recovery floor. 2. Select the assigned approved flap configuration. 3. Establish the approach-type descent and enter the stall with coordinated controls. 4. Recognize the full stall, recover promptly and return to climb/cruise. 5. Repeat the alternate configuration only after a stable reset.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Recognizes the full stall, promptly unloads and restores controlled flight without a secondary stall; assistance level follows the lesson gate.
errors: Delaying the unload while reaching for controls → reduce angle of attack before attending to configuration.
Retracting all flaps while still sinking → use the approved incremental recovery sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw, a wing drop that exceeds the briefed demonstration, an aircraft limitation or the recovery floor; no intentional spin demonstration.
steps.reference: AFH: power-off stalls; Sport PTS: Power-Off Stalls; POH

steps.title: Full power-on stalls: departure scenario
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and select the approved entry configuration and power. 2. Establish a coordinated departure-type entry. 3. Identify the full-stall indication. 4. Reduce angle of attack, maintain directional control and recover. 5. Reset before any approved turning entry.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains coordination through entry and recovery, recognizes the stall and avoids a secondary stall while returning to a safe climb.
errors: Rudder pressure unchanged as speed decreases → actively cross-check coordination and adjust rudder.
Aiming for an extreme pitch attitude → use the approved entry and judge the stall by aerodynamic cues.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for developing yaw/roll divergence or the recovery floor; instructor takes control before a spin tendency develops. No intentional spins.
steps.reference: AFH: power-on stalls; Sport PTS: Power-On Stalls; POH

steps.title: Steep turns in both directions
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current Sport PTS tolerances. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Clear and choose altitude, airspeed and rollout reference. 2. Establish the briefed bank with coordinated controls. 3. Maintain the outside pitch picture and cross-check altitude. 4. Complete the turn, roll out and stabilize. 5. Repeat in the other direction after clearing.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Controls bank, pitch and power without fixation; introductory performance may need coaching, while final assessment uses current Sport PTS tolerances.
errors: Trying to correct altitude with bank alone → restore the briefed bank and make a small pitch/power correction.
Looking only inside → return to the outside pitch reference and make short instrument cross-checks.
steps.stop: Roll out if bank, load, airspeed or altitude approaches an aircraft limit or safe practice boundary; never chase a tolerance through unsafe control inputs.
steps.reference: AFH: steep turns; Sport PTS: Steep Turns

steps.title: Return, stabilized approach and final landing
steps.instructor: Assess an independent arrival and landing; provide safety intervention if needed and record it. Recheck weather/traffic, airport/runway identity, landing performance, pattern entry and the aircraft-specific stabilized-approach gate. Teach an early go-around decision whenever safe landing is uncertain.
steps.student: 1. Secure maneuver/route work and complete descent checks. 2. Confirm airport/runway, wind and pattern/clearance. 3. Join with traffic awareness and an appropriate radio report. 4. Fly the approved stable approach and manage wind correction. 5. Land aligned and maintain control through rollout, or go around early.
steps.repetitions: One complete arrival and final landing; include a go-around whenever the real approach fails the briefed gate.
steps.success: Maintains traffic separation and a stable approach; touches down aligned with adequate runway margin or makes an early safe go-around.
errors: Forcing the landing to finish on time → go around and accept additional flight time.
Fixating on the aiming point → maintain airspeed, alignment, traffic and runway margin in the scan.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable path/speed, drift, clearance uncertainty or unsafe runway margin; divert if weather, fuel or lighting makes return unsuitable.
steps.reference: AFH: traffic patterns and landings; POH; AIM: airport operations

steps.title: Clear, taxi in, shut down and secure
steps.instructor: Observe after-landing and securing without distraction; inspect the learner’s checklist completion and aircraft condition. Keep the airplane controlled until clear of the runway, then use after-landing/taxi/shutdown checklists. Account for keys, tie-downs/chocks, discrepancies and postflight reporting.
steps.student: 1. Clear the runway fully and stop when needed before after-landing checks. 2. Follow the cleared/briefed taxi route with wind correction. 3. Park and shut down using the POH checklist. 4. Secure the aircraft and inspect for discrepancies. 5. Report actual tasks/counts and any concern before leaving.
steps.repetitions: One complete runway-exit-to-secured-aircraft sequence; parked debrief follows this flight block.
steps.success: Runway is clear before heads-down work; aircraft is safely shut down/secured and discrepancies are communicated.
errors: Doing cleanup during rollout → maintain control and wait until clear.
Leaving a tie-down/checklist item unverified → walk around and confirm the secured condition.
steps.stop: Stop taxi and request assistance for an uncertain clearance, brake/control problem or obstruction; do not leave an unsecured or unreported discrepant aircraft.
steps.reference: POH: after landing, shutdown and securing; AIM: taxi

preparation.title: Current Sport airplane PTS: lesson-related tasks
Current FAA Airplane Flying Handbook: related maneuver procedures

lessons.applicability: Single-engine-land airplane Sport pathway, using the current 2026 course portal’s October 2025 syllabus and currently effective FAA-S-8081-29B PTS. Check aircraft eligibility under current §61.316 and all privileges/limitations/endorsements in Part 61; the source’s older LSA shorthand does not establish current eligibility. Set speeds, power, configuration, recovery floors and performance from the actual POH/AFM and supplements with the instructor. The core route is daytime VFR; any expanded privilege requires its separate current training/endorsement and eligibility conditions.
lessons.title: Final Sport readiness assessment
lessons.summary: Use a complete current Sport airplane PTS plan of action and independent evidence of knowledge, aircraft control, navigation and emergency decisions. Verify the Part 61 experience and endorsement requirements separately.
objectives: Use a complete current Sport airplane PTS plan of action and independent evidence of knowledge, aircraft control, navigation and emergency decisions. Verify the Part 61 experience and endorsement requirements separately.
Use safe setup/control, recognize the earliest error cue and show a corrected repeat or independent assessment evidence appropriate to the lesson.
prerequisites: Complete the prerequisite ground preparation and resolve unsafe/deficient items from the preceding flight.
Have the instructor verify actual aircraft eligibility, operational limits and current Sport privileges/endorsements for the proposed mission.
Prepare an independent plan of action and identify required tasks not yet safely demonstrated.
briefing: Check the actual aircraft eligibility, limitations and installed supplements with current Sport privileges/endorsements. Select POH speeds/configurations, weather/crosswind limits, runway margins, fuel, practice area and safe recovery boundaries before movement.

Agree on positive control transfer, instructor lookout and authorized simulations. Keep aircraft control, traffic and terrain ahead of discussion; no intentional spins, surprise shutdowns or hazardous low-altitude failures.

Preview the ordered exercises: Navigate by landmarks and magnetic compass; Choose and fly a diversion; Slow flight: configuration, coordination and exit; Full power-off stalls: approach scenario; Full power-on stalls: departure scenario; Steep turns in both directions.

Explain angle of attack, stall warning/full-stall cues, yaw and spin prevention. This Sport PTS slow-flight condition is near an immediate stall, unlike Private ACS slow flight. Choose enough altitude to finish slow-flight/stall tasks above the applicable current PTS minimum and any higher aircraft/terrain safety floor.

State the assessment rules: no coaching during the independent attempt, safety intervention is documented, and all unobserved/deficient required tasks need continued training or assessment. Stage I determines safe solo readiness; the final check uses the current Sport PTS.

Assess certificates/eligibility, airworthiness, route planning, weather, airspace, aircraft systems/performance, human factors, principles of flight, airport signs/markings/lighting and emergency/survival equipment. Review all knowledge-test deficiency areas and applicable experience/endorsement prerequisites.
preflightGuide: Review aircraft documents/maintenance status, weather/NOTAMs, loading, fuel and current Sport aircraft/operation eligibility. Instructor verifies suitability and authorization.
Use the actual POH/AFM walkaround, fuel/oil and defect assessment. Set seats/restraints/controls, secure loose items and prepare charts/radios.
Give the aircraft-specific passenger/positive-control-transfer briefing; on solo review the specific mission and ground contact plan before release.
lessons.timingNote: The source target is 72 flight minutes and 90 discussion minutes, but its complete task list needs more observation time for many students/routes. Continue the assessment for every unobserved/deficient task; do not recommend a practical test from the timer alone.

steps.title: Start, taxi, run-up and runway confirmation
steps.instructor: Observe student-led surface operations without prompting; safety intervention means further training is needed. Use the actual start checklist, a clear propeller area, immediate engine indication check, early brake check, airport diagram, hold-short discipline and the before-takeoff checklist. Rehearse any ambiguous taxi clearance while stopped.
steps.student: 1. Start using the POH checklist and verify indications. 2. Test brakes at an appropriate safe speed. 3. Identify the route and every runway crossing. 4. Use required radio calls/readbacks and obtain crossing clearances. 5. Perform run-up/checks in a suitable location. 6. Confirm runway, wind, takeoff plan and rejection triggers before entry.
steps.repetitions: One complete start-to-runway sequence; stop for any uncertain clearance or configuration.
steps.success: Correct checklist, route, clearances and runway identified; aircraft remains controlled and no hold line is crossed without authority.
errors: Heads-down taxi work → stop in a safe place before consulting a chart or programming equipment.
Run-up hurried because of traffic → wait and complete the checks before taking the runway.
steps.stop: Do not depart with an unresolved aircraft discrepancy, uncertain clearance, failed brake/engine check or weather/endorsement exceedance.
steps.reference: POH: normal procedures; AIM: taxi/runway operations; FAA runway-incursion guidance

steps.title: Takeoff, climb and safe transit
steps.instructor: Observe an independent departure and traffic scan; give only task/route instructions. Confirm wake separation, runway alignment, aircraft-approved rotation/climb/configuration, crosswind correction and the published/assigned departure. For local work select a legal practice area, clear it and brief recovery boundaries before any maneuver.
steps.student: 1. Verify traffic, clearance when required and the correct runway. 2. Apply the approved takeoff technique while maintaining centerline and wind correction. 3. Climb at the POH/briefed condition and change configuration as approved. 4. Follow the published/assigned departure or pattern. 5. Level off, trim, complete checks and keep collision-avoidance scans.
steps.repetitions: One normal departure; use crosswind technique only within the aircraft and lesson authorization.
steps.success: Maintains runway/ground track, a safe climb and separation, then arrives at the intended area with the airplane configured and trimmed.
errors: Letting the nose drift on power application → use coordinated directional control and stop/reject if required.
Task briefing during a critical climb → finish the climb/checks before discussing the practice exercise.
steps.stop: Reject for a real takeoff abnormality per the briefed POH plan; discontinue training for wake, weather, traffic, fuel or terrain/airspace risk. No unbriefed low-altitude engine-failure simulation.
steps.reference: AFH: normal/crosswind takeoff; POH: climb; AIM: traffic/wake avoidance

steps.title: Navigate by landmarks and magnetic compass
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. Orient the chart and identify two independent position clues. 2. Fly the planned heading with wind correction. 3. Mark actual checkpoint time and revise ETA/fuel. 4. Scan weather and airspace ahead. 5. Explain the next landmark and landing alternative; make the assigned radio contact at a low-workload time.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Maintains a continuous position estimate, recognizes drift early and updates ETA/fuel while keeping an outside scan.
errors: Mistaking one similar feature for the checkpoint → verify with a second independent landmark.
Ignoring time/fuel after a wind change → update groundspeed, ETA and reserves at the next checkpoint.
steps.stop: Divert or terminate the exercise for deteriorating weather, uncertain position, unsafe fuel margin or airspace risk; GPS may be used by the instructor for safety without replacing the assigned visual-navigation exercise.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation; AFH: cross-country flight; current charts, Chart Supplement and AIM

steps.title: Choose and fly a diversion
steps.instructor: Assign this task under the prebriefed plan of action, retain safety lookout and observe independent execution. Look for this task-specific result: Chooses early, keeps flying while planning and selects an alternative with safe fuel, terrain and weather margins. Apply the current Sport PTS or Stage I solo-readiness criteria as appropriate. Do not demonstrate, hint or coach; document any safety intervention and mark unobserved elements for a continued assessment.
steps.student: 1. State the reason to abandon the original plan. 2. Choose a reachable suitable airport. 3. Estimate heading, distance, time and fuel. 4. Check terrain, airspace, weather and runway information. 5. Fly toward it, refine the estimate and explain the new decision gates.
steps.repetitions: One independently performed task sequence; repeat only under the assessor’s stated policy. A coached retry is training, not the original independent result.
steps.success: Chooses early, keeps flying while planning and selects an alternative with safe fuel, terrain and weather margins.
errors: Choosing the nearest symbol without checking suitability → verify runway, weather and airport status.
Continuing the old course while calculating → establish a safe interim heading and workload plan.
steps.stop: End the scenario and provide needed assistance if actual position, weather, terrain or fuel margin is threatened. Do not continue toward a fictitious hazard.
steps.reference: PHAK: navigation and aeronautical decision-making; Sport PTS: Diversion

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop
steps.instructor: Start with a stable attitude and power setting. Demonstrate attitude change, cross-check of performance, small correction, then trim. Explain which indication confirms each change; let the learner verbalize the scan before removing prompts.
steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check.
steps.repetitions: Two level-offs in each direction and at least two left/right turns; repeat the weakest transition.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Build the scan and trim loop; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Device setup and clearance review
steps.instructor: Verify the device configuration, intended training credit, database and weather scenario. Set failures only by the approved device method; state whether pauses are instruction or evaluation.
steps.student: Set up the cockpit as in the aircraft, verify navigation sources, copy the starting clearance, and explain today’s equipment/failure and approach plans.
steps.repetitions: One complete setup and clearance readback.
steps.success: Can explain the actual simulated aircraft/equipment state before the scenario runs.
errors: Unverified setup → compare the device state with the intended aircraft/manual.
steps.stop: Do not log unapproved credit or continue with an invalid configuration.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Failure recognition and backup control
steps.instructor: Brief a realistic failure supported by the aircraft or device. Reveal its indications, require independent confirmation, then demonstrate the remaining scan. Never disable equipment that compromises the actual flight or required equipment.
steps.student: Identify the simulated failed instrument, cross-check its reliability, establish control with valid indications, and use backup attitude/heading resources. Make timed turns and compass-supported turns with appropriate acceleration/dip error awareness.
steps.repetitions: Two different failures and one heading change each direction; device sessions may freeze only after the attempt for explanation.
steps.success: Rejects misleading data, controls the aircraft with valid sources, and communicates the degraded capability.
errors: Following a failed display → cross-check independent indications and isolate the bad source.
Treating compass as steady during a maneuver → stabilize before reading and use timed/backup methods as appropriate.
steps.stop: End the simulation for loss of orientation, unsafe deviations, unavailable reliable backup, or real equipment abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Failure recognition and backup control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Recognize and recover unusual attitudes
steps.instructor: Brief transfer of control and the approved recovery procedure. Present modest, realistic unusual attitudes within aircraft limitations; demonstrate how reliable indications distinguish nose-high, nose-low, spiral, and failed-display situations.
steps.student: Diagnose the attitude from reliable indications, use the aircraft-appropriate recovery priorities, stabilize attitude/power/airspeed, and explain how fixation or automation confusion caused the upset.
steps.repetitions: One nose-high and one nose-low recovery; repeat using the briefed reduced instrument set if the source lesson calls for it.
steps.success: Recognizes the condition, promptly reduces the immediate risk, avoids secondary loss of control, and re-establishes a useful scan.
errors: Control response before diagnosis → identify the attitude using reliable cues first.
Recovery creates a secondary stall/overspeed → manage angle of attack, bank, power, and load according to the approved procedure.
steps.stop: Instructor ends setup or takes control before aircraft limits, safety altitude, or recovery margin are threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Recognize and recover unusual attitudes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Secure device and verify results

steps.student: Complete the simulated shutdown/checklist, describe the main error and correction, and identify the remaining practice task.
steps.repetitions: One complete scenario wrap-up.
steps.success: Ends with an accurate account of what was practiced and what remains.
errors: Treating paused time as flight → record only credit permitted by the device authorization.
steps.stop: End before fatigue makes further practice ineffective.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Failure recognition and backup control
steps.instructor: Brief a realistic failure supported by the aircraft or device. Reveal its indications, require independent confirmation, then demonstrate the remaining scan. Never disable equipment that compromises the actual flight or required equipment.
steps.student: Identify the simulated failed instrument, cross-check its reliability, establish control with valid indications, and use backup attitude/heading resources. Make timed turns and compass-supported turns with appropriate acceleration/dip error awareness.
steps.repetitions: Two different failures and one heading change each direction; device sessions may freeze only after the attempt for explanation.
steps.success: Rejects misleading data, controls the aircraft with valid sources, and communicates the degraded capability.
errors: Following a failed display → cross-check independent indications and isolate the bad source.
Treating compass as steady during a maneuver → stabilize before reading and use timed/backup methods as appropriate.
steps.stop: End the simulation for loss of orientation, unsafe deviations, unavailable reliable backup, or real equipment abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Failure recognition and backup control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Combine attitude changes into flight patterns
steps.instructor: Draw and brief a climb-turn-level-descent sequence before flight. First fly it with a spoken scan, then give only the next altitude/heading clearance. Use the pattern to expose transitions rather than add new maneuver complexity.
steps.student: Fly the briefed rectangular or vertical pattern using assigned headings, altitudes, and rates. Call the next configuration and level-off in advance; repeat with fewer instructor cues.
steps.repetitions: Two complete patterns: coached, then independent; repeat one weak corner or level-off.
steps.success: Moves smoothly between maneuvers, stays oriented, and maintains the selected parameters without losing the cross-check.
errors: Next leg surprises the learner → pause the sequence, restate the picture, then rehearse the transition.
Trim omitted → stabilize each leg before moving to the next.
steps.stop: Simplify to straight-and-level flight if the scan or orientation deteriorates.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Combine attitude changes into flight patterns; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

errors: Unverified setup → compare the device state with the intended aircraft/manual.

steps.title: VOR orientation, intercept, and wind correction
steps.instructor: On the ground confirm receiver-check status, tune and identify the facility, and draw the selected radial/course relationship. Demonstrate one intercept with the correct source and TO/FROM interpretation, then compare tracking corrections before and after wind change.
steps.student: Tune, identify, select the course, state position relative to the station, intercept, and track inbound and outbound. Detect station passage, change the course, and cross-check position with another valid source.
steps.repetitions: Two intercepts with opposite geometry, inbound/outbound tracking, and one station passage or device equivalent.
steps.success: Uses a valid identified signal, distinguishes radial from course, and corrects wind without chasing the needle.
errors: Reverse sensing → verify selected course, TO/FROM indication, and intended direction.
Intercept mistaken for track → reduce to a sustainable wind correction after capture.
steps.stop: Discontinue use of an unreliable or unidentifiable signal; use a briefed legal alternative and tell ATC when required.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; VOR orientation, intercept, and wind correction; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

errors: Treating paused time as flight → record only credit permitted by the device authorization.
steps.stop: End before fatigue makes further practice ineffective.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: GPS setup, sequencing, and integrity
steps.instructor: Use the installed navigator manual to show source selection, flight-plan loading, leg activation, direct-to, nearest, and scaling changes. Explain integrity alerts and how WAAS/RAIM availability affects a planned procedure; confirm the next mode before changing it.
steps.student: Load and verify a short route, intercept an active leg, observe waypoint sequencing, accept a reroute with direct-to, then choose an appropriate nearest alternate. State navigation source, active leg, scaling, and response to an integrity alert.
steps.repetitions: One complete route plus one reroute and one integrity/failure decision.
steps.success: Verifies every clearance and active leg, understands available guidance, and preserves control while programming.
errors: Wrong leg activated → compare clearance, map, flight-plan list, and CDI before executing.
Heads-down programming → stabilize first; ask for delay or use a simpler navigation method.
steps.stop: Stop programming for control/traffic priorities; discontinue approach guidance when integrity or required equipment is unavailable.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; GPS setup, sequencing, and integrity; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Autopilot modes and manual reversion
steps.instructor: Brief the approved engagement envelope, limitations, disconnect methods, and failure signs. Demonstrate each installed mode by stating what is armed, active, commanded, and actually happening; then disconnect and hand-fly the same segment.
steps.student: Select heading, navigation, altitude, and permitted climb/descent modes. Confirm annunciations and resulting flight path after every change. Recover from a simulated wrong mode or failed automation using the approved disconnect and manual control.
steps.repetitions: One mode sequence, one capture verification, and two different disconnect/reversion methods if installed.
steps.success: Monitors rather than assumes automation behavior; disconnects early when it no longer supports the plan.
errors: Armed mistaken for active → point to annunciations and confirm actual capture.
Fighting engaged servos → use the approved disconnect and stabilize manually.
steps.stop: Disengage for unexpected flight path, unresolved mode confusion, or operation outside approved limitations.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Autopilot modes and manual reversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Failure recognition and backup control
steps.instructor: Brief a realistic failure supported by the aircraft or device. Reveal its indications, require independent confirmation, then demonstrate the remaining scan. Never disable equipment that compromises the actual flight or required equipment.
steps.student: Identify the simulated failed instrument, cross-check its reliability, establish control with valid indications, and use backup attitude/heading resources. Make timed turns and compass-supported turns with appropriate acceleration/dip error awareness.
steps.repetitions: Two different failures and one heading change each direction; device sessions may freeze only after the attempt for explanation.
steps.success: Rejects misleading data, controls the aircraft with valid sources, and communicates the degraded capability.
errors: Following a failed display → cross-check independent indications and isolate the bad source.
Treating compass as steady during a maneuver → stabilize before reading and use timed/backup methods as appropriate.
steps.stop: End the simulation for loss of orientation, unsafe deviations, unavailable reliable backup, or real equipment abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Failure recognition and backup control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

completion: Maintains aircraft control, checklist/clearance discipline, and safe decisions throughout the complete session.

carryForward: Source task for another focused block if not observed today: VOR Procedures (if equipped). Select the applicable FAA/aircraft procedure and schedule adequate instruction; no completion is implied by this checklist.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction
steps.instructor: Have the learner read back and sketch the clearance, fix, course, direction, restriction, and expect-further-clearance information. Demonstrate fix-crossing flow and one entry; explain that the chosen entry must remain within protected airspace.
steps.student: Copy and verify the clearance, select a defensible entry, cross the fix, establish the hold, and adjust outbound timing/distance and heading for wind. Communicate any inability and track clearance limits.
steps.repetitions: Two entries from different arrival directions and two complete circuits; one timed and one distance-based hold when available.
steps.success: Remains within the protected procedure, meets altitude/speed constraints, and corrects timing without losing control.
errors: Entry guessed from a moving display → orient the published inbound course and aircraft arrival direction before choosing.
Timing starts at the wrong place → identify the published timing convention and fix crossing.
steps.stop: Request clarification or vectors before reaching an unclear limit; abandon exercise for unsafe control or containment.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: ILS and approved vertical guidance
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent.
steps.repetitions: Two approaches with different guidance where available: one landing transition and one missed approach.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report.
steps.repetitions: One complete approach and one vectored approach; at least one missed approach.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.

steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.

steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

errors: Tightening bank to rescue the landing → abandon the unstable position and go missed.

lessons.timingLabel: Publisher lesson target; SUAREZ.CFI phase allocation is recommended. Brief/debrief are separate from flight.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Autopilot modes and manual reversion
steps.instructor: Brief the approved engagement envelope, limitations, disconnect methods, and failure signs. Demonstrate each installed mode by stating what is armed, active, commanded, and actually happening; then disconnect and hand-fly the same segment.
steps.student: Select heading, navigation, altitude, and permitted climb/descent modes. Confirm annunciations and resulting flight path after every change. Recover from a simulated wrong mode or failed automation using the approved disconnect and manual control.
steps.repetitions: One mode sequence, one capture verification, and two different disconnect/reversion methods if installed.
steps.success: Monitors rather than assumes automation behavior; disconnects early when it no longer supports the plan.
errors: Armed mistaken for active → point to annunciations and confirm actual capture.
Fighting engaged servos → use the approved disconnect and stabilize manually.
steps.stop: Disengage for unexpected flight path, unresolved mode confusion, or operation outside approved limitations.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Autopilot modes and manual reversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: ILS and approved vertical guidance
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent.
steps.repetitions: Two approaches with different guidance where available: one landing transition and one missed approach.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report.
steps.repetitions: One complete approach and one vectored approach; at least one missed approach.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.
Early descent after a shortcut → verify the cleared segment and remaining altitude restrictions.
steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction
steps.instructor: Have the learner read back and sketch the clearance, fix, course, direction, restriction, and expect-further-clearance information. Demonstrate fix-crossing flow and one entry; explain that the chosen entry must remain within protected airspace.
steps.student: Copy and verify the clearance, select a defensible entry, cross the fix, establish the hold, and adjust outbound timing/distance and heading for wind. Communicate any inability and track clearance limits.
steps.repetitions: Two entries from different arrival directions and two complete circuits; one timed and one distance-based hold when available.
steps.success: Remains within the protected procedure, meets altitude/speed constraints, and corrects timing without losing control.
errors: Entry guessed from a moving display → orient the published inbound course and aircraft arrival direction before choosing.
Timing starts at the wrong place → identify the published timing convention and fix crossing.
steps.stop: Request clarification or vectors before reaching an unclear limit; abandon exercise for unsafe control or containment.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Visual transition and circling decision
steps.instructor: Brief approach category, published circling area, wind, visual references, missed procedure, and aircraft/school operating limits. Demonstrate the ground track and decision gates on a chart before using an authorized visual or device scenario.
steps.student: Maintain required visual contact and circling altitude while positioning for a stabilized landing. Reject a poor position early; explain and fly the appropriate missed procedure if visual contact or a safe landing path is lost.
steps.repetitions: One straight-in visual transition and one authorized circling scenario; the device can rehearse loss of visual reference.
steps.success: Keeps the aircraft within the protected area, preserves required visibility, and makes an early conservative missed decision.
errors: Tightening bank to rescue the landing → abandon the unstable position and go missed.
Visual contact lost with no plan → brief the missed transition before starting the circle.
steps.stop: Go missed immediately when required references, protected-area assurance, or a stabilized landing path are lost.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Visual transition and circling decision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

completion: Maintains aircraft control, checklist/clearance discipline, and safe decisions throughout the complete session.
Demonstrates the selected objectives at today’s expected level: coached learning during introduction, fewer cues during review, and current ACS criteria independently at checks.
Unmet or unobserved source tasks are identified for a later flight; elapsed time and checkmarks are not a proficiency endorsement.
debrief: Learner names the strongest result and the first decision/control error.
Instructor ties one observed error to its cause, gives a specific correction, and confirms the next practice priority.
Compare actual exercise/route time with this plan and verify any regulatory experience credit independently.
carryForward: Source task for another focused block if not observed today: ATC Clearances and Clearance Compliance. Select the applicable FAA/aircraft procedure and schedule adequate instruction; no completion is implied by this checklist.
lessons.applicability: Aircraft-neutral: set speeds, configurations, limitations, approved simulation methods, and any endorsement conditions from the actual aircraft and current rules.
briefing: Agree on the named exercise priorities, aircraft-specific procedures, stop/takeover gates, weather/fuel/route limits, and how remaining source tasks will be carried forward.
Learner explains the initial plan and one credible failure/alternate decision. Instructor corrects misunderstanding before departure.

steps.title: Failure recognition and backup control
steps.instructor: Brief a realistic failure supported by the aircraft or device. Reveal its indications, require independent confirmation, then demonstrate the remaining scan. Never disable equipment that compromises the actual flight or required equipment.
steps.student: Identify the simulated failed instrument, cross-check its reliability, establish control with valid indications, and use backup attitude/heading resources. Make timed turns and compass-supported turns with appropriate acceleration/dip error awareness.
steps.repetitions: Two different failures and one heading change each direction; device sessions may freeze only after the attempt for explanation.
steps.success: Rejects misleading data, controls the aircraft with valid sources, and communicates the degraded capability.
errors: Following a failed display → cross-check independent indications and isolate the bad source.
Treating compass as steady during a maneuver → stabilize before reading and use timed/backup methods as appropriate.
steps.stop: End the simulation for loss of orientation, unsafe deviations, unavailable reliable backup, or real equipment abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Failure recognition and backup control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.repetitions: One complete setup and clearance readback.
steps.success: Can explain the actual simulated aircraft/equipment state before the scenario runs.
errors: Unverified setup → compare the device state with the intended aircraft/manual.
steps.stop: Do not log unapproved credit or continue with an invalid configuration.

steps.title: IFR route, weather, and contingency decisions
steps.instructor: Build an actual route with current weather, NOTAMs, alternates, fuel, departure/arrival restrictions, and approach options. In flight present one credible weather or routing change and require a decision supported by fuel and aircraft capability; rehearse lost communications without stopping real radio use.
steps.student: File the plan when appropriate, verify the clearance, fly the route and altitude restrictions, and update ETA/fuel/weather at each leg. Select an alternate before the escape option disappears; explain the applicable lost-communications response and request assistance while communications work.
steps.repetitions: At least two route checkpoints, one changed-clearance readback, one diversion decision, and approaches at planned destinations.
steps.success: Remains ahead of route and weather, keeps reserves and terrain/airspace protection, and communicates changes promptly.
errors: Continuing toward deteriorating weather → identify the last safe alternate and decide before reaching it.
Clearance lost in the flight plan → compare active route against the actual amended clearance.
steps.stop: Real weather, aircraft capability, or fuel margin controls the route; terminate a training scenario before it reduces safe options.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; IFR route, weather, and contingency decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report.
steps.repetitions: One complete approach and one vectored approach; at least one missed approach.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.
Early descent after a shortcut → verify the cleared segment and remaining altitude restrictions.
steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: ILS and approved vertical guidance
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent.
steps.repetitions: Two approaches with different guidance where available: one landing transition and one missed approach.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Visual transition and circling decision

steps.repetitions: One straight-in visual transition and one authorized circling scenario; the device can rehearse loss of visual reference.
steps.success: Keeps the aircraft within the protected area, preserves required visibility, and makes an early conservative missed decision.
errors: Tightening bank to rescue the landing → abandon the unstable position and go missed.
Visual contact lost with no plan → brief the missed transition before starting the circle.
steps.stop: Go missed immediately when required references, protected-area assurance, or a stabilized landing path are lost.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Visual transition and circling decision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Secure device and verify results
