steps.repetitions: One complete scenario wrap-up.
steps.success: Ends with an accurate account of what was practiced and what remains.
errors: Treating paused time as flight → record only credit permitted by the device authorization.
steps.stop: End before fatigue makes further practice ineffective.

Before dispatch choose and name approach A, B, and C at the actual planned airports; the instructor verifies three different qualifying kinds using navigation systems (for example VOR, ILS, and an eligible RNAV procedure). steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Autopilot modes and manual reversion
steps.instructor: Brief the approved engagement envelope, limitations, disconnect methods, and failure signs. Demonstrate each installed mode by stating what is armed, active, commanded, and actually happening; then disconnect and hand-fly the same segment.
steps.student: Select heading, navigation, altitude, and permitted climb/descent modes. Confirm annunciations and resulting flight path after every change. Recover from a simulated wrong mode or failed automation using the approved disconnect and manual control.
steps.repetitions: One mode sequence, one capture verification, and two different disconnect/reversion methods if installed.
steps.success: Monitors rather than assumes automation behavior; disconnects early when it no longer supports the plan.
errors: Armed mistaken for active → point to annunciations and confirm actual capture.
Fighting engaged servos → use the approved disconnect and stabilize manually.
steps.stop: Disengage for unexpected flight path, unresolved mode confusion, or operation outside approved limitations.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Autopilot modes and manual reversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: IFR route leg 1: navigation and decisions
steps.instructor: Build an actual route with current weather, NOTAMs, alternates, fuel, departure/arrival restrictions, and approach options. In flight present one credible weather or routing change and require a decision supported by fuel and aircraft capability; rehearse lost communications without stopping real radio use.
steps.student: Fly cleared route leg 1 to the airport assigned to approach A. Verify route/altitude restrictions and navigation source; update fuel, weather and alternate options. Complete the required approach at that airport before continuing under the next clearance.
steps.repetitions: Verify cleared route/altitude, ETA, fuel and current destination conditions on this leg.
steps.success: Remains ahead of route and weather, keeps reserves and terrain/airspace protection, and communicates changes promptly.
errors: Continuing toward deteriorating weather → identify the last safe alternate and decide before reaching it.
Clearance lost in the flight plan → compare active route against the actual amended clearance.
steps.stop: Real weather, aircraft capability, or fuel margin controls the route; terminate a training scenario before it reduces safe options.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; IFR route, weather, and contingency decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: A: selected lateral procedure
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report. Fly the briefed missed approach and cleared onward route unless an actual landing is planned. If landing, allocate additional taxi/departure movement time and extend the plan; parked stop time remains separate.
steps.repetitions: Fly the named approach at its planned airport and record actual procedure/navigation system; complete a legal landing or missed as planned. The actual flown route must include an approach at each airport.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.
Early descent after a shortcut → verify the cleared segment and remaining altitude restrictions.
steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: IFR route leg 2: navigation and decisions
steps.instructor: Build an actual route with current weather, NOTAMs, alternates, fuel, departure/arrival restrictions, and approach options. In flight present one credible weather or routing change and require a decision supported by fuel and aircraft capability; rehearse lost communications without stopping real radio use.
steps.student: Fly cleared route leg 2 to the airport assigned to approach B. Verify route/altitude restrictions and navigation source; update fuel, weather and alternate options. Complete the required approach at that airport before continuing under the next clearance.
steps.repetitions: Verify cleared route/altitude, ETA, fuel and current destination conditions on this leg.
steps.success: Remains ahead of route and weather, keeps reserves and terrain/airspace protection, and communicates changes promptly.
errors: Continuing toward deteriorating weather → identify the last safe alternate and decide before reaching it.

steps.stop: Real weather, aircraft capability, or fuel margin controls the route; terminate a training scenario before it reduces safe options.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; IFR route, weather, and contingency decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: B: selected ILS procedure
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent. Fly the briefed missed approach and cleared onward route unless an actual landing is planned. If landing, allocate additional taxi/departure movement time and extend the plan; parked stop time remains separate.
steps.repetitions: Fly the named approach at its planned airport and record actual procedure/navigation system; complete a legal landing or missed as planned. The actual flown route must include an approach at each airport.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: IFR route leg 3: navigation and decisions
steps.instructor: Build an actual route with current weather, NOTAMs, alternates, fuel, departure/arrival restrictions, and approach options. steps.student: Fly cleared route leg 3 to the airport assigned to approach C. Verify route/altitude restrictions and navigation source; update fuel, weather and alternate options. Complete the required approach at that airport before continuing under the next clearance.
steps.repetitions: Verify cleared route/altitude, ETA, fuel and current destination conditions on this leg.

errors: Continuing toward deteriorating weather → identify the last safe alternate and decide before reaching it.

steps.title: C: selected RNAV procedure
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Fly the third planned RNAV approach at its assigned airport. Verify equipment and integrity, the actual guidance annunciation, selected chart minima, and legal visual transition or missed approach. Choose an approach kind that the instructor has confirmed meets the three-kind Part 61 plan; LPV credit/classification must be checked against the applicable standard.
steps.repetitions: Fly the named approach at its planned airport and record actual procedure/navigation system; complete a legal landing or missed as planned. The actual flown route must include an approach at each airport.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.

steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; RNAV approach and vertical-guidance eligibility; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Destination C: qualifying landing
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: After approach C, make the legal visual transition and a stabilized landing at planned destination C, more than 50 NM straight-line from the original departure point. Go missed whenever required for safety; if the qualifying landing cannot be made, use a safe alternate and treat the original training-credit plan as unmet. The flight ends and is secured at this destination.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Assess the learner’s departure, configuration, and course intercept independently; give no coaching during the check.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed clearance, holding entry, and wind correction scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Remains within the protected procedure, meets altitude/speed constraints, and corrects timing without losing control. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Copy and verify the clearance, select a defensible entry, cross the fix, establish the hold, and adjust outbound timing/distance and heading for wind. Communicate any inability and track clearance limits.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Remains within the protected procedure, meets altitude/speed constraints, and corrects timing without losing control.
errors: Entry guessed from a moving display → orient the published inbound course and aircraft arrival direction before choosing.
Timing starts at the wrong place → identify the published timing convention and fix crossing.
steps.stop: Request clarification or vectors before reaching an unclear limit; abandon exercise for unsafe control or containment.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Recognize and recover unusual attitudes
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed recognize and recover unusual attitudes scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Recognizes the condition, promptly reduces the immediate risk, avoids secondary loss of control, and re-establishes a useful scan. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Diagnose the attitude from reliable indications, use the aircraft-appropriate recovery priorities, stabilize attitude/power/airspeed, and explain how fixation or automation confusion caused the upset.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Recognizes the condition, promptly reduces the immediate risk, avoids secondary loss of control, and re-establishes a useful scan.
errors: Control response before diagnosis → identify the attitude using reliable cues first.
Recovery creates a secondary stall/overspeed → manage angle of attack, bank, power, and load according to the approved procedure.
steps.stop: Instructor ends setup or takes control before aircraft limits, safety altitude, or recovery margin are threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Recognize and recover unusual attitudes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: DME arc and position cross-check
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed dme arc and position cross-check scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Remains oriented to the fix, anticipates intercepts, and uses the authorized distance source correctly. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Identify the station or approved substitute, intercept the arc, keep charted distance with incremental corrections, comply with altitude restrictions, and lead the inbound-course intercept.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Remains oriented to the fix, anticipates intercepts, and uses the authorized distance source correctly.
errors: Late arc intercept → calculate/brief lead using speed and geometry before the turn.
Large distance chase → make small heading changes and reassess trend.
steps.stop: Ask for vectors or another procedure if equipment, clearance, or containment is uncertain.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; DME arc and position cross-check; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed lateral approach and missed approach scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.
Early descent after a shortcut → verify the cleared segment and remaining altitude restrictions.
steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: ILS and approved vertical guidance
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed ils and approved vertical guidance scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Failure recognition and backup control
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed failure recognition and backup control scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Rejects misleading data, controls the aircraft with valid sources, and communicates the degraded capability. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Identify the simulated failed instrument, cross-check its reliability, establish control with valid indications, and use backup attitude/heading resources. Make timed turns and compass-supported turns with appropriate acceleration/dip error awareness.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Rejects misleading data, controls the aircraft with valid sources, and communicates the degraded capability.
errors: Following a failed display → cross-check independent indications and isolate the bad source.
Treating compass as steady during a maneuver → stabilize before reading and use timed/backup methods as appropriate.
steps.stop: End the simulation for loss of orientation, unsafe deviations, unavailable reliable backup, or real equipment abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA Instrument Flying Handbook / Instrument Procedures Handbook; Failure recognition and backup control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

courses.overview: An original flight teaching companion organized in the current publisher lesson sequence. Each flight begins with a complete operating plan, then assigns a realistic exercise budget and observable results. Ground entries point to the corresponding preparation; the detailed teaching is in the flight/device lessons. Source targets remain visible. Assessment and exercise selections must be adapted to the actual learner, aircraft, weather, and available facilities.
entryRequirements: Confirm prerequisite certificates, privileges, medical eligibility where required, recency, and aircraft authorization.
Use the applicable POH/AFM, current charts, approved equipment manuals, and current FAA standards.
Reconcile the student’s logbook against current Part 61 separately; completing these timed lessons does not establish certificate eligibility.
Device time is not aircraft flight time. Credit only approved training/tasks under the device authorization and applicable regulation.

stages.title: Commercial maneuvers and final readiness

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: VFR route management and diversion
steps.instructor: Review the learner’s route, weather, terrain, fuel, performance, airspace, and alternates. In dual lessons demonstrate one prediction-check-correction cycle; later introduce a diversion or lost-position scenario without removing safe navigation options.
steps.student: Depart on the planned course, identify checkpoints, compare groundspeed/fuel with estimates, and update arrival time. Navigate to a selected alternate, use ATC services when useful, and explain the lost-position recovery plan before continuing.
steps.repetitions: Two independent checkpoints, one diversion calculation, and one landing at an appropriately selected destination.
steps.success: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency.
errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.
Late diversion calculation → use a quick heading/time/fuel estimate first, refine after control is stable.
steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; VFR route management and diversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop
steps.instructor: Start with a stable attitude and power setting. Demonstrate attitude change, cross-check of performance, small correction, then trim. Explain which indication confirms each change; let the learner verbalize the scan before removing prompts.
steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 60 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: Two level-offs in each direction and at least two left/right turns; repeat the weakest transition.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.

steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision

errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. On the ground confirm that the pilot can execute it independently.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Night orientation and tower pattern work
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief night equipment, vision limitations, lighting identification, taxi hotspots, terrain, forced-landing options, and fatigue. Before an independent flight agree on airport/tower availability, weather, counts, fuel, and stop conditions; confirm privileges and any needed authorizations. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Fly a conservative night route or pattern as planned, positively identify the runway, comply with tower instructions, and make stabilized approaches and full-stop landings. After each landing reassess fatigue, weather, fuel, and the remaining safe training budget.
steps.repetitions: Plan a defensible number of full-stop patterns based on traffic and aircraft; extend or repeat flights when regulatory counts/hours remain unmet.
steps.success: Maintains orientation, uses lighting deliberately, and chooses go-around or termination before visual illusion or fatigue affects control.
errors: Black-hole approach cues → use a stabilized approach and available visual/electronic guidance.
Counts drive rushed circuits → accept sequencing delays or finish the remaining counts another flight.
steps.stop: End the flight for fatigue, deteriorating visibility, lighting/tower changes affecting the plan, or unstable approaches.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Night orientation and tower pattern work; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Review the return decision on the ground and arrange an overdue plan.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks

errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.

steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: VFR route management and diversion
steps.instructor: Review the learner’s route, weather, terrain, fuel, performance, airspace, and alternates. In dual lessons demonstrate one prediction-check-correction cycle; later introduce a diversion or lost-position scenario without removing safe navigation options.
steps.student: Depart on the planned course, identify checkpoints, compare groundspeed/fuel with estimates, and update arrival time. Navigate to a selected alternate, use ATC services when useful, and explain the lost-position recovery plan before continuing.
steps.repetitions: Two independent checkpoints, one diversion calculation, and one landing at an appropriately selected destination.
steps.success: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency.
errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.
Late diversion calculation → use a quick heading/time/fuel estimate first, refine after control is stable.
steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; VFR route management and diversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends.
steps.student: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.instructor: Before dispatch the instructor reviews the planned route, practice boundaries and return gates; no instructor is carried on a solo flight. For certificated PIC, agree on the actual pilot roles and logging eligibility.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. On the ground confirm that the pilot can execute it independently.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Steep turns with commercial precision
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief attitude, bank/load relationship, entry/exit, clearing, and the current ACS criteria. Demonstrate a smooth entry and coordinated correction; identify whether an altitude trend is caused by pitch, power, or bank before coaching the fix. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Clear the area, establish the approved entry, fly a steep turn in each direction, anticipate rollout, and return to the starting flight condition. Describe and correct the first attempt’s dominant error on the repeat.
steps.repetitions: One left/right pair plus one targeted repeat.
steps.success: Divides attention outside and inside, manages load/energy, and meets current ACS criteria on the independent attempt.
errors: Bank drift masked by pitch correction → correct bank and reassess altitude.
Late rollout → anticipate the exit and return smoothly to straight-and-level.
steps.stop: Recover before envelope, clearance, or altitude margin is threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep turns with commercial precision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief approved configuration, clearing, entry, cues, and recovery priorities. Contrast slow flight with an intentional stall exercise and show how bank/load and coordination change the risk; do not use a source task list as authority for prohibited aircraft maneuvers. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Establish the assigned slow-flight condition, make coordinated turns/climbs/descents, and recover. Conduct approved power-off/power-on stall exercises in the requested attitudes, recognize cues, reduce angle of attack, and restore a controlled flight path.
steps.repetitions: One slow-flight sequence and one power-off/power-on pair; accelerated-stall work only when approved and briefed.
steps.success: Recognizes cues early, manages coordination, and recovers without excessive altitude loss or secondary stall.
errors: Holding altitude after stall warning → reduce angle of attack and follow the approved recovery.
Yaw during entry → correct coordination or terminate before loss of control.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Review the return decision on the ground and arrange an overdue plan.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

debrief: Learner names the strongest result and the first decision/control error.

carryForward: Source task for another focused block if not observed today: Spin Awareness. Select the applicable FAA/aircraft procedure and schedule adequate instruction; no completion is implied by this checklist.

steps.title: VFR route management and diversion
steps.instructor: Review the learner’s route, weather, terrain, fuel, performance, airspace, and alternates. In dual lessons demonstrate one prediction-check-correction cycle; later introduce a diversion or lost-position scenario without removing safe navigation options.
steps.student: Depart on the planned course, identify checkpoints, compare groundspeed/fuel with estimates, and update arrival time. Navigate to a selected alternate, use ATC services when useful, and explain the lost-position recovery plan before continuing.
steps.repetitions: Two independent checkpoints, one diversion calculation, and one landing at an appropriately selected destination.
steps.success: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency.
errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.
Late diversion calculation → use a quick heading/time/fuel estimate first, refine after control is stable.
steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; VFR route management and diversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: High traffic and complex airport operations
steps.instructor: Brief current airport diagrams, hotspots, arrival routes, frequencies, clearances, wake turbulence, and escape options. Dual sessions model concise communication and workload allocation; independent sessions require the pilot to explain a plan for an amended clearance.
steps.student: Obtain required clearances, monitor the traffic/ATC picture, verify runway assignments aloud, and comply with speed/route instructions within aircraft limits. Request clarification, delay, vectors, or go-around whenever the clearance or landing picture is unsafe.
steps.repetitions: One high workload arrival/departure, one amended instruction, and a runway-assignment cross-check.
steps.success: Uses explicit clearances, avoids fixation and runway confusion, and asks for time before capacity is exceeded.
errors: Following traffic without own clearance → verify the actual clearance and runway.
ATC request exceeds capability → respond unable and propose a safe alternative.
steps.stop: Discontinue the planned destination when traffic, winds, runway, or workload prevents safe compliance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; High traffic and complex airport operations; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Instrument route control and avionics
steps.instructor: Establish the approved lookout/control arrangement, instrument training role, and navigation source. During the route teach a reliable attitude scan, course intercept/tracking, clearance-style heading/altitude changes, and one realistic backup-control scenario without compromising actual equipment. This can be legal VFR simulated instrument; actual IFR requires qualified/currency-compliant pilot roles, aircraft, and clearance.
steps.student: Under the agreed actual or simulated instrument conditions, control attitude/airspeed/altitude, intercept and track the route, verify GPS/VOR sources and sequencing, manage amended headings/altitudes, then recover a briefed backup-control scenario. Remove the view-limiting device for arrivals/traffic when required by the safety arrangement. Plan 150 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: Sustain the published instrument subset across the route segment; include two course intercepts, two level-offs, one source change, and one approved backup-control review.
steps.success: Remains ahead of route and weather, keeps reserves and terrain/airspace protection, and communicates changes promptly.
errors: Continuing toward deteriorating weather → identify the last safe alternate and decide before reaching it.
Clearance lost in the flight plan → compare active route against the actual amended clearance.
steps.stop: Real weather, aircraft capability, or fuel margin controls the route; terminate a training scenario before it reduces safe options.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Instrument route control and avionics; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.

errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.

steps.title: Device setup and clearance review
steps.instructor: Verify the device configuration, intended training credit, database and weather scenario. Set failures only by the approved device method; state whether pauses are instruction or evaluation.
steps.student: Set up the cockpit as in the aircraft, verify navigation sources, copy the starting clearance, and explain today’s equipment/failure and approach plans.
steps.repetitions: One complete setup and clearance readback.
steps.success: Can explain the actual simulated aircraft/equipment state before the scenario runs.
errors: Unverified setup → compare the device state with the intended aircraft/manual.
steps.stop: Do not log unapproved credit or continue with an invalid configuration.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Complex/TAA configuration and energy control
steps.instructor: Brief the installed gear/propeller or TAA systems, limitations, checklists, engine management, and cockpit flows. Demonstrate a configuration change with positive verification, then require checklist confirmation; TAA experience alone does not create a complex-airplane endorsement.
steps.student: Manage start, departure, climb, cruise, descent, and landing configurations using the approved checklist. Announce configuration and engine limits before changes, verify the result, and manage energy so the approach is stable before the landing decision.
steps.repetitions: One full configuration cycle plus two landing transitions; repeat the weakest checklist or energy-management step.
steps.success: Uses the correct aircraft procedure, verifies configuration, respects limits, and avoids rushed or ambiguous cockpit actions.
errors: Flow without verification → use the checklist to confirm actual system state.
Late energy management → plan descent/configuration sooner or go around.
steps.stop: End the simulation for a real system warning or unresolved configuration; use approved procedures and land as appropriate.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Complex/TAA configuration and energy control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: GPS setup, sequencing, and integrity
steps.instructor: Use the installed navigator manual to show source selection, flight-plan loading, leg activation, direct-to, nearest, and scaling changes. Explain integrity alerts and how WAAS/RAIM availability affects a planned procedure; confirm the next mode before changing it.
steps.student: Load and verify a short route, intercept an active leg, observe waypoint sequencing, accept a reroute with direct-to, then choose an appropriate nearest alternate. State navigation source, active leg, scaling, and response to an integrity alert.
steps.repetitions: One complete route plus one reroute and one integrity/failure decision.
steps.success: Verifies every clearance and active leg, understands available guidance, and preserves control while programming.
errors: Wrong leg activated → compare clearance, map, flight-plan list, and CDI before executing.
Heads-down programming → stabilize first; ask for delay or use a simpler navigation method.
steps.stop: Stop programming for control/traffic priorities; discontinue approach guidance when integrity or required equipment is unavailable.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; GPS setup, sequencing, and integrity; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.student: Complete the simulated shutdown/checklist, describe the main error and correction, and identify the remaining practice task.
steps.repetitions: One complete scenario wrap-up.
steps.success: Ends with an accurate account of what was practiced and what remains.
errors: Treating paused time as flight → record only credit permitted by the device authorization.
steps.stop: End before fatigue makes further practice ineffective.

steps.student: Independently: Establish the assigned slow-flight condition, make coordinated turns/climbs/descents, and recover. Conduct approved power-off/power-on stall exercises in the requested attitudes, recognize cues, reduce angle of attack, and restore a controlled flight path.
steps.repetitions: One slow-flight sequence and one power-off/power-on pair; accelerated-stall work only when approved and briefed.
steps.success: Recognizes cues early, manages coordination, and recovers without excessive altitude loss or secondary stall.
errors: Holding altitude after stall warning → reduce angle of attack and follow the approved recovery.
Yaw during entry → correct coordination or terminate before loss of control.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Review the return decision on the ground and arrange an overdue plan.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.repetitions: One complete setup and clearance readback.
steps.success: Can explain the actual simulated aircraft/equipment state before the scenario runs.
errors: Unverified setup → compare the device state with the intended aircraft/manual.

steps.title: GPS setup, sequencing, and integrity
steps.instructor: Use the installed navigator manual to show source selection, flight-plan loading, leg activation, direct-to, nearest, and scaling changes. Explain integrity alerts and how WAAS/RAIM availability affects a planned procedure; confirm the next mode before changing it.
steps.student: Load and verify a short route, intercept an active leg, observe waypoint sequencing, accept a reroute with direct-to, then choose an appropriate nearest alternate. State navigation source, active leg, scaling, and response to an integrity alert.
steps.repetitions: One complete route plus one reroute and one integrity/failure decision.
steps.success: Verifies every clearance and active leg, understands available guidance, and preserves control while programming.
errors: Wrong leg activated → compare clearance, map, flight-plan list, and CDI before executing.
Heads-down programming → stabilize first; ask for delay or use a simpler navigation method.
steps.stop: Stop programming for control/traffic priorities; discontinue approach guidance when integrity or required equipment is unavailable.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; GPS setup, sequencing, and integrity; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: IFR route, weather, and contingency decisions
steps.instructor: Build an actual route with current weather, NOTAMs, alternates, fuel, departure/arrival restrictions, and approach options. In flight present one credible weather or routing change and require a decision supported by fuel and aircraft capability; rehearse lost communications without stopping real radio use.
steps.student: File the plan when appropriate, verify the clearance, fly the route and altitude restrictions, and update ETA/fuel/weather at each leg. Select an alternate before the escape option disappears; explain the applicable lost-communications response and request assistance while communications work.
steps.repetitions: At least two route checkpoints, one changed-clearance readback, one diversion decision, and approaches at planned destinations.
steps.success: Remains ahead of route and weather, keeps reserves and terrain/airspace protection, and communicates changes promptly.
errors: Continuing toward deteriorating weather → identify the last safe alternate and decide before reaching it.
Clearance lost in the flight plan → compare active route against the actual amended clearance.
steps.stop: Real weather, aircraft capability, or fuel margin controls the route; terminate a training scenario before it reduces safe options.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; IFR route, weather, and contingency decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction
steps.instructor: Have the learner read back and sketch the clearance, fix, course, direction, restriction, and expect-further-clearance information. Demonstrate fix-crossing flow and one entry; explain that the chosen entry must remain within protected airspace.
steps.student: Copy and verify the clearance, select a defensible entry, cross the fix, establish the hold, and adjust outbound timing/distance and heading for wind. Communicate any inability and track clearance limits.
steps.repetitions: Two entries from different arrival directions and two complete circuits; one timed and one distance-based hold when available.
steps.success: Remains within the protected procedure, meets altitude/speed constraints, and corrects timing without losing control.
errors: Entry guessed from a moving display → orient the published inbound course and aircraft arrival direction before choosing.
Timing starts at the wrong place → identify the published timing convention and fix crossing.
steps.stop: Request clarification or vectors before reaching an unclear limit; abandon exercise for unsafe control or containment.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report.
steps.repetitions: One complete approach and one vectored approach; at least one missed approach.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.
Early descent after a shortcut → verify the cleared segment and remaining altitude restrictions.
steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: ILS and approved vertical guidance
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent.
steps.repetitions: Two approaches with different guidance where available: one landing transition and one missed approach.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Secure device and verify results
steps.instructor: Stop the scenario after a stable endpoint, review objective evidence, and distinguish simulated/device time from aircraft or airborne time.
steps.student: Complete the simulated shutdown/checklist, describe the main error and correction, and identify the remaining practice task.
steps.repetitions: One complete scenario wrap-up.
steps.success: Ends with an accurate account of what was practiced and what remains.
errors: Treating paused time as flight → record only credit permitted by the device authorization.
steps.stop: End before fatigue makes further practice ineffective.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.success: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency.
errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.

steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; VFR route management and diversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.success: Uses explicit clearances, avoids fixation and runway confusion, and asks for time before capacity is exceeded.
errors: Following traffic without own clearance → verify the actual clearance and runway.
ATC request exceeds capability → respond unable and propose a safe alternative.
steps.stop: Discontinue the planned destination when traffic, winds, runway, or workload prevents safe compliance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; High traffic and complex airport operations; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.

steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. On the ground confirm that the pilot can execute it independently.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: VFR route management and diversion
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Review the learner’s route, weather, terrain, fuel, performance, airspace, and alternates. In dual lessons demonstrate one prediction-check-correction cycle; later introduce a diversion or lost-position scenario without removing safe navigation options. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Depart on the planned course, identify checkpoints, compare groundspeed/fuel with estimates, and update arrival time. Navigate to a selected alternate, use ATC services when useful, and explain the lost-position recovery plan before continuing.
steps.repetitions: Two independent checkpoints, one diversion calculation, and one landing at an appropriately selected destination.
steps.success: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency.
errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.
Late diversion calculation → use a quick heading/time/fuel estimate first, refine after control is stable.
steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; VFR route management and diversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Performance-limited destination decisions
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Use actual weight, density altitude, runway surface/slope, obstacles, winds, and POH data to compare destination options. Brief terrain escape routes, turbulence, and turnaround/abort gates. The objective is a sound decision, including declining the landing. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Recalculate performance before committing to the destination, identify terrain and wind cues, select a safe approach/departure path, and retain an alternate. Fly only approved short/soft-field procedures with adequate calculated margins.
steps.repetitions: One arrival/departure decision and one alternative-airport decision; repeat performance calculations after a changed condition.
steps.success: Supports go/no-go decisions with current conditions and usable aircraft data, preserving terrain and runway margins.
errors: Sea-level habit applied at altitude → recalculate and use the actual aircraft procedure.
Destination commitment bias → compare the alternate before commencing the approach.
steps.stop: Reject takeoff or divert if required performance/terrain margins cannot be established.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Performance-limited destination decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Review the return decision on the ground and arrange an overdue plan.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.instructor: Build an actual route with current weather, NOTAMs, alternates, fuel, departure/arrival restrictions, and approach options. steps.student: File the plan when appropriate, verify the clearance, fly the route and altitude restrictions, and update ETA/fuel/weather at each leg.
