steps.success: Remains ahead of route and weather, keeps reserves and terrain/airspace protection, and communicates changes promptly.
errors: Continuing toward deteriorating weather → identify the last safe alternate and decide before reaching it.
Clearance lost in the flight plan → compare active route against the actual amended clearance.
steps.stop: Real weather, aircraft capability, or fuel margin controls the route; terminate a training scenario before it reduces safe options.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; IFR route, weather, and contingency decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: High traffic and complex airport operations
steps.instructor: Brief current airport diagrams, hotspots, arrival routes, frequencies, clearances, wake turbulence, and escape options. Dual sessions model concise communication and workload allocation; independent sessions require the pilot to explain a plan for an amended clearance.
steps.student: Obtain required clearances, monitor the traffic/ATC picture, verify runway assignments aloud, and comply with speed/route instructions within aircraft limits. Request clarification, delay, vectors, or go-around whenever the clearance or landing picture is unsafe.
steps.repetitions: One high workload arrival/departure, one amended instruction, and a runway-assignment cross-check.
steps.success: Uses explicit clearances, avoids fixation and runway confusion, and asks for time before capacity is exceeded.
errors: Following traffic without own clearance → verify the actual clearance and runway.
ATC request exceeds capability → respond unable and propose a safe alternative.
steps.stop: Discontinue the planned destination when traffic, winds, runway, or workload prevents safe compliance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; High traffic and complex airport operations; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report. Plan 48 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: One complete approach and one vectored approach; at least one missed approach.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.
Early descent after a shortcut → verify the cleared segment and remaining altitude restrictions.
steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: ILS and approved vertical guidance
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent. Plan 7 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: Two approaches with different guidance where available: one landing transition and one missed approach.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Device setup and clearance review
steps.instructor: Verify the device configuration, intended training credit, database and weather scenario. Set failures only by the approved device method; state whether pauses are instruction or evaluation.
steps.student: Set up the cockpit as in the aircraft, verify navigation sources, copy the starting clearance, and explain today’s equipment/failure and approach plans.
steps.repetitions: One complete setup and clearance readback.
steps.success: Can explain the actual simulated aircraft/equipment state before the scenario runs.
errors: Unverified setup → compare the device state with the intended aircraft/manual.
steps.stop: Do not log unapproved credit or continue with an invalid configuration.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Autopilot modes and manual reversion
steps.instructor: Brief the approved engagement envelope, limitations, disconnect methods, and failure signs. Demonstrate each installed mode by stating what is armed, active, commanded, and actually happening; then disconnect and hand-fly the same segment.
steps.student: Select heading, navigation, altitude, and permitted climb/descent modes. Confirm annunciations and resulting flight path after every change. Recover from a simulated wrong mode or failed automation using the approved disconnect and manual control.
steps.repetitions: One mode sequence, one capture verification, and two different disconnect/reversion methods if installed.
steps.success: Monitors rather than assumes automation behavior; disconnects early when it no longer supports the plan.
errors: Armed mistaken for active → point to annunciations and confirm actual capture.
Fighting engaged servos → use the approved disconnect and stabilize manually.
steps.stop: Disengage for unexpected flight path, unresolved mode confusion, or operation outside approved limitations.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Autopilot modes and manual reversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Failure recognition and backup control
steps.instructor: Brief a realistic failure supported by the aircraft or device. Reveal its indications, require independent confirmation, then demonstrate the remaining scan. Never disable equipment that compromises the actual flight or required equipment.
steps.student: Identify the simulated failed instrument, cross-check its reliability, establish control with valid indications, and use backup attitude/heading resources. Make timed turns and compass-supported turns with appropriate acceleration/dip error awareness.
steps.repetitions: Two different failures and one heading change each direction; device sessions may freeze only after the attempt for explanation.
steps.success: Rejects misleading data, controls the aircraft with valid sources, and communicates the degraded capability.
errors: Following a failed display → cross-check independent indications and isolate the bad source.
Treating compass as steady during a maneuver → stabilize before reading and use timed/backup methods as appropriate.
steps.stop: End the simulation for loss of orientation, unsafe deviations, unavailable reliable backup, or real equipment abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Failure recognition and backup control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options
steps.instructor: State the simulation method, instructor takeover gates, and any prohibited control actions. Teach aviate, diagnose, appropriate immediate actions, approved checklist, communication, and landing choice. Practice recognition and judgment without creating the actual failure.
steps.student: Identify a simulated abnormality from valid indications, control the aircraft, apply aircraft-approved actions, use the checklist, and select a suitable landing/alternate. For a simulated forced landing, establish the approved glide profile and plan a reachable field; terminate at the briefed gate.
steps.repetitions: One systems problem and one descent/forced-landing decision; one checklist recovery after the first response.
steps.success: Maintains control, avoids premature diagnosis, and chooses a landing plan supported by terrain, wind, and aircraft capability.
errors: Checklist before control → stabilize and manage the immediate hazard first.
Field selected without reachability → compare glide/terrain/wind and choose a viable alternative early.
steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report.
steps.repetitions: One complete approach and one vectored approach; at least one missed approach.
steps.success: Maintains lateral guidance and altitude restrictions, applies the correct minima, and promptly flies a missed approach when required.
errors: Advisory glidepath treated as authorization below MDA → use the selected chart minima and required visual conditions.
Early descent after a shortcut → verify the cleared segment and remaining altitude restrictions.
steps.stop: Go missed when required by the clearance/procedure, guidance loss, unstable approach, or unmet landing conditions.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lateral approach and missed approach; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: ILS and approved vertical guidance
steps.instructor: Contrast ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV guidance, minima, equipment requirements, and failure responses. LP provides lateral guidance only; it is not an APV. For test credit, consult current ACS conditions for the selected LPV procedure rather than labeling every LPV a precision approach.
steps.student: Brief an ILS or approved vertically guided procedure, verify the active navigation source and annunciation, intercept as cleared, establish a stabilized configuration, and follow lateral/vertical guidance to the selected DA. Execute a missed approach when the required visual conditions are absent.
steps.repetitions: Two approaches with different guidance where available: one landing transition and one missed approach.
steps.success: Uses the correct source, minima, and annunciations, stabilizes early, and makes a timely decision at DA.
errors: Wrong CDI source → verify the source before intercept and compare with the chart.
Below-path correction by steep descent → recover a stable path or go missed; do not chase near the ground.
steps.stop: Go missed for lost required guidance, instability, unavailable visual conditions, or an instruction requiring it.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; ILS and approved vertical guidance; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Secure device and verify results
steps.instructor: Stop the scenario after a stable endpoint, review objective evidence, and distinguish simulated/device time from aircraft or airborne time.
steps.student: Complete the simulated shutdown/checklist, describe the main error and correction, and identify the remaining practice task.
steps.repetitions: One complete scenario wrap-up.
steps.success: Ends with an accurate account of what was practiced and what remains.
errors: Treating paused time as flight → record only credit permitted by the device authorization.
steps.stop: End before fatigue makes further practice ineffective.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Do not assume the source’s international exercise is a Part 61 certificate requirement. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Conduct the approved international route with proper documents and permissions, verify boundary/reporting requirements, manage fuel and weather, and complete arrival/return procedures. steps.success: No departure with unresolved entry/return requirements; route and fuel decisions remain independent of the training schedule.
errors: Old checklist assumed current → verify official requirements for the actual date and traveler.
Paperwork done during a critical phase → complete it before departure or stabilize and delegate appropriately.
steps.stop: Do not launch across a border until applicable permissions, documents, and safe return arrangements are confirmed.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; International route and border preparation; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.

steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Assess the learner’s departure, configuration, and course intercept independently; give no coaching during the check.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: VFR route management and diversion
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed vfr route management and diversion scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Depart on the planned course, identify checkpoints, compare groundspeed/fuel with estimates, and update arrival time. Navigate to a selected alternate, use ATC services when useful, and explain the lost-position recovery plan before continuing.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency.
errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.
Late diversion calculation → use a quick heading/time/fuel estimate first, refine after control is stable.
steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; VFR route management and diversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Performance-limited destination decisions
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed performance-limited destination decisions scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Supports go/no-go decisions with current conditions and usable aircraft data, preserving terrain and runway margins. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Recalculate performance before committing to the destination, identify terrain and wind cues, select a safe approach/departure path, and retain an alternate. Fly only approved short/soft-field procedures with adequate calculated margins.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Supports go/no-go decisions with current conditions and usable aircraft data, preserving terrain and runway margins.
errors: Sea-level habit applied at altitude → recalculate and use the actual aircraft procedure.
Destination commitment bias → compare the alternate before commencing the approach.
steps.stop: Reject takeoff or divert if required performance/terrain margins cannot be established.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Performance-limited destination decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.

steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.

steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop

Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.

Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.

steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.

errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.

steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Build the scan and trim loop; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

errors: Treating paused time as flight → record only credit permitted by the device authorization.

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept

steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.

steps.title: Complex/TAA configuration and energy control
steps.instructor: Brief the installed gear/propeller or TAA systems, limitations, checklists, engine management, and cockpit flows. Demonstrate a configuration change with positive verification, then require checklist confirmation; TAA experience alone does not create a complex-airplane endorsement.
steps.student: Manage start, departure, climb, cruise, descent, and landing configurations using the approved checklist. Announce configuration and engine limits before changes, verify the result, and manage energy so the approach is stable before the landing decision.
steps.repetitions: One full configuration cycle plus two landing transitions; repeat the weakest checklist or energy-management step.
steps.success: Uses the correct aircraft procedure, verifies configuration, respects limits, and avoids rushed or ambiguous cockpit actions.
errors: Flow without verification → use the checklist to confirm actual system state.
Late energy management → plan descent/configuration sooner or go around.
steps.stop: End the simulation for a real system warning or unresolved configuration; use approved procedures and land as appropriate.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Complex/TAA configuration and energy control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends.
steps.student: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop
steps.instructor: Start with a stable attitude and power setting. Demonstrate attitude change, cross-check of performance, small correction, then trim. Explain which indication confirms each change; let the learner verbalize the scan before removing prompts.
steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: Two level-offs in each direction and at least two left/right turns; repeat the weakest transition.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Build the scan and trim loop; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision

steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.

steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

errors: Control response before diagnosis → identify the attitude using reliable cues first.

steps.stop: Instructor ends setup or takes control before aircraft limits, safety altitude, or recovery margin are threatened.

errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Complex/TAA configuration and energy control
steps.instructor: Brief the installed gear/propeller or TAA systems, limitations, checklists, engine management, and cockpit flows. Demonstrate a configuration change with positive verification, then require checklist confirmation; TAA experience alone does not create a complex-airplane endorsement.
steps.student: Manage start, departure, climb, cruise, descent, and landing configurations using the approved checklist. Announce configuration and engine limits before changes, verify the result, and manage energy so the approach is stable before the landing decision.
steps.repetitions: One full configuration cycle plus two landing transitions; repeat the weakest checklist or energy-management step.
steps.success: Uses the correct aircraft procedure, verifies configuration, respects limits, and avoids rushed or ambiguous cockpit actions.
errors: Flow without verification → use the checklist to confirm actual system state.
Late energy management → plan descent/configuration sooner or go around.
steps.stop: End the simulation for a real system warning or unresolved configuration; use approved procedures and land as appropriate.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Complex/TAA configuration and energy control; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends.
steps.student: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options
steps.instructor: State the simulation method, instructor takeover gates, and any prohibited control actions. Teach aviate, diagnose, appropriate immediate actions, approved checklist, communication, and landing choice. Practice recognition and judgment without creating the actual failure.
steps.student: Identify a simulated abnormality from valid indications, control the aircraft, apply aircraft-approved actions, use the checklist, and select a suitable landing/alternate. For a simulated forced landing, establish the approved glide profile and plan a reachable field; terminate at the briefed gate.
steps.repetitions: One systems problem and one descent/forced-landing decision; one checklist recovery after the first response.
steps.success: Maintains control, avoids premature diagnosis, and chooses a landing plan supported by terrain, wind, and aircraft capability.
errors: Checklist before control → stabilize and manage the immediate hazard first.
Field selected without reachability → compare glide/terrain/wind and choose a viable alternative early.
steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop
steps.instructor: Start with a stable attitude and power setting. Demonstrate attitude change, cross-check of performance, small correction, then trim. Explain which indication confirms each change; let the learner verbalize the scan before removing prompts.
steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: Two level-offs in each direction and at least two left/right turns; repeat the weakest transition.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Build the scan and trim loop; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.repetitions: One complete setup and clearance readback.

errors: Unverified setup → compare the device state with the intended aircraft/manual.

steps.title: Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction
steps.instructor: Have the learner read back and sketch the clearance, fix, course, direction, restriction, and expect-further-clearance information. Demonstrate fix-crossing flow and one entry; explain that the chosen entry must remain within protected airspace.
steps.student: Copy and verify the clearance, select a defensible entry, cross the fix, establish the hold, and adjust outbound timing/distance and heading for wind. Communicate any inability and track clearance limits.
steps.repetitions: Two entries from different arrival directions and two complete circuits; one timed and one distance-based hold when available.
steps.success: Remains within the protected procedure, meets altitude/speed constraints, and corrects timing without losing control.
errors: Entry guessed from a moving display → orient the published inbound course and aircraft arrival direction before choosing.
Timing starts at the wrong place → identify the published timing convention and fix crossing.
steps.stop: Request clarification or vectors before reaching an unclear limit; abandon exercise for unsafe control or containment.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Clearance, holding entry, and wind correction; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lateral approach and missed approach
steps.instructor: Brief procedure eligibility, source, course, altitudes, MDA, missed point, visual requirements, and missed route. Demonstrate a stabilized descent using approved advisory vertical guidance only as advisory; distinguish LNAV/LP from vertically guided minima.
steps.student: Load or tune and identify the procedure, brief it, fly the cleared entry, meet restrictions, descend to the published MDA, and hold it until a legal landing or missed approach. At the missed point, execute the aircraft procedure, navigation sequence, and ATC report.
steps.repetitions: One complete approach and one vectored approach; at least one missed approach.

steps.instructor: Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends.

errors: Checklist before control → stabilize and manage the immediate hazard first.

steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

errors: Control response before diagnosis → identify the attitude using reliable cues first.

steps.stop: Instructor ends setup or takes control before aircraft limits, safety altitude, or recovery margin are threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Recognize and recover unusual attitudes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.success: Keeps an accurate position/fuel picture and revises the plan before uncertainty becomes an emergency.
errors: Only looking at the moving map → cross-check terrain, chart, course, and fuel.
Late diversion calculation → use a quick heading/time/fuel estimate first, refine after control is stable.
steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; VFR route management and diversion; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed takeoff, landing, and go-around technique scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed abnormal systems, descent, and landing options scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Maintains control, avoids premature diagnosis, and chooses a landing plan supported by terrain, wind, and aircraft capability. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Identify a simulated abnormality from valid indications, control the aircraft, apply aircraft-approved actions, use the checklist, and select a suitable landing/alternate. For a simulated forced landing, establish the approved glide profile and plan a reachable field; terminate at the briefed gate.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Maintains control, avoids premature diagnosis, and chooses a landing plan supported by terrain, wind, and aircraft capability.
errors: Checklist before control → stabilize and manage the immediate hazard first.
Field selected without reachability → compare glide/terrain/wind and choose a viable alternative early.
steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed build the scan and trim loop scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Build the scan and trim loop; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks

steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.

steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept

steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade
steps.instructor: Sketch the maneuver’s changing bank/pitch/airspeed relationships. Demonstrate one direction, narrating the transition from the first half to the second and the coordinated rollout; use aircraft-approved entry parameters.
steps.student: Clear the area, enter at approved parameters, establish the climbing turn, manage the changing pitch and bank through the maneuver, and finish coordinated at the required heading and low-airspeed condition without a stall.
steps.repetitions: One each direction plus one repeat focused on the first/second-half transition.
steps.success: Uses a continuous coordinated energy trade and achieves the current ACS completion condition without abrupt corrections.
errors: Pitch/bank schedule rushed → identify the transition points and let airspeed trend develop.
Yaw near completion → prioritize coordination as airspeed decreases.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for stall cues, loss of coordination, or inadequate altitude/clearance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Steep spiral and glide planning
steps.instructor: Select a suitable reference with a safe altitude margin and explain how wind changes the bank/ground track. Brief approved glide/engine-management procedures and recovery gate; keep the simulated glide from becoming an actual emergency.
steps.student: Clear the area, establish the appropriate glide configuration and speed, turn around the reference with wind-adjusted bank, maintain coordination, and recover at the briefed gate on a selected heading.
steps.repetitions: One complete spiral within the available safe altitude; repeat one wind quadrant if needed.
steps.success: Maintains glide and reference spacing while respecting bank/load and recovery margins.
errors: Bank increased to fix poor reference choice → choose geometry that fits safe bank and altitude limits.
Airspeed neglected while watching the ground → cross-check glide performance throughout.
steps.stop: Recover at the prebriefed gate, before excessive bank/airspeed or insufficient terrain clearance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep spiral and glide planning; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery
steps.instructor: Brief approved configuration, clearing, entry, cues, and recovery priorities. Contrast slow flight with an intentional stall exercise and show how bank/load and coordination change the risk; do not use a source task list as authority for prohibited aircraft maneuvers.
steps.student: Establish the assigned slow-flight condition, make coordinated turns/climbs/descents, and recover. Conduct approved power-off/power-on stall exercises in the requested attitudes, recognize cues, reduce angle of attack, and restore a controlled flight path.
steps.repetitions: One slow-flight sequence and one power-off/power-on pair; accelerated-stall work only when approved and briefed.
steps.success: Recognizes cues early, manages coordination, and recovers without excessive altitude loss or secondary stall.
errors: Holding altitude after stall warning → reduce angle of attack and follow the approved recovery.
Yaw during entry → correct coordination or terminate before loss of control.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Steep turns with commercial precision
steps.instructor: Brief attitude, bank/load relationship, entry/exit, clearing, and the current ACS criteria. Demonstrate a smooth entry and coordinated correction; identify whether an altitude trend is caused by pitch, power, or bank before coaching the fix.
steps.student: Clear the area, establish the approved entry, fly a steep turn in each direction, anticipate rollout, and return to the starting flight condition. Describe and correct the first attempt’s dominant error on the repeat.
steps.repetitions: One left/right pair plus one targeted repeat.
steps.success: Divides attention outside and inside, manages load/energy, and meets current ACS criteria on the independent attempt.
errors: Bank drift masked by pitch correction → correct bank and reassess altitude.
Late rollout → anticipate the exit and return smoothly to straight-and-level.
steps.stop: Recover before envelope, clearance, or altitude margin is threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep turns with commercial precision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.

steps.title: Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness
steps.instructor: Brief the relationship among groundspeed, pivotal altitude, wind, suitable pylons, and safe terrain clearance. Demonstrate one pylon turn, explaining why pitch rather than rudder is used to maintain the sight line; use current FAA/aircraft guidance for entry.
steps.student: Select safe pylons, determine an appropriate entry and pivotal-altitude estimate, clear the area, and fly linked turns while adjusting altitude for changing groundspeed. Maintain coordination and abandon unsuitable geometry.
steps.repetitions: Two complete eights; repeat the downwind/upwind transition with the largest sight-line error.
steps.success: Keeps the pylon on the selected sight line using appropriate pitch changes without unsafe bank or clearance loss.
errors: Rudder used to hold the pylon → restore coordination and adjust pitch/altitude appropriately.
Pylons chosen too close or hazardous → discontinue and select a safe pair.
steps.stop: Exit when terrain/obstacles, bank, coordination, or aircraft limits cannot be maintained.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Power-off accuracy landing decisions
steps.instructor: Brief the selected landing exercise, touchdown area, wind, runway, approved configurations, and go-around gates. Demonstrate energy judgment and allowable slips/configuration changes. Separate the commercial ACS power-off 180 task from optional 90/360-degree source exercises.
steps.student: From the agreed position reduce power using the approved simulation, assess glide/wind, choose turn points and configuration deliberately, and aim for the selected touchdown area. Go around when a safe outcome is doubtful rather than forcing the target.
steps.repetitions: Two power-off 180 attempts if suitable; 90/360-degree planning rehearsed on the ground or added only with time, approval, and a safe traffic plan.
steps.success: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around.
errors: Stretching glide with pitch → preserve the approved glide condition and change the landing plan.
Late flap/slip correction near touchdown → improve the earlier energy decision or go around.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable geometry, unsafe bank, traffic, or insufficient runway; do not force the touchdown mark.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Power-off accuracy landing decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends.
steps.student: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

lessons.title: Performance maneuver integration

objectives: Divides attention outside and inside, manages load/energy, and meets current ACS criteria on the independent attempt.
Uses a continuous coordinated energy trade and achieves the current ACS completion condition without abrupt corrections.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Steep turns with commercial precision
steps.instructor: Brief attitude, bank/load relationship, entry/exit, clearing, and the current ACS criteria. Demonstrate a smooth entry and coordinated correction; identify whether an altitude trend is caused by pitch, power, or bank before coaching the fix.
steps.student: Clear the area, establish the approved entry, fly a steep turn in each direction, anticipate rollout, and return to the starting flight condition. Describe and correct the first attempt’s dominant error on the repeat.
steps.repetitions: One left/right pair plus one targeted repeat.
steps.success: Divides attention outside and inside, manages load/energy, and meets current ACS criteria on the independent attempt.
errors: Bank drift masked by pitch correction → correct bank and reassess altitude.
Late rollout → anticipate the exit and return smoothly to straight-and-level.
steps.stop: Recover before envelope, clearance, or altitude margin is threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep turns with commercial precision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade
steps.instructor: Sketch the maneuver’s changing bank/pitch/airspeed relationships. Demonstrate one direction, narrating the transition from the first half to the second and the coordinated rollout; use aircraft-approved entry parameters.
steps.student: Clear the area, enter at approved parameters, establish the climbing turn, manage the changing pitch and bank through the maneuver, and finish coordinated at the required heading and low-airspeed condition without a stall.
steps.repetitions: One each direction plus one repeat focused on the first/second-half transition.
steps.success: Uses a continuous coordinated energy trade and achieves the current ACS completion condition without abrupt corrections.
errors: Pitch/bank schedule rushed → identify the transition points and let airspeed trend develop.
Yaw near completion → prioritize coordination as airspeed decreases.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for stall cues, loss of coordination, or inadequate altitude/clearance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes
steps.instructor: Use ground reference directions to show the sequence and pitch/bank/airspeed trends. Demonstrate smooth control pressure and balanced segments, emphasizing anticipation rather than fixed control positions.
steps.student: Clear the area and fly linked left/right segments through the maneuver’s reference points. Observe the changing attitude/airspeed, coordinate the turns, and compare the second half with the first before repeating.
steps.repetitions: Two full left/right cycles; repeat the quarter where timing or coordination broke down.
steps.success: Maintains a smooth continuous maneuver, balanced segments, and current ACS criteria with useful outside references.
errors: Maneuver becomes two abrupt turns → smooth the control changes across reference points.
Reference fixation → distribute attention among horizon, references, coordination, and performance.
steps.stop: Stop for stall cues, disorientation, or a threatened aircraft/safety limit.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery
steps.instructor: Brief approved configuration, clearing, entry, cues, and recovery priorities. Contrast slow flight with an intentional stall exercise and show how bank/load and coordination change the risk; do not use a source task list as authority for prohibited aircraft maneuvers.
steps.student: Establish the assigned slow-flight condition, make coordinated turns/climbs/descents, and recover. Conduct approved power-off/power-on stall exercises in the requested attitudes, recognize cues, reduce angle of attack, and restore a controlled flight path.
steps.repetitions: One slow-flight sequence and one power-off/power-on pair; accelerated-stall work only when approved and briefed.
steps.success: Recognizes cues early, manages coordination, and recovers without excessive altitude loss or secondary stall.
errors: Holding altitude after stall warning → reduce angle of attack and follow the approved recovery.
Yaw during entry → correct coordination or terminate before loss of control.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Secondary and configuration-related stall risk
steps.instructor: Explain how trim, distraction, go-around power, or inappropriate rudder can raise angle of attack or upset coordination. Demonstrate only aircraft-approved scenarios at a safe altitude; cross-controlled and falling-leaf source items are discussion/device substitutes when aircraft approval or risk margin is absent. Spin awareness is recognition/avoidance, not an intentional spin authorization.
steps.student: Describe the causal chain, rehearse the correct go-around/trim response, and recover from approved simulated stall-risk scenarios. Distinguish a stall/spin risk from a diving spiral and explain prevention before another attempt.
steps.repetitions: Two selected approved risk scenarios plus a verbal spin-avoidance and spiral-recovery comparison.
steps.success: Recognizes the risk before control loss and prioritizes angle of attack, coordination, and approved configuration recovery.
errors: Aggressive pull after recovery → avoid a secondary stall and stabilize before returning to altitude.
Power/trim surprise on go-around → apply the approved sequence with deliberate pitch and trim control.
steps.stop: No intentional spins or nonapproved demonstrations; terminate for yaw/roll departure or reduced recovery margin.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Secondary and configuration-related stall risk; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Recognize and recover unusual attitudes
steps.instructor: Brief transfer of control and the approved recovery procedure. Present modest, realistic unusual attitudes within aircraft limitations; demonstrate how reliable indications distinguish nose-high, nose-low, spiral, and failed-display situations.
steps.student: Diagnose the attitude from reliable indications, use the aircraft-appropriate recovery priorities, stabilize attitude/power/airspeed, and explain how fixation or automation confusion caused the upset. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: One nose-high and one nose-low recovery; repeat using the briefed reduced instrument set if the source lesson calls for it.
steps.success: Recognizes the condition, promptly reduces the immediate risk, avoids secondary loss of control, and re-establishes a useful scan.
errors: Control response before diagnosis → identify the attitude using reliable cues first.
Recovery creates a secondary stall/overspeed → manage angle of attack, bank, power, and load according to the approved procedure.
steps.stop: Instructor ends setup or takes control before aircraft limits, safety altitude, or recovery margin are threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Recognize and recover unusual attitudes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Steep turns with commercial precision
steps.instructor: Brief attitude, bank/load relationship, entry/exit, clearing, and the current ACS criteria. Demonstrate a smooth entry and coordinated correction; identify whether an altitude trend is caused by pitch, power, or bank before coaching the fix.
steps.student: Clear the area, establish the approved entry, fly a steep turn in each direction, anticipate rollout, and return to the starting flight condition. Describe and correct the first attempt’s dominant error on the repeat.
steps.repetitions: One left/right pair plus one targeted repeat.
steps.success: Divides attention outside and inside, manages load/energy, and meets current ACS criteria on the independent attempt.
errors: Bank drift masked by pitch correction → correct bank and reassess altitude.
Late rollout → anticipate the exit and return smoothly to straight-and-level.
steps.stop: Recover before envelope, clearance, or altitude margin is threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep turns with commercial precision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade
steps.instructor: Sketch the maneuver’s changing bank/pitch/airspeed relationships. Demonstrate one direction, narrating the transition from the first half to the second and the coordinated rollout; use aircraft-approved entry parameters.
steps.student: Clear the area, enter at approved parameters, establish the climbing turn, manage the changing pitch and bank through the maneuver, and finish coordinated at the required heading and low-airspeed condition without a stall.
steps.repetitions: One each direction plus one repeat focused on the first/second-half transition.
steps.success: Uses a continuous coordinated energy trade and achieves the current ACS completion condition without abrupt corrections.
errors: Pitch/bank schedule rushed → identify the transition points and let airspeed trend develop.
Yaw near completion → prioritize coordination as airspeed decreases.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for stall cues, loss of coordination, or inadequate altitude/clearance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Power-off accuracy landing decisions
steps.instructor: Brief the selected landing exercise, touchdown area, wind, runway, approved configurations, and go-around gates. Demonstrate energy judgment and allowable slips/configuration changes. Separate the commercial ACS power-off 180 task from optional 90/360-degree source exercises.
steps.student: From the agreed position reduce power using the approved simulation, assess glide/wind, choose turn points and configuration deliberately, and aim for the selected touchdown area. Go around when a safe outcome is doubtful rather than forcing the target.
steps.repetitions: Two power-off 180 attempts if suitable; 90/360-degree planning rehearsed on the ground or added only with time, approval, and a safe traffic plan.
steps.success: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around.
errors: Stretching glide with pitch → preserve the approved glide condition and change the landing plan.
Late flap/slip correction near touchdown → improve the earlier energy decision or go around.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable geometry, unsafe bank, traffic, or insufficient runway; do not force the touchdown mark.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Power-off accuracy landing decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop

steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.

steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
