steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Coach checklist discipline and runway verification; during checks observe independently and intervene only for safety.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. Monitor actual conditions and model a concise post-takeoff configuration flow.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness
steps.instructor: Brief the relationship among groundspeed, pivotal altitude, wind, suitable pylons, and safe terrain clearance. Demonstrate one pylon turn, explaining why pitch rather than rudder is used to maintain the sight line; use current FAA/aircraft guidance for entry.
steps.student: Select safe pylons, determine an appropriate entry and pivotal-altitude estimate, clear the area, and fly linked turns while adjusting altitude for changing groundspeed. Maintain coordination and abandon unsuitable geometry.
steps.repetitions: Two complete eights; repeat the downwind/upwind transition with the largest sight-line error.
steps.success: Keeps the pylon on the selected sight line using appropriate pitch changes without unsafe bank or clearance loss.
errors: Rudder used to hold the pylon → restore coordination and adjust pitch/altitude appropriately.
Pylons chosen too close or hazardous → discontinue and select a safe pair.
steps.stop: Exit when terrain/obstacles, bank, coordination, or aircraft limits cannot be maintained.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Power-off accuracy landing decisions
steps.instructor: Brief the selected landing exercise, touchdown area, wind, runway, approved configurations, and go-around gates. Demonstrate energy judgment and allowable slips/configuration changes. Separate the commercial ACS power-off 180 task from optional 90/360-degree source exercises.
steps.student: From the agreed position reduce power using the approved simulation, assess glide/wind, choose turn points and configuration deliberately, and aim for the selected touchdown area. Go around when a safe outcome is doubtful rather than forcing the target.
steps.repetitions: Two power-off 180 attempts if suitable; 90/360-degree planning rehearsed on the ground or added only with time, approval, and a safe traffic plan.
steps.success: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around.
errors: Stretching glide with pitch → preserve the approved glide condition and change the landing plan.
Late flap/slip correction near touchdown → improve the earlier energy decision or go around.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable geometry, unsafe bank, traffic, or insufficient runway; do not force the touchdown mark.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Power-off accuracy landing decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique
steps.instructor: Select normal, short, or soft-field work from today’s source tasks and actual runway suitability. Review POH configuration/speeds, performance, touchdown plan, and go-around gates. Demonstrate one selected technique, then coach observation of approach/energy trends.
steps.student: Fly the selected takeoff technique, climb/configure as approved, then set up the matching stabilized approach and landing. State the go-around decision before conditions deteriorate; include a normal landing to compare energy management.
steps.repetitions: Three selected patterns if traffic permits: normal, one specialty technique, and one go-around; defer remaining variations rather than rush.
steps.success: Meets applicable commercial ACS criteria during evaluation and consistently recognizes an unstable or unsuitable landing.
errors: Technique memorized without performance calculation → tie the procedure to actual runway, weight, and conditions.
Touchdown target rescued with abrupt control → go around and analyze the energy trend.
steps.stop: Go around for instability, runway/traffic conflict, or loss of a safe landing path; use approved aircraft procedures.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Takeoff, landing, and go-around technique; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop
steps.instructor: Start with a stable attitude and power setting. Demonstrate attitude change, cross-check of performance, small correction, then trim. Explain which indication confirms each change; let the learner verbalize the scan before removing prompts.
steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: Two level-offs in each direction and at least two left/right turns; repeat the weakest transition.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Build the scan and trim loop; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade
steps.instructor: Sketch the maneuver’s changing bank/pitch/airspeed relationships. Demonstrate one direction, narrating the transition from the first half to the second and the coordinated rollout; use aircraft-approved entry parameters.
steps.student: Clear the area, enter at approved parameters, establish the climbing turn, manage the changing pitch and bank through the maneuver, and finish coordinated at the required heading and low-airspeed condition without a stall.
steps.repetitions: One each direction plus one repeat focused on the first/second-half transition.
steps.success: Uses a continuous coordinated energy trade and achieves the current ACS completion condition without abrupt corrections.

Yaw near completion → prioritize coordination as airspeed decreases.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for stall cues, loss of coordination, or inadequate altitude/clearance.

steps.title: Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes
steps.instructor: Use ground reference directions to show the sequence and pitch/bank/airspeed trends. Demonstrate smooth control pressure and balanced segments, emphasizing anticipation rather than fixed control positions.
steps.student: Clear the area and fly linked left/right segments through the maneuver’s reference points. Observe the changing attitude/airspeed, coordinate the turns, and compare the second half with the first before repeating.
steps.repetitions: Two full left/right cycles; repeat the quarter where timing or coordination broke down.
steps.success: Maintains a smooth continuous maneuver, balanced segments, and current ACS criteria with useful outside references.
errors: Maneuver becomes two abrupt turns → smooth the control changes across reference points.
Reference fixation → distribute attention among horizon, references, coordination, and performance.
steps.stop: Stop for stall cues, disorientation, or a threatened aircraft/safety limit.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.instructor: State the simulation method, instructor takeover gates, and any prohibited control actions. Teach aviate, diagnose, appropriate immediate actions, approved checklist, communication, and landing choice. Practice recognition and judgment without creating the actual failure.
steps.student: Identify a simulated abnormality from valid indications, control the aircraft, apply aircraft-approved actions, use the checklist, and select a suitable landing/alternate. For a simulated forced landing, establish the approved glide profile and plan a reachable field; terminate at the briefed gate.

steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Use ground reference directions to show the sequence and pitch/bank/airspeed trends. Demonstrate smooth control pressure and balanced segments, emphasizing anticipation rather than fixed control positions. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Clear the area and fly linked left/right segments through the maneuver’s reference points. Observe the changing attitude/airspeed, coordinate the turns, and compare the second half with the first before repeating.
steps.repetitions: Two full left/right cycles; repeat the quarter where timing or coordination broke down.
steps.success: Maintains a smooth continuous maneuver, balanced segments, and current ACS criteria with useful outside references.
errors: Maneuver becomes two abrupt turns → smooth the control changes across reference points.
Reference fixation → distribute attention among horizon, references, coordination, and performance.
steps.stop: Stop for stall cues, disorientation, or a threatened aircraft/safety limit.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief the relationship among groundspeed, pivotal altitude, wind, suitable pylons, and safe terrain clearance. Demonstrate one pylon turn, explaining why pitch rather than rudder is used to maintain the sight line; use current FAA/aircraft guidance for entry. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Select safe pylons, determine an appropriate entry and pivotal-altitude estimate, clear the area, and fly linked turns while adjusting altitude for changing groundspeed. Maintain coordination and abandon unsuitable geometry.
steps.repetitions: Two complete eights; repeat the downwind/upwind transition with the largest sight-line error.
steps.success: Keeps the pylon on the selected sight line using appropriate pitch changes without unsafe bank or clearance loss.
errors: Rudder used to hold the pylon → restore coordination and adjust pitch/altitude appropriately.
Pylons chosen too close or hazardous → discontinue and select a safe pair.
steps.stop: Exit when terrain/obstacles, bank, coordination, or aircraft limits cannot be maintained.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Power-off accuracy landing decisions
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief the selected landing exercise, touchdown area, wind, runway, approved configurations, and go-around gates. Demonstrate energy judgment and allowable slips/configuration changes. Separate the commercial ACS power-off 180 task from optional 90/360-degree source exercises. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: From the agreed position reduce power using the approved simulation, assess glide/wind, choose turn points and configuration deliberately, and aim for the selected touchdown area. Go around when a safe outcome is doubtful rather than forcing the target.
steps.repetitions: Two power-off 180 attempts if suitable; 90/360-degree planning rehearsed on the ground or added only with time, approval, and a safe traffic plan.
steps.success: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around.
errors: Stretching glide with pitch → preserve the approved glide condition and change the landing plan.
Late flap/slip correction near touchdown → improve the earlier energy decision or go around.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable geometry, unsafe bank, traffic, or insufficient runway; do not force the touchdown mark.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Power-off accuracy landing decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Review the return decision on the ground and arrange an overdue plan.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks

steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks

steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.

steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.

errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.

steps.title: Steep turns with commercial precision
steps.instructor: Brief attitude, bank/load relationship, entry/exit, clearing, and the current ACS criteria. Demonstrate a smooth entry and coordinated correction; identify whether an altitude trend is caused by pitch, power, or bank before coaching the fix.
steps.student: Clear the area, establish the approved entry, fly a steep turn in each direction, anticipate rollout, and return to the starting flight condition. Describe and correct the first attempt’s dominant error on the repeat.
steps.repetitions: One left/right pair plus one targeted repeat.
steps.success: Divides attention outside and inside, manages load/energy, and meets current ACS criteria on the independent attempt.
errors: Bank drift masked by pitch correction → correct bank and reassess altitude.
Late rollout → anticipate the exit and return smoothly to straight-and-level.
steps.stop: Recover before envelope, clearance, or altitude margin is threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep turns with commercial precision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery
steps.instructor: Brief approved configuration, clearing, entry, cues, and recovery priorities. Contrast slow flight with an intentional stall exercise and show how bank/load and coordination change the risk; do not use a source task list as authority for prohibited aircraft maneuvers.
steps.student: Establish the assigned slow-flight condition, make coordinated turns/climbs/descents, and recover. Conduct approved power-off/power-on stall exercises in the requested attitudes, recognize cues, reduce angle of attack, and restore a controlled flight path.
steps.repetitions: One slow-flight sequence and one power-off/power-on pair; accelerated-stall work only when approved and briefed.
steps.success: Recognizes cues early, manages coordination, and recovers without excessive altitude loss or secondary stall.
errors: Holding altitude after stall warning → reduce angle of attack and follow the approved recovery.
Yaw during entry → correct coordination or terminate before loss of control.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

errors: Checklist before control → stabilize and manage the immediate hazard first.

steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.

steps.title: VFR route management and diversion
steps.instructor: Review the learner’s route, weather, terrain, fuel, performance, airspace, and alternates. In dual lessons demonstrate one prediction-check-correction cycle; later introduce a diversion or lost-position scenario without removing safe navigation options.
steps.student: Depart on the planned course, identify checkpoints, compare groundspeed/fuel with estimates, and update arrival time. Navigate to a selected alternate, use ATC services when useful, and explain the lost-position recovery plan before continuing.

steps.stop: Return, land, or divert when actual conditions exceed the briefed limits; do not continue merely to complete a planned distance.

steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 30 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: Two level-offs in each direction and at least two left/right turns; repeat the weakest transition.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.

steps.title: Start, taxi, and departure checks
steps.instructor: Before dispatch the instructor reviews the planned route, practice boundaries and return gates; no instructor is carried on a solo flight. For certificated PIC, agree on the actual pilot roles and logging eligibility.
steps.student: Start and taxi using the approved checklist, review hotspots, read back restrictions, hold short correctly, and complete run-up/departure checks before entering the runway.
steps.repetitions: One complete ground departure flow.
steps.success: Positive runway/clearance verification, deliberate checklist and configuration checks.
errors: Heads-down taxi → stop before configuring or troubleshooting.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for uncertain clearance, traffic, or an unresolved abnormality.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Takeoff, climb, and intercept
steps.instructor: Brief the approved takeoff/abort and climb procedure. On the ground confirm that the pilot can execute it independently.
steps.student: Verify runway and clearance, take off using the approved technique, establish climb, configure/check, and intercept the cleared or planned course. A view-limiting device is used only after the outside-lookout/control arrangement is established.
steps.repetitions: One departure and course intercept.
steps.success: Maintains control, follows the route/clearance, and completes checks at an appropriate workload.
errors: Fixation on route programming → stabilize flight and defer the entry.
steps.stop: Abort or return under the actual aircraft procedure and conditions; no universal return altitude.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Steep turns with commercial precision
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief attitude, bank/load relationship, entry/exit, clearing, and the current ACS criteria. Demonstrate a smooth entry and coordinated correction; identify whether an altitude trend is caused by pitch, power, or bank before coaching the fix. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Clear the area, establish the approved entry, fly a steep turn in each direction, anticipate rollout, and return to the starting flight condition. Describe and correct the first attempt’s dominant error on the repeat.
steps.repetitions: One left/right pair plus one targeted repeat.
steps.success: Divides attention outside and inside, manages load/energy, and meets current ACS criteria on the independent attempt.
errors: Bank drift masked by pitch correction → correct bank and reassess altitude.
Late rollout → anticipate the exit and return smoothly to straight-and-level.
steps.stop: Recover before envelope, clearance, or altitude margin is threatened.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep turns with commercial precision; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Sketch the maneuver’s changing bank/pitch/airspeed relationships. Demonstrate one direction, narrating the transition from the first half to the second and the coordinated rollout; use aircraft-approved entry parameters. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Clear the area, enter at approved parameters, establish the climbing turn, manage the changing pitch and bank through the maneuver, and finish coordinated at the required heading and low-airspeed condition without a stall.
steps.repetitions: One each direction plus one repeat focused on the first/second-half transition.
steps.success: Uses a continuous coordinated energy trade and achieves the current ACS completion condition without abrupt corrections.
errors: Pitch/bank schedule rushed → identify the transition points and let airspeed trend develop.
Yaw near completion → prioritize coordination as airspeed decreases.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for stall cues, loss of coordination, or inadequate altitude/clearance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Chandelles: coordinated climbing energy trade; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Use ground reference directions to show the sequence and pitch/bank/airspeed trends. Demonstrate smooth control pressure and balanced segments, emphasizing anticipation rather than fixed control positions. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Clear the area and fly linked left/right segments through the maneuver’s reference points. Observe the changing attitude/airspeed, coordinate the turns, and compare the second half with the first before repeating.
steps.repetitions: Two full left/right cycles; repeat the quarter where timing or coordination broke down.
steps.success: Maintains a smooth continuous maneuver, balanced segments, and current ACS criteria with useful outside references.
errors: Maneuver becomes two abrupt turns → smooth the control changes across reference points.
Reference fixation → distribute attention among horizon, references, coordination, and performance.
steps.stop: Stop for stall cues, disorientation, or a threatened aircraft/safety limit.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief the relationship among groundspeed, pivotal altitude, wind, suitable pylons, and safe terrain clearance. Demonstrate one pylon turn, explaining why pitch rather than rudder is used to maintain the sight line; use current FAA/aircraft guidance for entry. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Select safe pylons, determine an appropriate entry and pivotal-altitude estimate, clear the area, and fly linked turns while adjusting altitude for changing groundspeed. Maintain coordination and abandon unsuitable geometry.
steps.repetitions: Two complete eights; repeat the downwind/upwind transition with the largest sight-line error.
steps.success: Keeps the pylon on the selected sight line using appropriate pitch changes without unsafe bank or clearance loss.
errors: Rudder used to hold the pylon → restore coordination and adjust pitch/altitude appropriately.
Pylons chosen too close or hazardous → discontinue and select a safe pair.
steps.stop: Exit when terrain/obstacles, bank, coordination, or aircraft limits cannot be maintained.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Eights on pylons and pivotal-altitude awareness; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Power-off accuracy landing decisions
steps.instructor: Before dispatch review the approved practice plan and safety gates. Brief the selected landing exercise, touchdown area, wind, runway, approved configurations, and go-around gates. Demonstrate energy judgment and allowable slips/configuration changes. Separate the commercial ACS power-off 180 task from optional 90/360-degree source exercises. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: From the agreed position reduce power using the approved simulation, assess glide/wind, choose turn points and configuration deliberately, and aim for the selected touchdown area. Go around when a safe outcome is doubtful rather than forcing the target.
steps.repetitions: Two power-off 180 attempts if suitable; 90/360-degree planning rehearsed on the ground or added only with time, approval, and a safe traffic plan.
steps.success: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around.
errors: Stretching glide with pitch → preserve the approved glide condition and change the landing plan.
Late flap/slip correction near touchdown → improve the earlier energy decision or go around.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable geometry, unsafe bank, traffic, or insufficient runway; do not force the touchdown mark.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Power-off accuracy landing decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Review the return decision on the ground and arrange an overdue plan.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.student: Independently: Clear the area, establish the appropriate glide configuration and speed, turn around the reference with wind-adjusted bank, maintain coordination, and recover at the briefed gate on a selected heading.
steps.repetitions: One complete spiral within the available safe altitude; repeat one wind quadrant if needed.
steps.success: Maintains glide and reference spacing while respecting bank/load and recovery margins.
errors: Bank increased to fix poor reference choice → choose geometry that fits safe bank and altitude limits.
Airspeed neglected while watching the ground → cross-check glide performance throughout.
steps.stop: Recover at the prebriefed gate, before excessive bank/airspeed or insufficient terrain clearance.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Steep spiral and glide planning; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

Contrast slow flight with an intentional stall exercise and show how bank/load and coordination change the risk; do not use a source task list as authority for prohibited aircraft maneuvers. For solo/PIC exercises, complete the explanation or demonstration on the ground or a preceding dual flight; there is no in-flight instructor coaching planned.
steps.student: Independently: Establish the assigned slow-flight condition, make coordinated turns/climbs/descents, and recover. Conduct approved power-off/power-on stall exercises in the requested attitudes, recognize cues, reduce angle of attack, and restore a controlled flight path.
steps.repetitions: One slow-flight sequence and one power-off/power-on pair; accelerated-stall work only when approved and briefed.
steps.success: Recognizes cues early, manages coordination, and recovers without excessive altitude loss or secondary stall.
errors: Holding altitude after stall warning → reduce angle of attack and follow the approved recovery.
Yaw during entry → correct coordination or terminate before loss of control.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.student: Clear the area and fly linked left/right segments through the maneuver’s reference points. Observe the changing attitude/airspeed, coordinate the turns, and compare the second half with the first before repeating.
steps.repetitions: Two full left/right cycles; repeat the quarter where timing or coordination broke down.
steps.success: Maintains a smooth continuous maneuver, balanced segments, and current ACS criteria with useful outside references.
errors: Maneuver becomes two abrupt turns → smooth the control changes across reference points.
Reference fixation → distribute attention among horizon, references, coordination, and performance.
steps.stop: Stop for stall cues, disorientation, or a threatened aircraft/safety limit.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery
steps.instructor: Brief approved configuration, clearing, entry, cues, and recovery priorities. Contrast slow flight with an intentional stall exercise and show how bank/load and coordination change the risk; do not use a source task list as authority for prohibited aircraft maneuvers.
steps.student: Establish the assigned slow-flight condition, make coordinated turns/climbs/descents, and recover. Conduct approved power-off/power-on stall exercises in the requested attitudes, recognize cues, reduce angle of attack, and restore a controlled flight path.
steps.repetitions: One slow-flight sequence and one power-off/power-on pair; accelerated-stall work only when approved and briefed.
steps.success: Recognizes cues early, manages coordination, and recovers without excessive altitude loss or secondary stall.
errors: Holding altitude after stall warning → reduce angle of attack and follow the approved recovery.
Yaw during entry → correct coordination or terminate before loss of control.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options
steps.instructor: State the simulation method, instructor takeover gates, and any prohibited control actions. Teach aviate, diagnose, appropriate immediate actions, approved checklist, communication, and landing choice. Practice recognition and judgment without creating the actual failure.
steps.student: Identify a simulated abnormality from valid indications, control the aircraft, apply aircraft-approved actions, use the checklist, and select a suitable landing/alternate. For a simulated forced landing, establish the approved glide profile and plan a reachable field; terminate at the briefed gate.
steps.repetitions: One systems problem and one descent/forced-landing decision; one checklist recovery after the first response.
steps.success: Maintains control, avoids premature diagnosis, and chooses a landing plan supported by terrain, wind, and aircraft capability.
errors: Checklist before control → stabilize and manage the immediate hazard first.
Field selected without reachability → compare glide/terrain/wind and choose a viable alternative early.
steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Power-off accuracy landing decisions
steps.instructor: Brief the selected landing exercise, touchdown area, wind, runway, approved configurations, and go-around gates. Demonstrate energy judgment and allowable slips/configuration changes. Separate the commercial ACS power-off 180 task from optional 90/360-degree source exercises.
steps.student: From the agreed position reduce power using the approved simulation, assess glide/wind, choose turn points and configuration deliberately, and aim for the selected touchdown area. Go around when a safe outcome is doubtful rather than forcing the target.
steps.repetitions: Two power-off 180 attempts if suitable; 90/360-degree planning rehearsed on the ground or added only with time, approval, and a safe traffic plan.
steps.success: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around.
errors: Stretching glide with pitch → preserve the approved glide condition and change the landing plan.
Late flap/slip correction near touchdown → improve the earlier energy decision or go around.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable geometry, unsafe bank, traffic, or insufficient runway; do not force the touchdown mark.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Power-off accuracy landing decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

errors: Pitch/bank schedule rushed → identify the transition points and let airspeed trend develop.

steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Lazy eights: visual references and smooth energy changes; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw, roll, envelope exceedance, altitude-margin loss, or an aircraft restriction.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Slow flight and stall recognition/recovery; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Power-off accuracy landing decisions
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed power-off accuracy landing decisions scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: From the agreed position reduce power using the approved simulation, assess glide/wind, choose turn points and configuration deliberately, and aim for the selected touchdown area. Go around when a safe outcome is doubtful rather than forcing the target.
steps.repetitions: One selected assessed/review attempt within this short block. Full teaching or remaining repetitions must be carried forward; do not rush the task.
steps.success: Uses a consistent glide picture and current ACS criteria on evaluation while preserving a safe runway landing or go-around.
errors: Stretching glide with pitch → preserve the approved glide condition and change the landing plan.
Late flap/slip correction near touchdown → improve the earlier energy decision or go around.
steps.stop: Go around for unstable geometry, unsafe bank, traffic, or insufficient runway; do not force the touchdown mark.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Power-off accuracy landing decisions; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed abnormal systems, descent, and landing options scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Maintains control, avoids premature diagnosis, and chooses a landing plan supported by terrain, wind, and aircraft capability. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Identify a simulated abnormality from valid indications, control the aircraft, apply aircraft-approved actions, use the checklist, and select a suitable landing/alternate. For a simulated forced landing, establish the approved glide profile and plan a reachable field; terminate at the briefed gate.
steps.repetitions: One selected assessed/review attempt within this short block. Full teaching or remaining repetitions must be carried forward; do not rush the task.
steps.success: Maintains control, avoids premature diagnosis, and chooses a landing plan supported by terrain, wind, and aircraft capability.
errors: Checklist before control → stabilize and manage the immediate hazard first.
Field selected without reachability → compare glide/terrain/wind and choose a viable alternative early.
steps.stop: Recover at the briefed safety gate; never shut down critical equipment or engines solely to imitate an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Abnormal systems, descent, and landing options; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Build the scan and trim loop
steps.instructor: Assign the briefed build the scan and trim loop scenario and observe setup, execution, and decisions without coaching. Assess this result: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage. Record errors for the parked debrief; intervene immediately for safety. New instruction and corrective demonstration belong in a separate training flight.
steps.student: Establish straight-and-level flight, make assigned standard-rate turns, then constant-airspeed climbs and descents. Lead the level-off, set cruise power, verify performance, and trim without abandoning the cross-check. Plan 18 minutes of this block as actual or simulated instrument only with the agreed legal pilot/instructor/lookout arrangement; actual conditions determine what can be logged.
steps.repetitions: One independent demonstration of each selected task; remedial coaching belongs in a later training flight.
steps.success: Maintains an effective cross-check and corrects trends before large deviations; uses applicable ACS tolerances at the evaluation stage.
errors: Fixation on one instrument → identify the missing cross-check and return to attitude/performance confirmation.
Large chase corrections → stabilize attitude and power, wait for the response, then refine.
steps.stop: Remove the view-limiting device or take control for unsafe trends, traffic conflict, disorientation, or an unrecoverable task load.
steps.reference: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook; Build the scan and trim loop; current ACS and applicable POH/AFM

steps.title: Return, landing, and go-around decision
steps.instructor: Reassess fuel, weather, traffic, runway and learner workload before returning. Let the learner plan the arrival; avoid rescuing a late approach with last-minute prompts.
steps.student: Obtain the arrival information/clearance, brief the runway and landing configuration, fly a stabilized approach, land if safe or go around using the approved procedure, then clear the runway.
steps.repetitions: One stable arrival and final landing; additional approaches are only those budgeted in exercise blocks.
steps.success: Timely configuration and a decisive landing/go-around choice.
errors: Late arrival briefing → finish the plan before descent or request delay.
steps.stop: Go around whenever the safe landing conditions are not met.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

steps.title: Taxi in, shutdown, and aircraft checks
steps.instructor: Keep the learner focused on taxi and securing the airplane; gather teaching notes after movement stops.
steps.student: Clear and identify the taxi route, perform after-landing checks when safe, park, shut down, secure, and report any equipment discrepancy.
steps.repetitions: One complete shutdown and securing flow.
steps.success: Safe taxi and accurate checklist/equipment follow-up.
errors: Debrief during a hotspot → postpone discussion until parked.
steps.stop: Stop for uncertain route or traffic; complete abnormal follow-up before another departure.
steps.reference: Applicable POH/AFM and checklist; FAA Airplane Flying Handbook

courses.overview: The student in this route is the instructor candidate; the instructor is the qualified trainer who can role-play a learner. The candidate prepares and teaches a measurable preflight lesson, demonstrates while explaining, supervises practice, diagnoses errors and assesses the result. Timing is an adjustable plan. Aircraft inspection/preparation, parked briefing and debrief are separate from the flight block; flight includes taxi, departure/transit, practice and safe return. Repeat or defer tasks until proficiency is demonstrated, and meet actual regulatory experience/endorsement requirements independently.
entryRequirements: Meet applicable 14 CFR 61.183 eligibility, pilot-rating, knowledge-test, PIC-experience and endorsement requirements; the recommending instructor verifies records.
Receive training from an instructor authorized and qualified for the initial certificate under 61.195, including the applicable initial-instructor qualification provisions.
Complete FOI, technical subject and preflight-preparation study before the corresponding candidate-taught lesson; use current FAA references rather than this flight guide as a full ground syllabus.
Verify the applicable 61.183(i) spin-training/endorsement requirement using a separately suitable approved aircraft and qualified instructor.
This authored flight sequence covers ASEL. ASES or a different existing-rating pathway needs its own applicable class tasks and additional-rating table review.

steps.title: Teach normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the aircraft systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Teach attitude, power, trim and the four fundamentals
steps.instructor: Demonstrate one change at a time: attitude, power, then trim. Give the candidate a desired flight path rather than a control command. Act as a learner who chases an instrument; require the candidate to redirect attention to an outside reference and then verify the result.
steps.student: State the purpose and target; demonstrate level flight, a coordinated level turn, climb and descent. Hand over positively, coach the role-play learner through the same sequence, and ask the learner to explain which change produced the observed result.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached learner attempt of each fundamental; prioritize a weak item for the remaining time.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the briefed commercial-level task tolerances while explaining cause and effect, then identifies and corrects a learner deviation without losing the traffic scan.
errors: Trimming before establishing the attitude/power combination -> stabilize the airplane first and then trim.
Continuous instrument fixation -> restore an outside attitude reference and use the instruments to confirm it.
steps.stop: Stop the exercise for uncoordinated control, an unsafe flight path, traffic conflict or loss of role clarity; reestablish ordinary flight before further explanation.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VIII.A-D; AFH chapter 3

steps.title: Teach coordinated steep turns and workload control
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to brief the applicable bank target, entry speed, power and limitation from the ACS/aircraft documents. Demonstrate a safe learner tendency to lose altitude by discussing it or making only a small recoverable deviation.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the entry condition; demonstrate a coordinated turn in each direction. Explain attitude, back-pressure, power and trim management, then coach a learner through a turn and rollout to the starting heading.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration each direction; one coached attempt in the weaker direction; reset between turns.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable commercial/instructor task standard and diagnoses the cause of altitude/airspeed deviations while retaining coordination and lookout.
errors: Adding more bank to correct an altitude loss -> diagnose the load/attitude problem before the correction.
Rolling out late while explaining -> lead the rollout and divide attention between instruction and the flight path.
steps.stop: Stop for aircraft load/speed limit, loss of coordination, significant flight-path deterioration or traffic conflict. The instructor takes control before the learner error becomes unsafe.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.A; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach normal pattern operations and crosswind judgment
steps.instructor: Let the candidate brief pattern entry, wind correction, runway choice, stabilized approach criteria and a positive control-transfer plan. Act as a learner who overlooks a checklist or misjudges spacing; use a verbal prompt instead of creating an unsafe approach.
steps.student: Teach a normal/crosswind departure and approach using the actual airport procedures. Demonstrate one approach, coach the next, explain workload management and make a planned go-around. Make the landing/go-around decision early enough to preserve options.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration circuit, one coached circuit and one planned go-around as traffic/ATC permit; no forced pattern count.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the airplane within task standards while teaching runway alignment, energy, spacing, communication and a timely go-around.
errors: Talking through final while losing airspeed/alignment -> shorten instruction, regain a stabilized approach or go around.
Treating an ATC instruction as permission to exceed a limit -> request an alternative and protect the aircraft margin.
steps.stop: Go around or discontinue for an unstable approach, unsafe spacing, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or unclear control responsibility. Touch-and-go operations require aircraft/airport authorization.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.A-B and VII.A-B,N; AFH chapters 6, 8-9

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
Candidate recognizes and diagnoses learner errors, intervenes before unsafe flight and provides a justified performance assessment.
Task mastery is based on observed performance; completing the time block or reading the checklist alone does not complete the lesson.

Observed task outcome: Candidate maintains the briefed commercial-level task tolerances while explaining cause and effect, then identifies and corrects a learner deviation without losing the traffic scan.
debrief: Candidate first explains which flight/teaching outcome was strongest and identifies one error with its cause.
Compare trainer evidence with candidate self-assessment; distinguish pilot performance from explanation, learner supervision and risk judgment.
Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.
carryForward: Focus the first flight on flight-path reliability; a full steep-turn teaching evaluation is deferred if instructor-seat control is not yet stable.
lessons.applicability: Aircraft-neutral instructor guidance. Actual aircraft authority, current rules/standards, weather, terrain and instructor judgment control each flight.

objectives: Teach the named tasks through purpose, setup, demonstration, learner practice and an evidence-based assessment.

Maintain aircraft control, positive flight-control exchanges, traffic protection and aircraft-specific risk/recovery limits while instructing.
prerequisites: Prepare a short preflight lesson with a measurable outcome for each fundamental.
Before dispatch, enter/brief actual aircraft targets, configuration, authorized simulation methods and task recovery limits from the POH/AFM, current standards and operator procedures.
Use the separate preflight budget for inspection, documents/equipment and current weather/NOTAM/performance checks; do not count this as airborne practice.

steps.title: Teach normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the aircraft systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Teach slow flight and configuration effects
steps.instructor: Have the candidate name the selected ACS slow-flight task, its configuration and recovery criterion before changing configuration. Demonstrate changing drag/power while preserving coordination. Role-play fixation on airspeed so the candidate must coach attitude, coordination and warning recognition. Distinguish maneuvering-during-slow-flight task X.A from the separate ASEL configuration/airspeed demonstration X.B; set the applicable cue/recovery criterion for each before beginning.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the approved configuration and briefed task condition. Explain how control response and power requirements change; demonstrate straight flight, a turn, climb and descent as applicable. Coach a learner attempt and return to the normal configuration using the aircraft checklist. For the separate X.B demonstration, compare handling, required power, pitch/trim, control response and stall margin in the applicable cruise, climb, approach and landing configurations/airspeeds using approved aircraft targets; explain the practical implication of each transition.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one short diagnosis of a deliberately small, safe deviation. The X.B configuration comparison is a separate observed demonstration; defer/repeat it if adequate safe practice does not fit.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the distinction between slow-flight tasks, uses the appropriate warning/recovery criterion, and maintains applicable ACS tolerances with coordinated control.
errors: Treating the stall-warning condition as the same for every slow-flight task -> restate the selected task criterion.
Trying to climb with pitch alone -> compare the flight-path and airspeed indications, then make the approved power/attitude change.
steps.stop: Recover for an unbriefed stall indication, degraded directional control, traffic conflict or reaching the applicable recovery floor. Never continue merely to consume the block.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.A-B and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach a power-off stall and its recovery
steps.instructor: Brief whether recovery is at the first indication or after a full stall, as applicable. Observe the candidate explain an approach-to-landing setup. Act as a learner who tries to hold the nose up during recovery; require prompt explanation of angle-of-attack reduction.
steps.student: Clear the area, verify recovery altitude and aircraft authorization, and establish the approved approach configuration. Explain the developing cues during entry. Recover using the aircraft procedure, regain controlled flight, clean up as appropriate, then coach one learner attempt.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached attempt; repeat only if the recovery remains controlled and the planned altitude margin is available.
steps.success: The candidate recognizes the briefed stall condition, reduces angle of attack promptly, maintains coordination, and explains the recovery while meeting the applicable ACS standard.
errors: Watching only the airspeed indicator -> identify aerodynamic and warning cues throughout entry.
Retraction or pitch changes that cause a second stall -> stabilize recovery and follow the approved configuration sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw/incipient spin, a recovery-floor threat, an unbriefed full stall, aircraft limitation, or a trainer intervention. Review the cause before another attempt.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.C and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach a power-on stall without hiding the yaw risk
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to brief approved power and configuration, pitch limits if applicable, and recovery cues. Watch the candidate explain the coordination demand. Introduce an oral learner misconception about correcting yaw with aileron; do not create a hazardous physical error.
steps.student: Clear the area and set the authorized departure configuration/power. Explain the changing control pressures and stall cues, demonstrate the briefed recovery, and coach a coordinated learner attempt. Compare the departure-stall risk with the earlier approach-stall lesson.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one coached attempt; one verbal yaw-error diagnosis.
steps.success: Candidate maintains directional control, detects the chosen stall cue, recovers by the approved procedure, and gives an accurate explanation while flying.
errors: Increasing pitch without monitoring coordination -> restore coordinated control and reassess the entry.
Explaining during a developing loss of control -> recover first, then discuss the cue.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for unbriefed yaw/roll, impending spin, an exceeded aircraft limit, or insufficient recovery margin. Do not reproduce a hazardous learner error.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.D and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

steps.stop: Leave the exercise for unsuitable terrain/obstructions, people/property risk, traffic, an unavailable emergency option or a breached altitude margin; do not descend to make the diagram look better.

steps.repetitions: One candidate pair and one coached pair if conditions permit; otherwise complete the explanation and defer the required flight practice.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the intended visual reference relationship without fixation and can explain the effect of groundspeed on the required flight path.
errors: Using one computed altitude regardless of groundspeed -> connect changing groundspeed to the reference movement.

steps.stop: Exit for unsuitable terrain/pylon spacing, traffic, lack of safe forced-landing options or loss of terrain margin. No universal operational altitude is supplied.
