steps.title: Teach short-field takeoff planning and execution
steps.instructor: Require an actual performance calculation with the selected weight, weather, runway and obstacles. Ask the candidate to compare available distance with the approved takeoff/obstacle profile and to identify reject/continue decisions from the aircraft and conditions.
steps.student: Explain configuration, runway use, approved target speeds and obstacle-clearance path. Demonstrate or coach the assigned short-field takeoff; verify the flight path and checklist transition after obstacle clearance. Teach why a computed capability is not a reason to accept inadequate margin.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff with complete briefing; a second only if runway/traffic/time permit.
steps.success: Candidate uses correct aircraft-specific performance and configuration, achieves the applicable task standard, and explains reject/continue judgment clearly.
errors: Using a memorized generic speed -> locate and use the approved speed for this aircraft/loading.
Skipping the runway/performance comparison -> recalculate before departure.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway/obstacle margin or an unmet aircraft condition. Reject only by the briefed approved procedure; simulated failures must be separately authorized and safely bounded.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.E; AFH chapter 6

steps.title: Teach short-field landing and a safe go-around choice
steps.instructor: Have the candidate choose the touchdown point, approved approach profile, wind correction and go-around gate. Role-play excessive focus on the touchdown mark and ask for a decision before the approach becomes unstable.
steps.student: Brief and fly a stabilized short-field approach with the approved configuration and speeds. Explain the aim point versus touchdown point, coach the learner through roundout/landing, and apply approved stopping procedures only after maintaining directional control.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached attempt when traffic permits; any required go-around replaces the landing attempt.
steps.success: Candidate satisfies applicable task accuracy while making a safe approach/landing decision and teaching directional control and energy management.
errors: Stretching a glide to reach the mark -> correct the energy/path while options exist or go around.
Forcing the touchdown after an unstable approach -> go around; record why the original target was not met.
steps.stop: Go around for an unstable path, unsafe wind, runway conflict or inadequate remaining distance. Never force a landing solely to achieve a target mark.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.F; AFH chapter 9

steps.title: Teach soft-field takeoff technique and surface decisions
steps.instructor: Require approved surface operations and aircraft technique. Use the briefing to compare actual soft/rough conditions with a simulated exercise on a suitable hard runway. Observe the candidate explain loading, drag and acceleration management.
steps.student: Demonstrate the approved control positioning and liftoff/acceleration profile, then coach a learner attempt. Explain why liftoff and climb are separate phases and how approved speed/configuration establish a safe departure.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated or coached takeoff; compare the omitted role verbally if time/traffic prevent a second.
steps.success: Candidate follows the aircraft procedure, maintains directional control, and explains the transition from surface drag to safe acceleration and climb.
errors: Using an aggressive pitch change to leave the ground -> restore the approved attitude/profile.
Beginning climb before adequate acceleration -> follow the aircraft departure sequence and protect stall margin.
steps.stop: Do not use an unsuitable surface or operate outside aircraft limitations. Stop/reject using the briefed aircraft procedure if directional control or performance becomes unacceptable.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.C; AFH chapter 6

steps.title: Teach soft-field landing without losing control
steps.instructor: Brief the approved configuration and touchdown/rollout technique. Ask the candidate to explain how the surface and landing-gear design alter the procedure. Use a suitable runway for simulation when actual surface operations are inappropriate.
steps.student: Demonstrate or coach a stabilized soft-field approach, touchdown and rollout using the aircraft procedure. Explain the required control positioning and why aircraft control and safe stopping remain the primary objectives.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one coached attempt as conditions permit; a go-around replaces any unsafe attempt.
steps.success: Candidate uses approved surface-specific technique, meets applicable task standards and provides concise coaching through touchdown and rollout.
errors: Adding unbriefed power during touchdown -> use the aircraft-approved technique and preserve runway margin.
Releasing control positioning immediately on touchdown -> maintain the required surface/wind correction through rollout.
steps.stop: Go around for an unstable approach, unsuitable surface or inadequate margin; do not land merely to demonstrate the surface technique.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.D; AFH chapter 9

steps.title: Teach forward slip, sideslip and landing limitations
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to identify aircraft restrictions on slipping and flap/configuration combinations. Explain the different purposes of a forward slip and a sideslip before any demonstration.
steps.student: At a suitable altitude, demonstrate the authorized slip and recover to coordinated flight. Teach how a landing application changes the flight path or wind correction, then coach an approved approach application only if stable and legal.
steps.repetitions: One altitude demonstration; one approach application only when authorized and needed.
steps.success: Candidate distinguishes the two slip purposes, respects aircraft limits and restores the appropriate coordinated/landing condition before touchdown.
errors: Confusing a skid with a deliberate slip -> explain the control relationship and discontinue the skid.
Using a slip to rescue an approach outside safe limits -> go around and rebuild the approach.
steps.stop: Do not use a prohibited slip/configuration or accept stall/terrain margin loss. Abandon an unstable approach; no maneuver practice overrides the POH/AFM.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.M; AFH chapter 9

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
Candidate recognizes and diagnoses learner errors, intervenes before unsafe flight and provides a justified performance assessment.
Task mastery is based on observed performance; completing the time block or reading the checklist alone does not complete the lesson.
Observed task outcome: Candidate uses correct aircraft-specific performance and configuration, achieves the applicable task standard, and explains reject/continue judgment clearly.
debrief: Candidate first explains which flight/teaching outcome was strongest and identifies one error with its cause.
Compare trainer evidence with candidate self-assessment; distinguish pilot performance from explanation, learner supervision and risk judgment.
Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.
carryForward: Five task blocks provide focused exposure, not automatic mastery; carry the weakest takeoff/landing variant to lessons 12 or 15.
lessons.applicability: Aircraft-neutral instructor guidance. Actual aircraft authority, current rules/standards, weather, terrain and instructor judgment control each flight.

lessons.title: Teach abnormal systems and a simulated forced landing
lessons.summary: Prioritize control, a viable landing option and an applicable checklist while supervising a distracted learner.
objectives: Teach the named tasks through purpose, setup, demonstration, learner practice and an evidence-based assessment.
Prioritize control, a viable landing option and an applicable checklist while supervising a distracted learner.
Maintain aircraft control, positive flight-control exchanges, traffic protection and aircraft-specific risk/recovery limits while instructing.
prerequisites: Select two aircraft-specific malfunctions; brief simulated power loss and descent recovery limits.
In the parked briefing, teach location/use of emergency and survival equipment (ACS XII.D).
Before dispatch, enter/brief actual aircraft targets, configuration, authorized simulation methods and task recovery limits from the POH/AFM, current standards and operator procedures.
Use the separate preflight budget for inspection, documents/equipment and current weather/NOTAM/performance checks; do not count this as airborne practice.

steps.title: Teach normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the aircraft systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Teach system-failure recognition and checklist discipline
steps.instructor: Choose two aircraft-applicable scenarios and state which indications are simulated. Require the candidate to distinguish an indication failure from a physical aircraft failure and to justify any checklist selection.
steps.student: Explain the indications, control/flight-path consequences and appropriate aircraft checklist. Teach a role-play learner to prioritize the aircraft, verify the diagnosis, request assistance and decide whether to continue, divert or land.
steps.repetitions: Two verbal/simulated scenarios with no unsafe system disablement; candidate leads one and coaches one.
steps.success: Candidate selects applicable procedures without unsupported memory actions, maintains safe flight and teaches a reasoned landing/diversion decision.
errors: Choosing a checklist from one alarming indication -> cross-check and identify the actual problem.
Pulling a breaker or moving a critical control without authorization -> stop simulation and use the approved aircraft procedure.
steps.stop: Do not create a real malfunction to simulate one. Stop for actual abnormal indications, a prohibited equipment action, workload saturation or loss of flight-path control.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.C; AFH chapter 18; aircraft POH/AFM

steps.title: Teach simulated engine failure and landing-option judgment
steps.instructor: Select a safe scenario location with a viable real landing option if power is unavailable. Brief simulation, who moves controls, recovery limits and manufacturer restrictions. Act as a learner who fixates on troubleshooting after maintaining flight-path safety has been established.
steps.student: Maintain aircraft control using the approved glide/performance procedure. Explain landing-area choice and path planning, teach the applicable memory/checklist actions and communications, and recover from the simulation at the agreed safe point.
steps.repetitions: One candidate-led scenario and one coached planning segment; include a change in landing-option quality as a verbal event.
steps.success: Candidate manages energy and a viable landing option first, prioritizes the appropriate checklist/communication, and intervenes before a role-play learner becomes unsafe.
errors: Troubleshooting before establishing the flight path -> fly and secure a landing option first.
Keeping a poor initial landing site after conditions change -> reassess available choices without abrupt low-altitude maneuvering.
steps.stop: No intentional engine shutdown in a single-engine airplane. Terminate while a safe recovery is possible; an actual failure immediately replaces the exercise with the real emergency response.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.B and Appendix 2; AFH chapter 18

steps.title: Teach an emergency descent with a recovery plan
steps.instructor: Give a scenario such as smoke or pressurization concern and require the candidate to identify the applicable aircraft procedure. Brief the selected configuration, speed limit, clearing, terrain and level-off plan before demonstrating.
steps.student: Explain the priority and immediate actions from the aircraft checklist, demonstrate the authorized descent profile and recover at the briefed safe altitude. Coach a learner through a second segment without creating an actual system emergency.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one short coached segment; one oral scenario comparison.
steps.success: Candidate chooses the appropriate procedure, remains oriented, respects configuration/speed limits and teaches a controlled recovery/level-off.
errors: Diving before checking terrain/traffic -> maintain control and select a safe path.
Inventing one descent configuration for every emergency -> identify and apply the specific aircraft procedure.
steps.stop: Recover before a terrain/altitude limit, aircraft speed/configuration limit or traffic conflict. Actual smoke, fire or equipment failure ends the training scenario and requires the real procedure.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.A; AFH chapter 18

steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.

steps.title: Teach coordinated steep turns and workload control
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to brief the applicable bank target, entry speed, power and limitation from the ACS/aircraft documents. Demonstrate a safe learner tendency to lose altitude by discussing it or making only a small recoverable deviation.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the entry condition; demonstrate a coordinated turn in each direction. Explain attitude, back-pressure, power and trim management, then coach a learner through a turn and rollout to the starting heading.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration each direction; one coached attempt in the weaker direction; reset between turns.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable commercial/instructor task standard and diagnoses the cause of altitude/airspeed deviations while retaining coordination and lookout.
errors: Adding more bank to correct an altitude loss -> diagnose the load/attitude problem before the correction.
Rolling out late while explaining -> lead the rollout and divide attention between instruction and the flight path.
steps.stop: Stop for aircraft load/speed limit, loss of coordination, significant flight-path deterioration or traffic conflict. The instructor takes control before the learner error becomes unsafe.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.A; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach a steep spiral around a selected landing reference
steps.instructor: Require a suitable ground reference, wind plan, emergency options and recovery floor. Ask the candidate to explain how the maneuver differs from a descending steep turn or spin. Observe manufacturer guidance for engine clearing and the prescribed configuration.
steps.student: Demonstrate the applicable coordinated gliding spiral, adjusting bank for wind while controlling airspeed and the radius about the reference. Coach a learner segment, maintain traffic/terrain awareness and recover above the briefed limit.
steps.repetitions: One complete candidate demonstration only when altitude permits the required task; one coached segment. Carry additional circles to a later block instead of consuming recovery margin.
steps.success: Candidate maintains task tolerances, explains wind-dependent bank and energy management, and leaves enough altitude for a normal recovery/return.
errors: Confusing a wind-driven track change with an airspeed problem -> separate bank/radius correction from pitch/airspeed control.
Losing the recovery margin while counting turns -> prioritize recovery over the repetition target.
steps.stop: Recover before the applicable ACS/aircraft floor, engine limitation, traffic conflict or loss of the safe landing option. Do not intentionally shut down a single-engine airplane.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.B; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach power-off accuracy landing and judgment
steps.instructor: Require a touchdown point, wind/energy assessment, approved power/propeller condition and safe landing options. Distinguish task performance assessment from the non-negotiable decision to avoid an unsafe landing.
steps.student: Demonstrate an energy-managed power-off accuracy approach using the aircraft-approved training condition. Coach a learner attempt, explaining path adjustments and configuration timing. Make a landing/go-around decision while adequate options remain.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated attempt and one coached attempt as pattern traffic permits; do not force both into the clock.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable task accuracy when landing safely and can explain why an attempt failed without sacrificing runway safety.
errors: Fixating on the mark and delaying a decision -> broaden the energy/runway scan and choose a safe outcome.
Using a universal idle/propeller rule -> use the aircraft training procedure and Appendix 3 applicability.
steps.stop: Do not force a landing. A safety-driven go-around is always available; record the training/test performance implications separately from the safety decision.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.O and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 9

steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Teach the chandelle as a coordinated climbing reversal
steps.instructor: Have the candidate explain the two halves of the maneuver, the planned bank/pitch progression and expected energy changes. Act as a learner who starts changing bank/pitch at the wrong stage; keep any physical deviation small and safe.
steps.student: Clear the area and use the approved entry condition. Demonstrate the coordinated climbing reversal, narrating the change in pitch and bank through its two halves. Coach an opposite-direction attempt and use a normal transition at completion.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration; one coached opposite-direction attempt; one targeted correction if time remains.
steps.success: Candidate follows the applicable ACS profile, maintains coordination near the low-speed finish, and explains the geometry and energy change without stalling.
errors: Changing bank during the wrong half -> reset the visual reference and teach the sequence before repeating.
Forcing the final pitch instead of recognizing aircraft response -> control angle of attack and finish safely.
steps.stop: Terminate for a stall indication outside the briefed task condition, loss of coordination, aircraft restriction or inadequate practice altitude; return to normal flight.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.C; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach lazy eights through pitch-bank timing and visual references
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose useful visual reference points and describe the changing pitch/bank/airspeed pattern before flying. Role-play a learner who treats each half as a level turn.
steps.student: Demonstrate a coordinated pair of climbing/descending reversals using the selected references. Explain which control and energy trend should be seen at each part of the arc. Coach a learner pair and compare symmetry, altitude, heading and airspeed at completion.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated pair and one coached pair; one short segment repair if the setup remains suitable.
steps.success: Candidate meets task tolerances and teaches smooth, continuously changing control rather than abrupt control checkpoints.
errors: Abruptly chasing a reference point -> restore smooth control changes and look ahead in the maneuver.
Unequal halves without diagnosis -> compare starting conditions and timing before repeating.
steps.stop: Stop for loss of coordination, an unbriefed stall warning, aircraft limitation or excessive flight-path deviation; stabilize before instruction continues.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.D; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach eights on pylons without trading away altitude margin
steps.instructor: Require suitable pylons, a safe operating area, wind assessment and emergency options. Ask the candidate to explain the groundspeed-related pivotal-altitude concept using actual units and the applicable guidance. Never use the exercise to justify unsafe low flight.
steps.student: Demonstrate the approved pylon selection and entry, explain the visual reference movement, and coach a learner through one pair. Adjust the flight path as appropriate while preserving coordination, traffic scan and safe terrain separation.
steps.repetitions: One candidate pair and one coached pair if conditions permit; otherwise complete the explanation and defer the required flight practice.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the intended visual reference relationship without fixation and can explain the effect of groundspeed on the required flight path.
errors: Using one computed altitude regardless of groundspeed -> connect changing groundspeed to the reference movement.
Chasing a pylon downward toward terrain -> abandon the maneuver and select a safer setup.
steps.stop: Exit for unsuitable terrain/pylon spacing, traffic, lack of safe forced-landing options or loss of terrain margin. No universal operational altitude is supplied.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.F; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.

steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.

steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.

Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.

steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.

steps.title: Teach load factor and accelerated-stall recognition
steps.instructor: Use a ground sketch before flight to distinguish bank angle, load factor and angle of attack. Require approved entry configuration and a recovery at the first indication. Ask the candidate to describe a tightening-turn learner error rather than deliberately provoking an excessive load.
steps.student: Clear the area, set the aircraft-approved entry condition, demonstrate the applicable turning entry, and recover at the first stall indication. Explain why the indicated airspeed can be higher than in an unaccelerated stall. Coach one safe repetition.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one supervised coached attempt, with a reset between attempts.
steps.success: Candidate links load factor to stall risk, recognizes the first indication, makes a coordinated recovery, and never relies on an airspeed alone as stall protection.
errors: Confusing bank with load factor in every flight condition -> distinguish a coordinated level turn from unloaded flight.
Continuing to pull after the first cue -> reduce angle of attack promptly and return to controlled flight.
steps.stop: Recovery is at the first indication, not a prolonged/full accelerated stall. Stop for an exceeded load/configuration limit or a recovery-floor threat.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.E and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Demonstrate cross-controlled-stall risk at altitude
steps.instructor: Brief this as an instructor familiarization demonstration, not a pattern exercise for a private learner. Require the aircraft limitations and precise entry/recovery plan. Discuss the base-to-final overshoot scenario while remaining in a safe practice area.
steps.student: Explain how an inappropriate rudder/aileron combination can produce a stall/spin threat. Demonstrate only the authorized ACS/aircraft procedure at a suitable altitude, recover as briefed, and teach a safer overshoot response: maintain control and go around.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration if authorized; two verbal learner-error cases. Do not require the role-play learner to perform this demonstration.
steps.success: Candidate explains the hazard and recognition cues, performs an authorized demonstration/recovery, and teaches avoidance without suggesting a low-altitude reenactment.
errors: Teaching rudder as a way to tighten the base-to-final turn -> teach coordinated flight and a go-around.
Treating absent warning as permission to continue -> use coordination and aerodynamic cues as well as any warning system.
steps.stop: Terminate for incipient spin, unexpected roll/yaw, aircraft restriction or recovery-margin loss. If aircraft authorization is absent, defer the flight demonstration to a suitable aircraft; verbal discussion does not complete a required flight task.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.F and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Demonstrate the elevator-trim-stall mechanism
steps.instructor: On the ground, ask the candidate to explain how approach trim and a power change can produce unexpected pitch. Verify the aircraft-approved configuration and the recovery plan. Observe a demonstration rather than allowing an unbriefed learner surprise.
steps.student: Establish the authorized approach-trim condition at altitude. Explain the pitch response to the prescribed power change, demonstrate the briefed recovery, and then describe the control/trim sequence that prevents the event during a real go-around.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration; one coached, normal go-around-configuration discussion without inducing a second demonstration.
steps.success: Candidate anticipates the pitch tendency, retains positive control and explains why immediate control precedes retrimming.
errors: Relying on trim as the primary flight control -> hold the required attitude with the controls, then trim.
Letting a nose-up tendency develop while explaining -> control or recover first and resume instruction later.
steps.stop: Stop for an unexpected pitch excursion, stall/spin threat, aircraft limitation or inadequate recovery margin. Use the approved procedure; no universal trim or power setting is supplied.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.G and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach secondary-stall prevention during recovery
steps.instructor: Brief that this demonstration includes a full stall under the ACS task, subject to aircraft authorization. Ask the candidate to explain why an overly aggressive recovery can stall the wing again. Keep the exercise distinct from an ordinary learner stall recovery.
steps.student: Demonstrate the authorized secondary-stall sequence and recovery, explaining the renewed angle-of-attack problem. Then teach a normal recovery with controlled pitch/load and appropriate aircraft configuration management.
steps.repetitions: One authorized candidate demonstration, followed by one verbal comparison with a normal recovery.
steps.success: Candidate recognizes the renewed stall, recovers without cascading into another event, and clearly teaches prevention.
errors: Trying to erase altitude loss with an abrupt pull -> recover lift/control before demanding additional load.
Confusing a secondary stall with lingering buffet -> compare the renewed angle-of-attack increase and the aircraft response.
steps.stop: Terminate for unexpected yaw/roll, inability to recover promptly or a threatened recovery floor. Do not continue a chain of stalls for repetition count.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.H and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach unusual-attitude recognition and recovery

steps.repetitions: One nose-high and one nose-low recovery scenario with a complete reset; partial-panel variation only after baseline proficiency.
steps.success: Candidate recognizes the condition promptly, recovers by the applicable procedure and teaches why the chosen control sequence is appropriate.
errors: Moving controls from an unverified instrument impression -> confirm the attitude/trend promptly before the appropriate recovery.
Pulling while a dangerous bank persists -> use the recovery sequence suited to the condition rather than a generic pull-up.
steps.stop: Terminate for an aircraft limit, aggressive control response, recovery-margin threat or suspected actual instrument failure. Restore normal flight before discussing the event.

Continuous instrument fixation -> restore an outside attitude reference and use the instruments to confirm it.
steps.stop: Stop the exercise for uncoordinated control, an unsafe flight path, traffic conflict or loss of role clarity; reestablish ordinary flight before further explanation.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VIII.A-D; AFH chapter 3

steps.title: Teach wind correction through ground-reference maneuvers
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to select a legal, suitable ground reference and explain wind, traffic, emergency landing options and altitude risks. Role-play a learner who corrects drift with rudder instead of a coordinated bank change.
steps.student: Brief and demonstrate a rectangular course, S-turns or turns around a point as assigned. Explain wind-dependent bank changes and reference selection, coach a learner attempt, and compare the aircraft track with the intended ground path.
steps.repetitions: Two selected reference maneuvers: one demonstrated and one coached circuit each; the remaining variant is carried to review if time is insufficient.
steps.success: Candidate maintains applicable ACS limits, keeps an outside scan and teaches the relationship between ground track, wind and bank without fixation on the point.
errors: Fixating on the reference -> restore the traffic/terrain scan and broaden the visual picture.
Using a fixed bank around the entire ground path -> identify where groundspeed changes and adjust coordinated bank.
steps.stop: Leave the exercise for unsuitable terrain/obstructions, people/property risk, traffic, an unavailable emergency option or a breached altitude margin; do not descend to make the diagram look better.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.E; AFH chapter 7

steps.title: Teach coordinated steep turns and workload control
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to brief the applicable bank target, entry speed, power and limitation from the ACS/aircraft documents. Demonstrate a safe learner tendency to lose altitude by discussing it or making only a small recoverable deviation.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the entry condition; demonstrate a coordinated turn in each direction. Explain attitude, back-pressure, power and trim management, then coach a learner through a turn and rollout to the starting heading.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration each direction; one coached attempt in the weaker direction; reset between turns.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable commercial/instructor task standard and diagnoses the cause of altitude/airspeed deviations while retaining coordination and lookout.
errors: Adding more bank to correct an altitude loss -> diagnose the load/attitude problem before the correction.
Rolling out late while explaining -> lead the rollout and divide attention between instruction and the flight path.
steps.stop: Stop for aircraft load/speed limit, loss of coordination, significant flight-path deterioration or traffic conflict. The instructor takes control before the learner error becomes unsafe.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.A; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach normal pattern operations and crosswind judgment
steps.instructor: Let the candidate brief pattern entry, wind correction, runway choice, stabilized approach criteria and a positive control-transfer plan. Act as a learner who overlooks a checklist or misjudges spacing; use a verbal prompt instead of creating an unsafe approach.
steps.student: Teach a normal/crosswind departure and approach using the actual airport procedures. Demonstrate one approach, coach the next, explain workload management and make a planned go-around. Make the landing/go-around decision early enough to preserve options.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration circuit, one coached circuit and one planned go-around as traffic/ATC permit; no forced pattern count.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the airplane within task standards while teaching runway alignment, energy, spacing, communication and a timely go-around.
errors: Talking through final while losing airspeed/alignment -> shorten instruction, regain a stabilized approach or go around.
Treating an ATC instruction as permission to exceed a limit -> request an alternative and protect the aircraft margin.
steps.stop: Go around or discontinue for an unstable approach, unsafe spacing, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or unclear control responsibility. Touch-and-go operations require aircraft/airport authorization.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.A-B and VII.A-B,N; AFH chapters 6, 8-9

steps.title: Teach system-failure recognition and checklist discipline
steps.instructor: Choose two aircraft-applicable scenarios and state which indications are simulated. Require the candidate to distinguish an indication failure from a physical aircraft failure and to justify any checklist selection.
steps.student: Explain the indications, control/flight-path consequences and appropriate aircraft checklist. Teach a role-play learner to prioritize the aircraft, verify the diagnosis, request assistance and decide whether to continue, divert or land.
steps.repetitions: Two verbal/simulated scenarios with no unsafe system disablement; candidate leads one and coaches one.
steps.success: Candidate selects applicable procedures without unsupported memory actions, maintains safe flight and teaches a reasoned landing/diversion decision.
errors: Choosing a checklist from one alarming indication -> cross-check and identify the actual problem.
Pulling a breaker or moving a critical control without authorization -> stop simulation and use the approved aircraft procedure.
steps.stop: Do not create a real malfunction to simulate one. Stop for actual abnormal indications, a prohibited equipment action, workload saturation or loss of flight-path control.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.C; AFH chapter 18; aircraft POH/AFM

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
Candidate recognizes and diagnoses learner errors, intervenes before unsafe flight and provides a justified performance assessment.
Task mastery is based on observed performance; completing the time block or reading the checklist alone does not complete the lesson.

Observed task outcome: Candidate maintains the briefed commercial-level task tolerances while explaining cause and effect, then identifies and corrects a learner deviation without losing the traffic scan.
debrief: Candidate first explains which flight/teaching outcome was strongest and identifies one error with its cause.
Compare trainer evidence with candidate self-assessment; distinguish pilot performance from explanation, learner supervision and risk judgment.
Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.
carryForward: The listed review is a default; replace an equal-time block with a documented weak task before dispatch. Record the replacement in the printed/session notes; a replaced item is not assessed on this flight.

objectives: Teach the named tasks through purpose, setup, demonstration, learner practice and an evidence-based assessment.

steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.

steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit

steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.

errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.

steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.instructor: Assign a briefed VFR route and one verbal change in weather, fuel, airspace or destination availability. Observe the candidate teach position verification, actual aircraft performance and a workable diversion. Role-play a learner who keeps the original destination after its margins deteriorate; do not create an actual emergency or airspace violation.
steps.student: Verify present position and compare actual time/fuel with the preflight plan. Explain the route, airspace, terrain, weather and available landing options; choose a suitable diversion, estimate its fuel/time/performance, request help or an amended ATC instruction when appropriate, then coach the learner through the next safe action.
steps.repetitions: One candidate-led position/fuel check and one coached diversion decision; a verbal destination change is enough when a physical diversion would consume the return reserve.
steps.success: Candidate teaches a defensible continue/divert/land decision using current information and aircraft capability, maintains a safe flight path, and states what would change the decision.
errors: Continuing toward a destination because it was in the original plan -> reassess current weather, fuel, terrain and landing options.
Programming a diversion before securing control and position -> fly, verify position, then manage navigation and communication.
steps.stop: Actual ATC instructions, airspace clearance, weather and aircraft margins govern. End the script if workload, fuel reserve, position uncertainty or a deteriorating landing option threatens the safe return.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 II.G-I, III.C; Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, navigation and aeronautical decision making

steps.title: Teach normal pattern operations and crosswind judgment
steps.instructor: Let the candidate brief pattern entry, wind correction, runway choice, stabilized approach criteria and a positive control-transfer plan. Act as a learner who overlooks a checklist or misjudges spacing; use a verbal prompt instead of creating an unsafe approach.
steps.student: Teach a normal/crosswind departure and approach using the actual airport procedures. Demonstrate one approach, coach the next, explain workload management and make a planned go-around. Make the landing/go-around decision early enough to preserve options.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration circuit, one coached circuit and one planned go-around as traffic/ATC permit; no forced pattern count.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the airplane within task standards while teaching runway alignment, energy, spacing, communication and a timely go-around.
errors: Talking through final while losing airspeed/alignment -> shorten instruction, regain a stabilized approach or go around.
Treating an ATC instruction as permission to exceed a limit -> request an alternative and protect the aircraft margin.
steps.stop: Go around or discontinue for an unstable approach, unsafe spacing, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or unclear control responsibility. Touch-and-go operations require aircraft/airport authorization.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.A-B and VII.A-B,N; AFH chapters 6, 8-9

steps.title: Teach system-failure recognition and checklist discipline
steps.instructor: Choose two aircraft-applicable scenarios and state which indications are simulated. Require the candidate to distinguish an indication failure from a physical aircraft failure and to justify any checklist selection.
steps.student: Explain the indications, control/flight-path consequences and appropriate aircraft checklist. Teach a role-play learner to prioritize the aircraft, verify the diagnosis, request assistance and decide whether to continue, divert or land.
steps.repetitions: Two verbal/simulated scenarios with no unsafe system disablement; candidate leads one and coaches one.
steps.success: Candidate selects applicable procedures without unsupported memory actions, maintains safe flight and teaches a reasoned landing/diversion decision.
errors: Choosing a checklist from one alarming indication -> cross-check and identify the actual problem.
Pulling a breaker or moving a critical control without authorization -> stop simulation and use the approved aircraft procedure.
steps.stop: Do not create a real malfunction to simulate one. Stop for actual abnormal indications, a prohibited equipment action, workload saturation or loss of flight-path control.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.C; AFH chapter 18; aircraft POH/AFM

steps.title: Teach simulated engine failure and landing-option judgment
steps.instructor: Select a safe scenario location with a viable real landing option if power is unavailable. Brief simulation, who moves controls, recovery limits and manufacturer restrictions. Act as a learner who fixates on troubleshooting after maintaining flight-path safety has been established.
steps.student: Maintain aircraft control using the approved glide/performance procedure. Explain landing-area choice and path planning, teach the applicable memory/checklist actions and communications, and recover from the simulation at the agreed safe point.
steps.repetitions: One candidate-led scenario and one coached planning segment; include a change in landing-option quality as a verbal event.
steps.success: Candidate manages energy and a viable landing option first, prioritizes the appropriate checklist/communication, and intervenes before a role-play learner becomes unsafe.
errors: Troubleshooting before establishing the flight path -> fly and secure a landing option first.
Keeping a poor initial landing site after conditions change -> reassess available choices without abrupt low-altitude maneuvering.
steps.stop: No intentional engine shutdown in a single-engine airplane. Terminate while a safe recovery is possible; an actual failure immediately replaces the exercise with the real emergency response.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.B and Appendix 2; AFH chapter 18

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
Candidate recognizes and diagnoses learner errors, intervenes before unsafe flight and provides a justified performance assessment.
Task mastery is based on observed performance; completing the time block or reading the checklist alone does not complete the lesson.

Observed task outcome: Candidate teaches a defensible continue/divert/land decision using current information and aircraft capability, maintains a safe flight path, and states what would change the decision.
debrief: Candidate first explains which flight/teaching outcome was strongest and identifies one error with its cause.
Compare trainer evidence with candidate self-assessment; distinguish pilot performance from explanation, learner supervision and risk judgment.
Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.
carryForward: Repeat a weak mission decision with a new scenario before the practical-test assessment. Extend or defer work when a safe diversion and return will not fit the planned block.
lessons.applicability: Aircraft-neutral instructor guidance. Actual aircraft authority, current rules/standards, weather, terrain and instructor judgment control each flight.

objectives: Teach the named tasks through purpose, setup, demonstration, learner practice and an evidence-based assessment.
Use an independently selected plan and learner-error cases to assess readiness against the applicable current ACS.
Maintain aircraft control, positive flight-control exchanges, traffic protection and aircraft-specific risk/recovery limits while instructing.
prerequisites: Candidate supplies an organized lesson plan and relevant qualification/endorsement records; trainer selects class-applicable tasks.
Before dispatch, enter/brief actual aircraft targets, configuration, authorized simulation methods and task recovery limits from the POH/AFM, current standards and operator procedures.

steps.title: Assess normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Assess independently without coaching new technique; safety intervention ends the assessed attempt. Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error. Assess independently and record errors; do not coach new technique.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the aircraft systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Assess the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Assess independently without coaching new technique; safety intervention ends the assessed attempt. Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope. Assess independently and record errors; do not coach new technique.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Assess normal operations and landing judgment
steps.instructor: Assess without coaching new technique. Select appropriate preflight/start/taxi teaching and at least the required takeoff/landing tasks for the applicant’s class and rating status. Include a stabilized-approach/go-around decision. Record pilot performance, teaching accuracy, learner-error diagnosis and risk decisions separately. Intervene immediately for safety; intervention ends that assessed attempt.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the task, demonstrates while explaining, supervises the trainer acting as learner, identifies the scripted error and states a justified assessment/correction. Maintain checklist discipline, control transfers and outside/flight-path scan throughout.
steps.repetitions: One assessed demonstration and one learner-error case for each selected task; unobserved items remain unobserved.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable task standards, provides effective instruction and identifies a safe learner error without prompting; selected ground tasks are assessed in briefing/preflight/taxi, not counted as airborne practice.
errors: Deviation outside the task standard -> record the evidence and assign remediation; do not coach it into a pass.
Inaccurate explanation or missed learner hazard -> record the teaching deficiency and stop before it becomes an aircraft-control hazard.
steps.stop: Stop for safety intervention, aircraft/clearance limit, traffic or unsuitable conditions. Record deferred tasks separately from unsuccessful tasks; the clock does not grant completion.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V-VII

steps.title: Assess maneuver instruction and risk management
steps.instructor: Assess without coaching new technique. Choose the class-applicable ACS selection after reviewing the candidate’s prior evidence. State which maneuvers are selected and which remain for a later check; do not attempt every option in one block. Record pilot performance, teaching accuracy, learner-error diagnosis and risk decisions separately. Intervene immediately for safety; intervention ends that assessed attempt.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the task, demonstrates while explaining, supervises the trainer acting as learner, identifies the scripted error and states a justified assessment/correction. Maintain checklist discipline, control transfers and outside/flight-path scan throughout.
steps.repetitions: One assessed demonstration and one learner-error case for each selected task; unobserved items remain unobserved.
steps.success: Candidate meets the relevant commercial/instructor standard, explains the task correctly and diagnoses the learner’s error while protecting coordination, traffic and recovery margins.
errors: Deviation outside the task standard -> record the evidence and assign remediation; do not coach it into a pass.
Inaccurate explanation or missed learner hazard -> record the teaching deficiency and stop before it becomes an aircraft-control hazard.
steps.stop: Stop for safety intervention, aircraft/clearance limit, traffic or unsuitable conditions. Record deferred tasks separately from unsuccessful tasks; the clock does not grant completion.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VIII-X

steps.title: Assess abnormal-event instruction and instrument control
steps.instructor: Assess without coaching new technique. Select an aircraft-applicable emergency scenario and an appropriate basic-instrument task. Assess emergency equipment/survival knowledge in the preflight briefing; simulate malfunctions only by approved safe means. Record pilot performance, teaching accuracy, learner-error diagnosis and risk decisions separately. Intervene immediately for safety; intervention ends that assessed attempt.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the task, demonstrates while explaining, supervises the trainer acting as learner, identifies the scripted error and states a justified assessment/correction. Maintain checklist discipline, control transfers and outside/flight-path scan throughout.
steps.repetitions: One assessed demonstration and one learner-error case for each selected task; unobserved items remain unobserved.
steps.success: Candidate prioritizes safe flight, chooses the applicable checklist, teaches the selected instrument/emergency task and makes a defensible landing/diversion decision without coaching.
errors: Deviation outside the task standard -> record the evidence and assign remediation; do not coach it into a pass.
Inaccurate explanation or missed learner hazard -> record the teaching deficiency and stop before it becomes an aircraft-control hazard.
steps.stop: Stop for safety intervention, aircraft/clearance limit, traffic or unsuitable conditions. Record deferred tasks separately from unsuccessful tasks; the clock does not grant completion.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XI-XII

steps.title: Assess return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Assess independently without coaching new technique; safety intervention ends the assessed attempt. Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count. Assess independently and record errors; do not coach new technique.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.instructor: Assess independently without coaching new technique; safety intervention ends the assessed attempt. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up. Assess independently and record errors; do not coach new technique.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.

courses.overview: The student in this route is the instructor candidate; the instructor is the qualified trainer who can role-play a learner. The candidate prepares and teaches a measurable preflight lesson, demonstrates while explaining, supervises practice, diagnoses errors and assesses the result. Timing is an adjustable plan. Aircraft inspection/preparation, parked briefing and debrief are separate from the flight block; flight includes taxi, departure/transit, practice and safe return. Repeat or defer tasks until proficiency is demonstrated, and meet actual regulatory experience/endorsement requirements independently.
entryRequirements: Determine whether this is an initial instrument-instructor application or an additional rating and apply 61.183/61.187/61.191 and the correct PTS scope.
Verify the required pilot/instructor instrument ratings, aircraft category/class, trainer authority and actual-IFR or simulated-IFR legality.
Complete weather, IFR regulations, flight planning, instruments/equipment and records/endorsement preparation before the relevant flight.
When simulated instrument flight is used, brief qualified lookout/control responsibilities and meet the applicable 91.109 requirements; do not restrict the observing pilot’s vision.
For a multiengine applicant/aircraft, determine whether PTS emergency tasks IX.C-D are required; the conditional multiengine lesson becomes applicable required training when those tasks are in scope.

steps.title: Teach instrument checks and taxi clearance
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach stationary/moving instrument checks using the aircraft checklist and verify the real clearance, navigation source and airport diagram. Act as a learner who overlooks a hold-short or source mismatch only through a verbal cue.
steps.student: Candidate explains the instrument checks, clearance route and taxi plan; confirms indications/equipment status, briefs hold-short points and stops for any uncertainty before continuing.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi route with each required aircraft instrument check; no head-down programming while moving.
steps.success: Checks and clearance/airport route are correctly taught; taxi remains under positive control.
errors: Head-down setup while moving -> stop in a safe location before programming.
Check completed without noticing an inconsistent indication -> resolve the indication before dispatch.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for unclear clearance/route, unsafe distraction, abnormal instruments or runway-incursion risk.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E III.C,V.A,X.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach departure and transition to instrument flight
steps.instructor: Confirm who is pilot flying and outside observer; assess the candidate’s teaching of actual clearance, departure path, approved speeds/configuration and view-device timing. Prevent a scenario instruction from replacing the real clearance.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the cleared departure, flies/teaches the approved takeoff and climb, verifies navigation/modes and transitions to instrument exercise only after workload and lookout responsibilities are established.
steps.repetitions: One authorized departure/transit; instrument time begins only under actual qualifying conditions.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the correct path/configuration and establishes a stable instrument scan without losing clearance or lookout protection.
errors: Discussing the lesson while missing a clearance restriction -> fly/comply first and shorten instruction.
Using a view device before a safe observer/control arrangement -> defer device use until responsibilities are clear.
steps.stop: Discontinue the exercise for an actual clearance conflict, control deterioration, unsafe weather/equipment or lookout failure.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B,VI; aircraft departure checklist; 91.109 as applicable

steps.title: Teach basic instrument control and changes of airspeed
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to teach control/performance or primary/supporting technique using the actual instrument presentation. Act as a learner who overcontrols a small error; require concise feedback that reconnects attitude/power with the desired flight path.
steps.student: Teach level flight and turns, then change airspeed while preserving the path. Demonstrate constant-airspeed and constant-rate climbs/descents, explaining which parameter is controlled and which instrument trend verifies it. Coach an integrated learner sequence.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one focused repeat of an unstable transition.
steps.success: Candidate flies to the applicable instrument skill standard while giving accurate instruction and correcting scan/control errors before they grow.
errors: Changing pitch and power repeatedly without waiting for the result -> make a purposeful change, observe and refine.
Confusing constant rate with constant airspeed -> restate the assigned target and use the appropriate controlling indication.
steps.stop: End simulated instrument conditions for traffic/lookout failure, control deterioration, disorientation or an aircraft limitation. Maintain a clearly briefed pilot flying and outside observer.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VI.A-E; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Teach IFR clearances and procedure compliance
steps.instructor: Assign a realistic clearance and observe the candidate teach copying, readback, route/altitude interpretation and avionics setup. Act as a learner who accepts an ambiguous instruction; require a clarification request instead of an assumption.
steps.student: Explain the clearance limit and applicable departure/en-route/arrival path, verify chart/NOTAM/equipment suitability, set and cross-check the navigation, and teach compliance through one amended clearance. Use simulated clearances only when their status is explicitly announced.
steps.repetitions: One complete clearance briefing and one amendment; fly the applicable procedure segment when authorized.
steps.success: Candidate teaches an accurate clearance interpretation, anticipates the next restriction and seeks clarification before uncertainty changes the flight path.
errors: Reading back correctly but programming a different route -> compare the clearance, chart and active navigation.
Assuming a clearance removes a published restriction without justification -> clarify and apply the current rules/procedure.
steps.stop: No unapproved route/altitude deviation for a training script. Actual ATC instructions and aircraft limitations govern; request an alternative when unable.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapters 1-3

steps.title: Complete a supported approach or visual return
steps.instructor: Require a current return/approach briefing, aircraft category/equipment, minima if applicable and a missed/landing plan. Observe the candidate’s final coaching and protect against fixation on the lesson timer.
steps.student: Candidate teaches the authorized return, approach or visual pattern, confirms active guidance and approved configuration, makes the landing/missed decision and maintains positive control through rollout.
steps.repetitions: One final supported approach/landing or authorized missed/visual alternative; no forced extra approach.
steps.success: Actual ATC, approach/visual rules and aircraft limits are respected; teaching stays concise during high workload.
errors: Trying to finish an explanation below an appropriate workload gate -> fly the approach and discuss later.
Unstable approach or unmet visual conditions -> execute the safe authorized missed/go-around.
steps.stop: Miss/go around or use the authorized alternative for unstable flight, invalid guidance, unmet required references or runway conflict.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII; current charts and aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E X.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
