steps.title: Teach instrument checks and taxi clearance
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach stationary/moving instrument checks using the aircraft checklist and verify the real clearance, navigation source and airport diagram. Act as a learner who overlooks a hold-short or source mismatch only through a verbal cue.
steps.student: Candidate explains the instrument checks, clearance route and taxi plan; confirms indications/equipment status, briefs hold-short points and stops for any uncertainty before continuing.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi route with each required aircraft instrument check; no head-down programming while moving.
steps.success: Checks and clearance/airport route are correctly taught; taxi remains under positive control.
errors: Head-down setup while moving -> stop in a safe location before programming.
Check completed without noticing an inconsistent indication -> resolve the indication before dispatch.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for unclear clearance/route, unsafe distraction, abnormal instruments or runway-incursion risk.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E III.C,V.A,X.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach departure and transition to instrument flight
steps.instructor: Confirm who is pilot flying and outside observer; assess the candidate’s teaching of actual clearance, departure path, approved speeds/configuration and view-device timing. Prevent a scenario instruction from replacing the real clearance.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the cleared departure, flies/teaches the approved takeoff and climb, verifies navigation/modes and transitions to instrument exercise only after workload and lookout responsibilities are established.
steps.repetitions: One authorized departure/transit; instrument time begins only under actual qualifying conditions.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the correct path/configuration and establishes a stable instrument scan without losing clearance or lookout protection.
errors: Discussing the lesson while missing a clearance restriction -> fly/comply first and shorten instruction.
Using a view device before a safe observer/control arrangement -> defer device use until responsibilities are clear.
steps.stop: Discontinue the exercise for an actual clearance conflict, control deterioration, unsafe weather/equipment or lookout failure.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B,VI; aircraft departure checklist; 91.109 as applicable

steps.title: Teach basic instrument control and changes of airspeed
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to teach control/performance or primary/supporting technique using the actual instrument presentation. Act as a learner who overcontrols a small error; require concise feedback that reconnects attitude/power with the desired flight path.
steps.student: Teach level flight and turns, then change airspeed while preserving the path. Demonstrate constant-airspeed and constant-rate climbs/descents, explaining which parameter is controlled and which instrument trend verifies it. Coach an integrated learner sequence.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one focused repeat of an unstable transition.
steps.success: Candidate flies to the applicable instrument skill standard while giving accurate instruction and correcting scan/control errors before they grow.
errors: Changing pitch and power repeatedly without waiting for the result -> make a purposeful change, observe and refine.
Confusing constant rate with constant airspeed -> restate the assigned target and use the appropriate controlling indication.
steps.stop: End simulated instrument conditions for traffic/lookout failure, control deterioration, disorientation or an aircraft limitation. Maintain a clearly briefed pilot flying and outside observer.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VI.A-E; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Teach timed turns and compass-heading errors
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to explain actual compass behavior, heading source limitations and rate/time planning. Use the aircraft indications and current handbook technique; do not invent universal lead/lag values for an unfamiliar instrument.
steps.student: Teach a timed heading change at the selected authorized turn rate. Compare expected time and actual heading, then explain compass acceleration/turning effects and how a learner can cross-check the result.
steps.repetitions: Two timed heading changes in opposite directions; one verbal compass-error case.
steps.success: Candidate teaches a valid time/rate method, makes appropriate heading corrections and distinguishes instrument error from control error.
errors: Starting the clock before establishing turn rate -> establish the rate and define a consistent timing point.
Chasing compass movement in turbulence -> maintain control and interpret the indication using the appropriate technique.
steps.stop: Stop for unreliable attitude information, unsafe bank, workload saturation or loss of an outside lookout during simulation; restore the best available safe control method.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VI.F; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Teach instrument steep turns
steps.instructor: Have the candidate brief the applicable instrument task standard and aircraft limitations. Role-play an altitude/scan error only within a safe envelope; assess whether the candidate identifies the cause instead of issuing many unrelated commands.
steps.student: Clear the area with the observing pilot; demonstrate coordinated instrument steep turns in each direction. Teach the attitude, power and scan changes, then coach the learner through a turn and controlled rollout.
steps.repetitions: One demonstrated turn each direction; one coached turn in the weaker direction.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the instrument task standard while giving concise teaching and preserving coordination and outside collision protection.
errors: Bank fixation while altitude diverges -> reconnect the attitude/performance cross-check.
Abrupt rollout during an explanation -> anticipate the heading and make a smooth transition.
steps.stop: Discontinue for control deterioration, aircraft limit, traffic or an inadequate outside scan. Safety intervention ends the assessed attempt.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VI.G; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Complete a supported approach or visual return
steps.instructor: Require a current return/approach briefing, aircraft category/equipment, minima if applicable and a missed/landing plan. Observe the candidate’s final coaching and protect against fixation on the lesson timer.
steps.student: Candidate teaches the authorized return, approach or visual pattern, confirms active guidance and approved configuration, makes the landing/missed decision and maintains positive control through rollout.
steps.repetitions: One final supported approach/landing or authorized missed/visual alternative; no forced extra approach.
steps.success: Actual ATC, approach/visual rules and aircraft limits are respected; teaching stays concise during high workload.
errors: Trying to finish an explanation below an appropriate workload gate -> fly the approach and discuss later.
Unstable approach or unmet visual conditions -> execute the safe authorized missed/go-around.
steps.stop: Miss/go around or use the authorized alternative for unstable flight, invalid guidance, unmet required references or runway conflict.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII; current charts and aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E X.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

steps.title: Teach instrument unusual attitudes and failure recognition

steps.success: Candidate teaches a prompt, correctly prioritized recovery and detects misleading indications without losing control.

steps.stop: End the simulation for actual equipment malfunction, uncontrolled attitude, aircraft limit or insufficient altitude margin. Restore full visual references when required for safety.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VI.H; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.student: Cross-check reliable sources, stabilize control, select appropriate navigation/approach equipment and teach a supported approach with the remaining indications. Coach a learner transition, request assistance as appropriate and explain why a different approach or landing may be safer.
steps.repetitions: One failure-recognition transition and one supported approach segment; complete a full required approach when routing/time permits or carry it forward.
steps.success: Candidate identifies the simulated loss, maintains instrument control and gives clear, equipment-applicable instruction through a safe approach decision.
errors: Continuing to follow a failed display -> identify reliable independent indications and change the scan.
Choosing an approach unsupported by remaining equipment -> select a supported alternative or discontinue.
steps.stop: End simulation for actual system failure, loss of reliable attitude/control, unsupported navigation or unsafe workload. Restore the simulated indication or visual references when needed for safety.

steps.stop: Discontinue for unreliable/unidentified navigation, unsafe workload or a route conflict. Never invent a procedure or substitute unsupported equipment for a required demonstration.

steps.title: Teach a hold from clearance to exit
steps.instructor: Assign a complete hold clearance and ask the candidate to teach fix, direction, turns, leg limit, altitude, entry, speed and expected clearance time. Act as a learner who reverses the inbound course or overlooks a restriction.
steps.student: Brief the protected holding geometry and aircraft/procedure limits, enter the hold, establish the outbound correction and adjust the next inbound leg using observed wind. Coach a second circuit and teach an orderly clearance-compliant exit.
steps.repetitions: One candidate-led entry and circuit; one coached circuit; one exit/amendment discussion.
steps.success: Candidate teaches a valid entry/holding plan, respects limits and manages wind corrections and clearance status without losing aircraft control.
errors: Selecting an entry without understanding the inbound leg -> draw/brief the geometry before crossing the fix.
Programming the hold but failing to verify turn direction or leg limit -> compare the active hold with the clearance.
steps.stop: Do not exceed clearance/procedure protection to finish a demonstration. Exit or request amended clearance if equipment, weather, fuel or workload makes the hold unsuitable.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VII.B; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapter 2

steps.title: Teach IFR clearances and procedure compliance
steps.instructor: Assign a realistic clearance and observe the candidate teach copying, readback, route/altitude interpretation and avionics setup. Act as a learner who accepts an ambiguous instruction; require a clarification request instead of an assumption.
steps.student: Explain the clearance limit and applicable departure/en-route/arrival path, verify chart/NOTAM/equipment suitability, set and cross-check the navigation, and teach compliance through one amended clearance. Use simulated clearances only when their status is explicitly announced.
steps.repetitions: One complete clearance briefing and one amendment; fly the applicable procedure segment when authorized.
steps.success: Candidate teaches an accurate clearance interpretation, anticipates the next restriction and seeks clarification before uncertainty changes the flight path.
errors: Reading back correctly but programming a different route -> compare the clearance, chart and active navigation.
Assuming a clearance removes a published restriction without justification -> clarify and apply the current rules/procedure.
steps.stop: No unapproved route/altitude deviation for a training script. Actual ATC instructions and aircraft limitations govern; request an alternative when unable.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapters 1-3

steps.title: Complete a supported approach or visual return
steps.instructor: Require a current return/approach briefing, aircraft category/equipment, minima if applicable and a missed/landing plan. Observe the candidate’s final coaching and protect against fixation on the lesson timer.
steps.student: Candidate teaches the authorized return, approach or visual pattern, confirms active guidance and approved configuration, makes the landing/missed decision and maintains positive control through rollout.
steps.repetitions: One final supported approach/landing or authorized missed/visual alternative; no forced extra approach.
steps.success: Actual ATC, approach/visual rules and aircraft limits are respected; teaching stays concise during high workload.
errors: Trying to finish an explanation below an appropriate workload gate -> fly the approach and discuss later.
Unstable approach or unmet visual conditions -> execute the safe authorized missed/go-around.
steps.stop: Miss/go around or use the authorized alternative for unstable flight, invalid guidance, unmet required references or runway conflict.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII; current charts and aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E X.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

steps.title: Teach instrument checks and taxi clearance
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach stationary/moving instrument checks using the aircraft checklist and verify the real clearance, navigation source and airport diagram. Act as a learner who overlooks a hold-short or source mismatch only through a verbal cue.
steps.student: Candidate explains the instrument checks, clearance route and taxi plan; confirms indications/equipment status, briefs hold-short points and stops for any uncertainty before continuing.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi route with each required aircraft instrument check; no head-down programming while moving.
steps.success: Checks and clearance/airport route are correctly taught; taxi remains under positive control.
errors: Head-down setup while moving -> stop in a safe location before programming.
Check completed without noticing an inconsistent indication -> resolve the indication before dispatch.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for unclear clearance/route, unsafe distraction, abnormal instruments or runway-incursion risk.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E III.C,V.A,X.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach departure and transition to instrument flight
steps.instructor: Confirm who is pilot flying and outside observer; assess the candidate’s teaching of actual clearance, departure path, approved speeds/configuration and view-device timing. Prevent a scenario instruction from replacing the real clearance.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the cleared departure, flies/teaches the approved takeoff and climb, verifies navigation/modes and transitions to instrument exercise only after workload and lookout responsibilities are established.
steps.repetitions: One authorized departure/transit; instrument time begins only under actual qualifying conditions.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the correct path/configuration and establishes a stable instrument scan without losing clearance or lookout protection.
errors: Discussing the lesson while missing a clearance restriction -> fly/comply first and shorten instruction.
Using a view device before a safe observer/control arrangement -> defer device use until responsibilities are clear.
steps.stop: Discontinue the exercise for an actual clearance conflict, control deterioration, unsafe weather/equipment or lookout failure.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B,VI; aircraft departure checklist; 91.109 as applicable

steps.title: Teach a nonprecision approach and descent planning
steps.instructor: Require a full approach briefing using current charts/NOTAMs, aircraft category, equipment and minima. Observe the candidate teach course/altitude restrictions, descent planning, missed approach and the required visual transition. Role-play one misidentified waypoint verbally.
steps.student: Verify source/mode and active procedure, fly the cleared approach, teach the applicable minimum altitude and descent method, and monitor the lateral/vertical path. At the decision point, teach the appropriate missed approach or a legal visual transition.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one coached approach if routing permits; otherwise one approach with a detailed diagnosis and carry-forward.
steps.success: Candidate teaches a current, properly briefed procedure, respects every applicable restriction and makes a timely, lawful missed/landing decision.
errors: Using a displayed advisory glidepath as permission below a minimum -> explain its status and respect the published/regulatory limits.
Delaying the missed approach while searching for references -> act at the briefed decision point.
steps.stop: Miss or discontinue for an unstable approach, wrong source/leg, prohibited descent, loss of required guidance or an unmet visual requirement. Published procedures and actual ATC govern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII.A; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapter 4

steps.title: Teach a missed approach as an immediate aircraft-control task
steps.instructor: Prebrief the aircraft transition, climb capability, initial path, sequencing and actual ATC instructions. Assign a missed approach at the briefed point; assess whether the candidate manages flight control before lengthy explanation or programming.
steps.student: Initiate the approved climb/configuration transition, follow the authorized missed path and communicate appropriately. Teach the learner how to confirm navigation sequencing while maintaining control and obstacle clearance, then accept the next clearance only when ready.
steps.repetitions: One candidate-led missed approach and one coached missed/transition, subject to ATC and traffic.
steps.success: Candidate teaches and executes a prompt, controlled transition with correct path, configuration and communications.
errors: Programming before establishing the climb -> fly the transition first, then verify navigation.
Turning before the procedure permits -> remain on the authorized path and verify the missed instructions.
steps.stop: Actual clearance, aircraft performance and obstacle protection govern. Stop the training script for a climb-performance threat, mode uncertainty or excessive workload and use the safest authorized alternative.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII.C; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapter 4

steps.stop: Miss for guidance failure, an unstable path, unmet visual conditions or an aircraft/procedure restriction. Never descend on an invalid or unverified vertical path.

steps.title: Teach instrument checks and taxi clearance
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach stationary/moving instrument checks using the aircraft checklist and verify the real clearance, navigation source and airport diagram. Act as a learner who overlooks a hold-short or source mismatch only through a verbal cue.
steps.student: Candidate explains the instrument checks, clearance route and taxi plan; confirms indications/equipment status, briefs hold-short points and stops for any uncertainty before continuing.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi route with each required aircraft instrument check; no head-down programming while moving.
steps.success: Checks and clearance/airport route are correctly taught; taxi remains under positive control.
errors: Head-down setup while moving -> stop in a safe location before programming.
Check completed without noticing an inconsistent indication -> resolve the indication before dispatch.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for unclear clearance/route, unsafe distraction, abnormal instruments or runway-incursion risk.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E III.C,V.A,X.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach departure and transition to instrument flight
steps.instructor: Confirm who is pilot flying and outside observer; assess the candidate’s teaching of actual clearance, departure path, approved speeds/configuration and view-device timing. Prevent a scenario instruction from replacing the real clearance.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the cleared departure, flies/teaches the approved takeoff and climb, verifies navigation/modes and transitions to instrument exercise only after workload and lookout responsibilities are established.
steps.repetitions: One authorized departure/transit; instrument time begins only under actual qualifying conditions.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the correct path/configuration and establishes a stable instrument scan without losing clearance or lookout protection.
errors: Discussing the lesson while missing a clearance restriction -> fly/comply first and shorten instruction.
Using a view device before a safe observer/control arrangement -> defer device use until responsibilities are clear.
steps.stop: Discontinue the exercise for an actual clearance conflict, control deterioration, unsafe weather/equipment or lookout failure.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B,VI; aircraft departure checklist; 91.109 as applicable

steps.title: Teach IFR clearances and procedure compliance
steps.instructor: Assign a realistic clearance and observe the candidate teach copying, readback, route/altitude interpretation and avionics setup. Act as a learner who accepts an ambiguous instruction; require a clarification request instead of an assumption.
steps.student: Explain the clearance limit and applicable departure/en-route/arrival path, verify chart/NOTAM/equipment suitability, set and cross-check the navigation, and teach compliance through one amended clearance. Use simulated clearances only when their status is explicitly announced.
steps.repetitions: One complete clearance briefing and one amendment; fly the applicable procedure segment when authorized.
steps.success: Candidate teaches an accurate clearance interpretation, anticipates the next restriction and seeks clarification before uncertainty changes the flight path.
errors: Reading back correctly but programming a different route -> compare the clearance, chart and active navigation.
Assuming a clearance removes a published restriction without justification -> clarify and apply the current rules/procedure.
steps.stop: No unapproved route/altitude deviation for a training script. Actual ATC instructions and aircraft limitations govern; request an alternative when unable.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapters 1-3

steps.title: Teach a hold from clearance to exit
steps.instructor: Assign a complete hold clearance and ask the candidate to teach fix, direction, turns, leg limit, altitude, entry, speed and expected clearance time. Act as a learner who reverses the inbound course or overlooks a restriction.
steps.student: Brief the protected holding geometry and aircraft/procedure limits, enter the hold, establish the outbound correction and adjust the next inbound leg using observed wind. Coach a second circuit and teach an orderly clearance-compliant exit.
steps.repetitions: One candidate-led entry and circuit; one coached circuit; one exit/amendment discussion.
steps.success: Candidate teaches a valid entry/holding plan, respects limits and manages wind corrections and clearance status without losing aircraft control.
errors: Selecting an entry without understanding the inbound leg -> draw/brief the geometry before crossing the fix.
Programming the hold but failing to verify turn direction or leg limit -> compare the active hold with the clearance.
steps.stop: Do not exceed clearance/procedure protection to finish a demonstration. Exit or request amended clearance if equipment, weather, fuel or workload makes the hold unsuitable.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VII.B; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapter 2

steps.title: Teach approach continuation with lost primary indications
steps.instructor: Brief exactly which indications are simulated failed and which remain reliable. Use approved simulation methods; never disable an essential system without explicit authority. Require the candidate to teach failure identification and a workload-reduction/diversion plan.
steps.student: Cross-check reliable sources, stabilize control, select appropriate navigation/approach equipment and teach a supported approach with the remaining indications. Coach a learner transition, request assistance as appropriate and explain why a different approach or landing may be safer.
steps.repetitions: One failure-recognition transition and one supported approach segment; complete a full required approach when routing/time permits or carry it forward.
steps.success: Candidate identifies the simulated loss, maintains instrument control and gives clear, equipment-applicable instruction through a safe approach decision.
errors: Continuing to follow a failed display -> identify reliable independent indications and change the scan.
Choosing an approach unsupported by remaining equipment -> select a supported alternative or discontinue.
steps.stop: End simulation for actual system failure, loss of reliable attitude/control, unsupported navigation or unsafe workload. Restore the simulated indication or visual references when needed for safety.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E IX.B; Instrument Flying Handbook; aircraft equipment supplements

steps.title: Teach a loss-of-communications decision without guessing clearance
steps.instructor: Use a prebriefed scenario card and clearly distinguish simulated silence from a real radio failure. Ask the candidate to teach VMC/IMC decision differences, troubleshooting, route/altitude and clearance-limit reasoning using current references.
steps.student: Maintain aircraft control; verify the simulated failure; identify available communication alternatives; explain and apply the appropriate rule/procedure to the scenario. Teach how current weather, fuel and landing options affect the decision.
steps.repetitions: One VMC and one IMC verbal scenario while following the actual authorized flight path; do not intentionally stop complying with ATC.
steps.success: Candidate gives a regulation-supported route/altitude/landing plan, maintains flight control and does not confuse a scenario clearance with the real clearance.
errors: Reciting a mnemonic without resolving the clearance limit -> work through the actual clearance and rule.
Changing route during a pretend radio failure -> keep actual ATC compliance while discussing the simulated decision.
steps.stop: Actual communications failure or clearance uncertainty ends role-play. Apply current rules and available assistance; do not deviate merely to enact a scenario.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E IX.A; current 14 CFR 91.185 and AIM

steps.title: Complete a supported approach or visual return
steps.instructor: Require a current return/approach briefing, aircraft category/equipment, minima if applicable and a missed/landing plan. Observe the candidate’s final coaching and protect against fixation on the lesson timer.
steps.student: Candidate teaches the authorized return, approach or visual pattern, confirms active guidance and approved configuration, makes the landing/missed decision and maintains positive control through rollout.
steps.repetitions: One final supported approach/landing or authorized missed/visual alternative; no forced extra approach.
steps.success: Actual ATC, approach/visual rules and aircraft limits are respected; teaching stays concise during high workload.
errors: Trying to finish an explanation below an appropriate workload gate -> fly the approach and discuss later.
Unstable approach or unmet visual conditions -> execute the safe authorized missed/go-around.
steps.stop: Miss/go around or use the authorized alternative for unstable flight, invalid guidance, unmet required references or runway conflict.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII; current charts and aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E X.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
Candidate recognizes and diagnoses learner errors, intervenes before unsafe flight and provides a justified performance assessment.
Task mastery is based on observed performance; completing the time block or reading the checklist alone does not complete the lesson.
Observed task outcome: Candidate teaches an accurate clearance interpretation, anticipates the next restriction and seeks clarification before uncertainty changes the flight path.
debrief: Candidate first explains which flight/teaching outcome was strongest and identifies one error with its cause.
Compare trainer evidence with candidate self-assessment; distinguish pilot performance from explanation, learner supervision and risk judgment.
Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.
carryForward: If a complete required partial-panel approach cannot be flown, record it as deferred and plan a dedicated follow-up.
lessons.applicability: Aircraft-neutral instructor guidance. Actual aircraft authority, current rules/standards, weather, terrain and instructor judgment control each flight.

lessons.summary: Build a pilot-specific IPC plan from current requirements, then teach selected instrument-control/navigation/approach segments and identify every remaining required observation.
objectives: Teach the named tasks through purpose, setup, demonstration, learner practice and an evidence-based assessment.
Build a pilot-specific IPC plan from current requirements, then teach selected instrument-control/navigation/approach segments and identify every remaining required observation.
Maintain aircraft control, positive flight-control exchanges, traffic protection and aircraft-specific risk/recovery limits while instructing.
prerequisites: Review 61.57(d), current Instrument Rating ACS IPC table and aircraft/device credit limits; interview the role-play pilot about recency and operation.
Before dispatch, enter/brief actual aircraft targets, configuration, authorized simulation methods and task recovery limits from the POH/AFM, current standards and operator procedures.
Use the separate preflight budget for inspection, documents/equipment and current weather/NOTAM/performance checks; do not count this as airborne practice.

steps.title: Teach basic instrument control and changes of airspeed
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to teach control/performance or primary/supporting technique using the actual instrument presentation. Act as a learner who overcontrols a small error; require concise feedback that reconnects attitude/power with the desired flight path.
steps.student: Teach level flight and turns, then change airspeed while preserving the path. Demonstrate constant-airspeed and constant-rate climbs/descents, explaining which parameter is controlled and which instrument trend verifies it. Coach an integrated learner sequence.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one focused repeat of an unstable transition.
steps.success: Candidate flies to the applicable instrument skill standard while giving accurate instruction and correcting scan/control errors before they grow.
errors: Changing pitch and power repeatedly without waiting for the result -> make a purposeful change, observe and refine.
Confusing constant rate with constant airspeed -> restate the assigned target and use the appropriate controlling indication.
steps.stop: End simulated instrument conditions for traffic/lookout failure, control deterioration, disorientation or an aircraft limitation. Maintain a clearly briefed pilot flying and outside observer.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VI.A-E; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Teach intercepts, tracking and DME-arc principles
steps.instructor: Require identification/integrity checks of the selected navigation source and a briefing of the intended intercept/track. Change only a simulated wind or a safe assignment; ask the candidate to diagnose the effect on course tracking.
steps.student: Demonstrate intercepting and tracking with the aircraft’s authorized ground-based or satellite source. Teach wind correction and source/mode verification. When DME-arc practice is applicable and available, explain distance control, lead points and station geometry before coaching a segment.
steps.repetitions: One intercept and tracking segment for each available required source; one DME-arc segment if applicable; carry unavailable equipment work to an appropriate aircraft/device.
steps.success: Candidate teaches source selection, course/distance control and wind correction while meeting the applicable instrument standard.
errors: Using the wrong CDI/navigation source -> verify the selected source and active leg before correction.
Chasing displacement with repeated large heading changes -> use a reasoned intercept and refine the wind correction.
steps.stop: Discontinue for unreliable/unidentified navigation, unsafe workload or a route conflict. Never invent a procedure or substitute unsupported equipment for a required demonstration.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VII.A; Instrument Flying Handbook; Instrument Procedures Handbook

steps.title: Teach a nonprecision approach and descent planning
steps.instructor: Require a full approach briefing using current charts/NOTAMs, aircraft category, equipment and minima. Observe the candidate teach course/altitude restrictions, descent planning, missed approach and the required visual transition. Role-play one misidentified waypoint verbally.
steps.student: Verify source/mode and active procedure, fly the cleared approach, teach the applicable minimum altitude and descent method, and monitor the lateral/vertical path. At the decision point, teach the appropriate missed approach or a legal visual transition.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one coached approach if routing permits; otherwise one approach with a detailed diagnosis and carry-forward.
steps.success: Candidate teaches a current, properly briefed procedure, respects every applicable restriction and makes a timely, lawful missed/landing decision.
errors: Using a displayed advisory glidepath as permission below a minimum -> explain its status and respect the published/regulatory limits.
Delaying the missed approach while searching for references -> act at the briefed decision point.
steps.stop: Miss or discontinue for an unstable approach, wrong source/leg, prohibited descent, loss of required guidance or an unmet visual requirement. Published procedures and actual ATC govern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII.A; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapter 4

steps.title: Teach precision/vertical-guidance approach management
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to identify the exact approach type and available guidance; do not label every GPS vertical path a precision approach. Brief mode capture, minima, missed procedure and required equipment.
steps.student: Demonstrate source/mode verification, interception and tracking of the required lateral/vertical guidance. Coach the learner through configuration, stabilized descent and the approach decision, while explaining the indicated trend rather than issuing disconnected corrections.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one coached approach when available; verify the actual PTS-required approach equipment/type before claiming task coverage.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the applicable approach accurately, maintains task limits and chooses missed approach or legal landing at the correct point.
errors: Assuming the armed mode is active guidance -> confirm capture/annunciation and actual course response.
Treating LPV, LNAV/VNAV and ILS as interchangeable -> identify the procedure type and applicable task requirements.
steps.stop: Miss for guidance failure, an unstable path, unmet visual conditions or an aircraft/procedure restriction. Never descend on an invalid or unverified vertical path.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII.B; Instrument Procedures Handbook chapter 4

steps.student: Candidate briefs the task, demonstrates while explaining, supervises the trainer acting as learner, identifies the scripted error and states a justified assessment/correction. Maintain checklist discipline, control transfers and outside/flight-path scan throughout.

Inaccurate explanation or missed learner hazard -> record the teaching deficiency and stop before it becomes an aircraft-control hazard.

steps.title: Teach instrument checks and taxi clearance
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach stationary/moving instrument checks using the aircraft checklist and verify the real clearance, navigation source and airport diagram. Act as a learner who overlooks a hold-short or source mismatch only through a verbal cue.
steps.student: Candidate explains the instrument checks, clearance route and taxi plan; confirms indications/equipment status, briefs hold-short points and stops for any uncertainty before continuing.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi route with each required aircraft instrument check; no head-down programming while moving.
steps.success: Checks and clearance/airport route are correctly taught; taxi remains under positive control.
errors: Head-down setup while moving -> stop in a safe location before programming.
Check completed without noticing an inconsistent indication -> resolve the indication before dispatch.
steps.stop: Stop taxi for unclear clearance/route, unsafe distraction, abnormal instruments or runway-incursion risk.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E III.C,V.A,X.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach departure and transition to instrument flight
steps.instructor: Confirm who is pilot flying and outside observer; assess the candidate’s teaching of actual clearance, departure path, approved speeds/configuration and view-device timing. Prevent a scenario instruction from replacing the real clearance.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the cleared departure, flies/teaches the approved takeoff and climb, verifies navigation/modes and transitions to instrument exercise only after workload and lookout responsibilities are established.
steps.repetitions: One authorized departure/transit; instrument time begins only under actual qualifying conditions.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the correct path/configuration and establishes a stable instrument scan without losing clearance or lookout protection.
errors: Discussing the lesson while missing a clearance restriction -> fly/comply first and shorten instruction.
Using a view device before a safe observer/control arrangement -> defer device use until responsibilities are clear.
steps.stop: Discontinue the exercise for an actual clearance conflict, control deterioration, unsafe weather/equipment or lookout failure.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E V.A-B,VI; aircraft departure checklist; 91.109 as applicable

steps.title: Teach multiengine instrument control and OEI approach
steps.instructor: Use an appropriately rated trainer and a suitable multiengine airplane. Verify IFR/engine-out equipment and performance, approved simulation/zero-thrust values and safe recovery/landing options. Require the candidate to brief the one-engine approach and communications implications.
steps.student: Teach recognition and control of a simulated engine failure during instrument straight flight/turns. Identify/verify using the aircraft procedure, reduce workload and fly a supported approach with the approved OEI profile. Coach the learner through a decision to land or use the prebriefed safe alternative.
steps.repetitions: One instrument OEI control sequence and one supported OEI approach; do not force a second approach into the block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches instrument control and the aircraft-specific failure/approach sequence while respecting guidance, minima and performance limits.
errors: Diagnosing the engine while the instrument path deteriorates -> stabilize control first.
Assuming an OEI missed approach is available -> verify aircraft performance and brief a safe alternative before dispatch.
steps.stop: Multiengine only. Terminate for unreliable indications, wrong-engine selection, control/airspeed-margin loss or unsupported OEI climb/approach. Any actual failure replaces simulation with the aircraft emergency procedure.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E IX.C-D; AFH chapter 13; Instrument Procedures Handbook

steps.title: Teach a loss-of-communications decision without guessing clearance
steps.instructor: Use a prebriefed scenario card and clearly distinguish simulated silence from a real radio failure. Ask the candidate to teach VMC/IMC decision differences, troubleshooting, route/altitude and clearance-limit reasoning using current references.
steps.student: Maintain aircraft control; verify the simulated failure; identify available communication alternatives; explain and apply the appropriate rule/procedure to the scenario. Teach how current weather, fuel and landing options affect the decision.
steps.repetitions: One VMC and one IMC verbal scenario while following the actual authorized flight path; do not intentionally stop complying with ATC.
steps.success: Candidate gives a regulation-supported route/altitude/landing plan, maintains flight control and does not confuse a scenario clearance with the real clearance.
errors: Reciting a mnemonic without resolving the clearance limit -> work through the actual clearance and rule.
Changing route during a pretend radio failure -> keep actual ATC compliance while discussing the simulated decision.
steps.stop: Actual communications failure or clearance uncertainty ends role-play. Apply current rules and available assistance; do not deviate merely to enact a scenario.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E IX.A; current 14 CFR 91.185 and AIM

steps.title: Complete a supported approach or visual return
steps.instructor: Require a current return/approach briefing, aircraft category/equipment, minima if applicable and a missed/landing plan. Observe the candidate’s final coaching and protect against fixation on the lesson timer.
steps.student: Candidate teaches the authorized return, approach or visual pattern, confirms active guidance and approved configuration, makes the landing/missed decision and maintains positive control through rollout.
steps.repetitions: One final supported approach/landing or authorized missed/visual alternative; no forced extra approach.
steps.success: Actual ATC, approach/visual rules and aircraft limits are respected; teaching stays concise during high workload.
errors: Trying to finish an explanation below an appropriate workload gate -> fly the approach and discuss later.
Unstable approach or unmet visual conditions -> execute the safe authorized missed/go-around.
steps.stop: Miss/go around or use the authorized alternative for unstable flight, invalid guidance, unmet required references or runway conflict.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E VIII; current charts and aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-8081-9E X.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

courses.overview: The student in this route is the instructor candidate; the instructor is the qualified trainer who can role-play a learner. The candidate prepares and teaches a measurable preflight lesson, demonstrates while explaining, supervises practice, diagnoses errors and assesses the result. Timing is an adjustable plan. Aircraft inspection/preparation, parked briefing and debrief are separate from the flight block; flight includes taxi, departure/transit, practice and safe return. Repeat or defer tasks until proficiency is demonstrated, and meet actual regulatory experience/endorsement requirements independently.
entryRequirements: This route is for an initial airplane multiengine instructor applicant; verify 61.183/61.187 eligibility and a trainer qualified under 61.195 for initial instructor training.

Initial airplane-instructor spin-training/endorsement applicability under 61.183(i) must be satisfied in a separately suitable spin-approved airplane; intentional spins are prohibited in the multiengine training aircraft.

Verify aircraft-specific takeoff/landing and OEI performance, authorized maneuver/loading limits, zero-thrust simulation, feather/restart conditions and suitable landing options before asymmetric flight.

steps.title: Teach normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the two-engine systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Teach multiengine systems, performance and normal control
steps.instructor: Require aircraft-specific systems, fuel, propeller, gear and engine-control briefs and performance calculations before dispatch. Observe the candidate teach a normal control transition from the instructor seat and identify workload/scan differences without inventing model-specific settings.
steps.student: Teach the approved preflight/start/taxi/checklist procedures. In the practice area demonstrate level flight, turns, climbs and descents, explaining the aircraft systems/configuration cues. Coach a learner sequence and monitor both engines and the outside environment.
steps.repetitions: One integrated normal-flight demonstration and one coached sequence; ground/start/taxi teaching occurs in the separate preflight and taxi phases.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the specific aircraft’s normal procedures and common flight tasks while maintaining applicable standards and clear control responsibility.
errors: Moving engine/propeller controls as an undifferentiated group -> identify the control and approved purpose before movement.
Focusing on the extra engine instruments while losing attitude/traffic scan -> prioritize flight path and integrate the scan.
steps.stop: No dispatch without verified aircraft procedures and performance. Stop for asymmetric indications, a control misunderstanding, aircraft limit or loss of situational awareness.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F and VIII.A-D; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach normal pattern operations and crosswind judgment
steps.instructor: Let the candidate brief pattern entry, wind correction, runway choice, stabilized approach criteria and a positive control-transfer plan. Act as a learner who overlooks a checklist or misjudges spacing; use a verbal prompt instead of creating an unsafe approach.
steps.student: Teach a normal/crosswind departure and approach using the actual airport procedures. Demonstrate one approach, coach the next, explain workload management and make a planned go-around. Make the landing/go-around decision early enough to preserve options.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration circuit, one coached circuit and one planned go-around as traffic/ATC permit; no forced pattern count.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the airplane within task standards while teaching runway alignment, energy, spacing, communication and a timely go-around.
errors: Talking through final while losing airspeed/alignment -> shorten instruction, regain a stabilized approach or go around.
Treating an ATC instruction as permission to exceed a limit -> request an alternative and protect the aircraft margin.
steps.stop: Go around or discontinue for an unstable approach, unsafe spacing, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or unclear control responsibility. Touch-and-go operations require aircraft/airport authorization.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.A-B and VII.A-B,N; AFH chapters 6, 8-9

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

steps.title: Teach attitude, power, trim and the four fundamentals
steps.instructor: Demonstrate one change at a time: attitude, power, then trim. Give the candidate a desired flight path rather than a control command. Act as a learner who chases an instrument; require the candidate to redirect attention to an outside reference and then verify the result.
steps.student: State the purpose and target; demonstrate level flight, a coordinated level turn, climb and descent. Hand over positively, coach the role-play learner through the same sequence, and ask the learner to explain which change produced the observed result.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached learner attempt of each fundamental; prioritize a weak item for the remaining time.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the briefed commercial-level task tolerances while explaining cause and effect, then identifies and corrects a learner deviation without losing the traffic scan.
errors: Trimming before establishing the attitude/power combination -> stabilize the airplane first and then trim.
Continuous instrument fixation -> restore an outside attitude reference and use the instruments to confirm it.
steps.stop: Stop the exercise for uncoordinated control, an unsafe flight path, traffic conflict or loss of role clarity; reestablish ordinary flight before further explanation.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VIII.A-D; AFH chapter 3

steps.title: Teach wind correction through ground-reference maneuvers
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to select a legal, suitable ground reference and explain wind, traffic, emergency landing options and altitude risks. Role-play a learner who corrects drift with rudder instead of a coordinated bank change.
steps.student: Brief and demonstrate a rectangular course, S-turns or turns around a point as assigned. Explain wind-dependent bank changes and reference selection, coach a learner attempt, and compare the aircraft track with the intended ground path.
steps.repetitions: Two selected reference maneuvers: one demonstrated and one coached circuit each; the remaining variant is carried to review if time is insufficient.
steps.success: Candidate maintains applicable ACS limits, keeps an outside scan and teaches the relationship between ground track, wind and bank without fixation on the point.
errors: Fixating on the reference -> restore the traffic/terrain scan and broaden the visual picture.
Using a fixed bank around the entire ground path -> identify where groundspeed changes and adjust coordinated bank.
steps.stop: Leave the exercise for unsuitable terrain/obstructions, people/property risk, traffic, an unavailable emergency option or a breached altitude margin; do not descend to make the diagram look better.

steps.title: Teach normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the two-engine systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Teach slow flight and configuration effects
steps.instructor: Have the candidate name the selected ACS slow-flight task, its configuration and recovery criterion before changing configuration. Demonstrate changing drag/power while preserving coordination. Role-play fixation on airspeed so the candidate must coach attitude, coordination and warning recognition.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the approved configuration and briefed task condition. Explain how control response and power requirements change; demonstrate straight flight, a turn, climb and descent as applicable. Coach a learner attempt and return to the normal configuration using the aircraft checklist.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one short diagnosis of a deliberately small, safe deviation.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the distinction between slow-flight tasks, uses the appropriate warning/recovery criterion, and maintains applicable ACS tolerances with coordinated control.
errors: Treating the stall-warning condition as the same for every slow-flight task -> restate the selected task criterion.
Trying to climb with pitch alone -> compare the flight-path and airspeed indications, then make the approved power/attitude change.
steps.stop: Recover for an unbriefed stall indication, degraded directional control, traffic conflict or reaching the applicable recovery floor. Never continue merely to consume the block.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.A and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach a power-off stall and its recovery
steps.instructor: Brief whether recovery is at the first indication or after a full stall, as applicable. Observe the candidate explain an approach-to-landing setup. Act as a learner who tries to hold the nose up during recovery; require prompt explanation of angle-of-attack reduction.
steps.student: Clear the area, verify recovery altitude and aircraft authorization, and establish the approved approach configuration. Explain the developing cues during entry. Recover using the aircraft procedure, regain controlled flight, clean up as appropriate, then coach one learner attempt.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached attempt; repeat only if the recovery remains controlled and the planned altitude margin is available.
steps.success: The candidate recognizes the briefed stall condition, reduces angle of attack promptly, maintains coordination, and explains the recovery while meeting the applicable ACS standard.
errors: Watching only the airspeed indicator -> identify aerodynamic and warning cues throughout entry.
Retraction or pitch changes that cause a second stall -> stabilize recovery and follow the approved configuration sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw/incipient spin, a recovery-floor threat, an unbriefed full stall, aircraft limitation, or a trainer intervention. Review the cause before another attempt.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.C and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach a power-on stall without hiding the yaw risk
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to brief approved power and configuration, pitch limits if applicable, and recovery cues. Watch the candidate explain the coordination demand. Introduce an oral learner misconception about correcting yaw with aileron; do not create a hazardous physical error.
steps.student: Clear the area and set the authorized departure configuration/power. Explain the changing control pressures and stall cues, demonstrate the briefed recovery, and coach a coordinated learner attempt. Compare the departure-stall risk with the earlier approach-stall lesson.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration and one coached attempt; one verbal yaw-error diagnosis.
steps.success: Candidate maintains directional control, detects the chosen stall cue, recovers by the approved procedure, and gives an accurate explanation while flying.
errors: Increasing pitch without monitoring coordination -> restore coordinated control and reassess the entry.
Explaining during a developing loss of control -> recover first, then discuss the cue.
steps.stop: Recover immediately for unbriefed yaw/roll, impending spin, an exceeded aircraft limit, or insufficient recovery margin. Do not reproduce a hazardous learner error.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.D and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach coordinated steep turns and workload control
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to brief the applicable bank target, entry speed, power and limitation from the ACS/aircraft documents. Demonstrate a safe learner tendency to lose altitude by discussing it or making only a small recoverable deviation.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the entry condition; demonstrate a coordinated turn in each direction. Explain attitude, back-pressure, power and trim management, then coach a learner through a turn and rollout to the starting heading.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration each direction; one coached attempt in the weaker direction; reset between turns.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable commercial/instructor task standard and diagnoses the cause of altitude/airspeed deviations while retaining coordination and lookout.
errors: Adding more bank to correct an altitude loss -> diagnose the load/attitude problem before the correction.
Rolling out late while explaining -> lead the rollout and divide attention between instruction and the flight path.
steps.stop: Stop for aircraft load/speed limit, loss of coordination, significant flight-path deterioration or traffic conflict. The instructor takes control before the learner error becomes unsafe.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.A; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
Candidate recognizes and diagnoses learner errors, intervenes before unsafe flight and provides a justified performance assessment.
Task mastery is based on observed performance; completing the time block or reading the checklist alone does not complete the lesson.
Observed task outcome: Candidate teaches the distinction between slow-flight tasks, uses the appropriate warning/recovery criterion, and maintains applicable ACS tolerances with coordinated control.
debrief: Candidate first explains which flight/teaching outcome was strongest and identifies one error with its cause.
Compare trainer evidence with candidate self-assessment; distinguish pilot performance from explanation, learner supervision and risk judgment.
Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.
carryForward: Repeat weak slow-flight/stall control before asymmetric work. A full steep-turn instruction cycle may require a later block.
lessons.applicability: Initial AMEL instructor training: common initial-instructor/ground prerequisites apply; do not perform intentional spins in the multiengine airplane.

lessons.title: Coach normal and short-field pattern work
lessons.summary: Teach normal/crosswind and short-field operations, reject judgment and an approved go-around.
objectives: Teach the named tasks through purpose, setup, demonstration, learner practice and an evidence-based assessment.
Teach normal/crosswind and short-field operations, reject judgment and an approved go-around.
Maintain aircraft control, positive flight-control exchanges, traffic protection and aircraft-specific risk/recovery limits while instructing.
prerequisites: Compute takeoff, landing and OEI performance; brief wind/runway/obstacle and go-around limitations.
Before dispatch, enter/brief actual aircraft targets, configuration, authorized simulation methods and task recovery limits from the POH/AFM, current standards and operator procedures.
Use the separate preflight budget for inspection, documents/equipment and current weather/NOTAM/performance checks; do not count this as airborne practice.

steps.title: Teach normal pattern operations and crosswind judgment
steps.instructor: Let the candidate brief pattern entry, wind correction, runway choice, stabilized approach criteria and a positive control-transfer plan. Act as a learner who overlooks a checklist or misjudges spacing; use a verbal prompt instead of creating an unsafe approach.
steps.student: Teach a normal/crosswind departure and approach using the actual airport procedures. Demonstrate one approach, coach the next, explain workload management and make a planned go-around. Make the landing/go-around decision early enough to preserve options.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration circuit, one coached circuit and one planned go-around as traffic/ATC permit; no forced pattern count.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the airplane within task standards while teaching runway alignment, energy, spacing, communication and a timely go-around.
errors: Talking through final while losing airspeed/alignment -> shorten instruction, regain a stabilized approach or go around.
Treating an ATC instruction as permission to exceed a limit -> request an alternative and protect the aircraft margin.
steps.stop: Go around or discontinue for an unstable approach, unsafe spacing, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or unclear control responsibility. Touch-and-go operations require aircraft/airport authorization.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.A-B and VII.A-B,N; AFH chapters 6, 8-9

steps.instructor: Require an actual performance calculation with the selected weight, weather, runway and obstacles. Ask the candidate to compare available distance with the approved takeoff/obstacle profile and to identify reject/continue decisions from the aircraft and conditions.
steps.student: Explain configuration, runway use, approved target speeds and obstacle-clearance path. Demonstrate or coach the assigned short-field takeoff; verify the flight path and checklist transition after obstacle clearance. Teach why a computed capability is not a reason to accept inadequate margin.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff with complete briefing; a second only if runway/traffic/time permit.
steps.success: Candidate uses correct aircraft-specific performance and configuration, achieves the applicable task standard, and explains reject/continue judgment clearly.
errors: Using a memorized generic speed -> locate and use the approved speed for this aircraft/loading.
Skipping the runway/performance comparison -> recalculate before departure.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway/obstacle margin or an unmet aircraft condition. Reject only by the briefed approved procedure; simulated failures must be separately authorized and safely bounded.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.E; AFH chapter 6

steps.title: Teach short-field landing and a safe go-around choice

steps.student: Brief and fly a stabilized short-field approach with the approved configuration and speeds. Explain the aim point versus touchdown point, coach the learner through roundout/landing, and apply approved stopping procedures only after maintaining directional control.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached attempt when traffic permits; any required go-around replaces the landing attempt.
steps.success: Candidate satisfies applicable task accuracy while making a safe approach/landing decision and teaching directional control and energy management.
errors: Stretching a glide to reach the mark -> correct the energy/path while options exist or go around.
Forcing the touchdown after an unstable approach -> go around; record why the original target was not met.
steps.stop: Go around for an unstable path, unsafe wind, runway conflict or inadequate remaining distance. Never force a landing solely to achieve a target mark.

steps.title: Teach engine-failure recognition and OEI maneuvering
steps.instructor: Brief simulation, the aircraft memory/checklist actions, approved speeds/zero-thrust condition, recovery margins and who touches each control. Begin at a suitable altitude with a real landing option; do not create an unannounced critical-engine event.
steps.student: Recognize the announced simulated failure, maintain control and use the approved aircraft sequence to identify/verify the affected engine and reduce drag. Teach aircraft-specific zero-sideslip/performance technique, then coach straight flight and turns with one engine simulated inoperative.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached OEI maneuvering sequence, with normal-power resets as briefed.
steps.success: Candidate teaches accurate identification/verification and maintains control/performance without confusing minimum controllability with climb capability.
errors: Acting on the wrong engine before verification -> maintain control, identify, verify and use the approved checklist.
Allowing airspeed to decay while troubleshooting -> restore the safe aircraft condition before further diagnosis.
steps.stop: Recover for loss of directional control, stall indication, speed/altitude-margin threat or incorrect critical-control selection. No intentional shutdown is included unless the separately briefed feathering gates are satisfied.

steps.title: Teach the effect of drag, airspeed and configuration on OEI performance

steps.student: Demonstrate one change at a time and compare observed performance with the prediction. Explain propeller, gear, flap, sideslip and airspeed effects as applicable, then coach the learner to restore the best approved performance configuration.
steps.repetitions: Three approved comparisons, each followed by a reset; omit any unsupported configuration and carry its required demonstration to suitable equipment.
steps.success: Candidate distinguishes directional control from climb performance, explains the drag penalty and restores a safe aircraft-specific condition.
errors: Changing several variables at once -> reset and isolate one factor.
Assuming positive climb because controllability remains -> consult actual performance and assess terrain/landing options.
steps.stop: Stop for airspeed/control-margin loss, an aircraft restriction or inadequate altitude. Do not sacrifice stall or terrain margin to make the performance loss visually dramatic.
