steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.

steps.title: Teach VMC demonstration and first-cue recovery
steps.instructor: Require the exact aircraft-authorized entry/configuration, applicable ACS recovery limits and a stall-versus-controllability briefing. Explain that published VMC is condition-dependent and is not a safe target for routine engine-out flight. Observe a controlled demonstration only after baseline OEI proficiency.
steps.student: Clear the area and establish the authorized demonstration condition. Explain the developing directional-control or stall cues and recover at the required first cue using the approved power/attitude procedure. Teach how density altitude/configuration may cause a stall cue before directional-control loss.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration; one coached explanation/reset. A second demonstration only with adequate margin and a clear training need.
steps.success: Candidate recognizes the first limiting cue, recovers promptly and explains why the demonstration does not establish a universal operational speed.
errors: Insisting on reaching the published red line -> recover at the applicable first cue instead.
Allowing a stall while searching for yaw -> prioritize the first stall/control warning and terminate the demonstration.
steps.stop: Immediate recovery for stall warning, loss of directional control, an aircraft/ACS limit or declining recovery margin. Never deliberately pursue an uncontrollable condition or apply a generic power/configuration value.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.B and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach the effect of drag, airspeed and configuration on OEI performance
steps.instructor: Have the candidate predict the effect of one approved configuration/airspeed change using actual aircraft data. Announce each change and keep the airplane in an authorized training condition; no low-altitude experiment is permitted.
steps.student: Demonstrate one change at a time and compare observed performance with the prediction. Explain propeller, gear, flap, sideslip and airspeed effects as applicable, then coach the learner to restore the best approved performance configuration.
steps.repetitions: Three approved comparisons, each followed by a reset; omit any unsupported configuration and carry its required demonstration to suitable equipment.
steps.success: Candidate distinguishes directional control from climb performance, explains the drag penalty and restores a safe aircraft-specific condition.
errors: Changing several variables at once -> reset and isolate one factor.
Assuming positive climb because controllability remains -> consult actual performance and assess terrain/landing options.
steps.stop: Stop for airspeed/control-margin loss, an aircraft restriction or inadequate altitude. Do not sacrifice stall or terrain margin to make the performance loss visually dramatic.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.C; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

steps.instructor: Brief runway/performance, the authorized simulation point, ACS simulation restriction, reject action and who manipulates controls. Prefer ground discussion or an approved device until the candidate is proficient; any airplane event is planned and safely bounded.
steps.student: Teach how the aircraft’s takeoff plan establishes a reject decision. In an authorized, prebriefed low-speed simulation, maintain directional control and use the approved stop procedure. After stopping, teach why an attempted airborne continuation could be unsafe.

steps.stop: Never surprise the candidate or simulate outside the applicable ACS/aircraft restriction. Stop for directional-control loss, inadequate runway, traffic or any real abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.E and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 13

Coach the decision among appropriate landing options; distinguish actual aircraft capability from a generic engine-out script.
steps.repetitions: Two verbal takeoff cases with different performance margins; one authorized airborne simulation when appropriate.
steps.success: Candidate maintains control, uses actual performance/terrain to justify the decision and teaches the approved procedure without a universal return altitude or guaranteed climb assumption.
errors: Treating VMC as proof of climb capability -> compare controllability with actual OEI performance.
Following a memorized return-after-takeoff height -> evaluate the aircraft, wind, terrain, obstacles and landing options.
steps.stop: No engine-failure simulation below the applicable ACS/aircraft limits. Recover for stall/control-margin loss or actual malfunction. This guide does not authorize a turnback or a fixed return gate.

steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable task standard while teaching a purposeful scan and preserving positive control transfers and collision avoidance.
errors: Fixating on one indication -> return to an integrated cross-check and verify the flight path.
Letting instruction replace the lookout -> stop the exercise until a qualified outside scan is restored.
steps.stop: Remove the view restriction or terminate for traffic, unclear safety responsibilities, disorientation or control deterioration. The device must not restrict the observing instructor’s view.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XI.A-D; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Teach unusual-attitude recognition and recovery
steps.instructor: Brief safe attitude entry, aircraft limits, recovery method and control transfer. Establish any unusual attitude gently within the authorized training envelope; never surprise the candidate with a dangerous or extreme upset.

errors: Moving controls from an unverified instrument impression -> confirm the attitude/trend promptly before the appropriate recovery.
Pulling while a dangerous bank persists -> use the recovery sequence suited to the condition rather than a generic pull-up.
steps.stop: Terminate for an aircraft limit, aggressive control response, recovery-margin threat or suspected actual instrument failure. Restore normal flight before discussing the event.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XI.E; Instrument Flying Handbook

steps.title: Teach VFR mission monitoring and a diversion decision
steps.instructor: Assign a briefed VFR route and one verbal change in weather, fuel, airspace or destination availability. Observe the candidate teach position verification, actual aircraft performance and a workable diversion. Role-play a learner who keeps the original destination after its margins deteriorate; do not create an actual emergency or airspace violation.
steps.student: Verify present position and compare actual time/fuel with the preflight plan. Explain the route, airspace, terrain, weather and available landing options; choose a suitable diversion, estimate its fuel/time/performance, request help or an amended ATC instruction when appropriate, then coach the learner through the next safe action.
steps.repetitions: One candidate-led position/fuel check and one coached diversion decision; a verbal destination change is enough when a physical diversion would consume the return reserve.

errors: Continuing toward a destination because it was in the original plan -> reassess current weather, fuel, terrain and landing options.
Programming a diversion before securing control and position -> fly, verify position, then manage navigation and communication.
steps.stop: Actual ATC instructions, airspace clearance, weather and aircraft margins govern. End the script if workload, fuel reserve, position uncertainty or a deteriorating landing option threatens the safe return.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 II.G-I, III.C; Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, navigation and aeronautical decision making

steps.title: Teach engine-failure recognition and OEI maneuvering

Teach aircraft-specific zero-sideslip/performance technique, then coach straight flight and turns with one engine simulated inoperative.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached OEI maneuvering sequence, with normal-power resets as briefed.

errors: Acting on the wrong engine before verification -> maintain control, identify, verify and use the approved checklist.
Allowing airspeed to decay while troubleshooting -> restore the safe aircraft condition before further diagnosis.
steps.stop: Recover for loss of directional control, stall indication, speed/altitude-margin threat or incorrect critical-control selection. No intentional shutdown is included unless the separately briefed feathering gates are satisfied.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.A and Appendix 2; AFH chapter 13

steps.stop: Discontinue a training approach before control/performance margins erode. Do not command an unsupported OEI go-around or treat a generic minimum speed as universal.

steps.title: Teach normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the two-engine systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Assess normal operations and landing judgment
steps.instructor: Assess without coaching new technique. Select appropriate preflight/start/taxi teaching and at least the required takeoff/landing tasks for the applicant’s class and rating status. Include a stabilized-approach/go-around decision. Record pilot performance, teaching accuracy, learner-error diagnosis and risk decisions separately. Intervene immediately for safety; intervention ends that assessed attempt.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the task, demonstrates while explaining, supervises the trainer acting as learner, identifies the scripted error and states a justified assessment/correction. Maintain checklist discipline, control transfers and outside/flight-path scan throughout.
steps.repetitions: One assessed demonstration and one learner-error case for each selected task; unobserved items remain unobserved.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable task standards, provides effective instruction and identifies a safe learner error without prompting; selected ground tasks are assessed in briefing/preflight/taxi, not counted as airborne practice.
errors: Deviation outside the task standard -> record the evidence and assign remediation; do not coach it into a pass.
Inaccurate explanation or missed learner hazard -> record the teaching deficiency and stop before it becomes an aircraft-control hazard.
steps.stop: Stop for safety intervention, aircraft/clearance limit, traffic or unsuitable conditions. Record deferred tasks separately from unsuccessful tasks; the clock does not grant completion.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V-VII

steps.title: Teach load factor and accelerated-stall recognition
steps.instructor: Use a ground sketch before flight to distinguish bank angle, load factor and angle of attack. Require approved entry configuration and a recovery at the first indication. Ask the candidate to describe a tightening-turn learner error rather than deliberately provoking an excessive load. In this multiengine airplane verify that the ACS task and manufacturer authorize the selected entry and recovery; use symmetric power and do not allow a demonstration to become an asymmetric controllability exercise.
steps.student: Clear the area, set the aircraft-approved entry condition, demonstrate the applicable turning entry, and recover at the first stall indication. Explain why the indicated airspeed can be higher than in an unaccelerated stall. Coach one safe repetition.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one supervised coached attempt, with a reset between attempts.
steps.success: Candidate links load factor to stall risk, recognizes the first indication, makes a coordinated recovery, and never relies on an airspeed alone as stall protection.
errors: Confusing bank with load factor in every flight condition -> distinguish a coordinated level turn from unloaded flight.
Continuing to pull after the first cue -> reduce angle of attack promptly and return to controlled flight.
steps.stop: Recover for unbriefed yaw/roll, any stall/control-margin threat, a manufacturer limitation or the applicable multiengine recovery-floor threat. Never allow an intentional spin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.E and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach coordinated steep turns and workload control
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to brief the applicable bank target, entry speed, power and limitation from the ACS/aircraft documents. Demonstrate a safe learner tendency to lose altitude by discussing it or making only a small recoverable deviation.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the entry condition; demonstrate a coordinated turn in each direction. Explain attitude, back-pressure, power and trim management, then coach a learner through a turn and rollout to the starting heading.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration each direction; one coached attempt in the weaker direction; reset between turns.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable commercial/instructor task standard and diagnoses the cause of altitude/airspeed deviations while retaining coordination and lookout.
errors: Adding more bank to correct an altitude loss -> diagnose the load/attitude problem before the correction.
Rolling out late while explaining -> lead the rollout and divide attention between instruction and the flight path.
steps.stop: Stop for aircraft load/speed limit, loss of coordination, significant flight-path deterioration or traffic conflict. The instructor takes control before the learner error becomes unsafe.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.A; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach slow flight and configuration effects
steps.instructor: Have the candidate name the selected ACS slow-flight task, its configuration and recovery criterion before changing configuration. Demonstrate changing drag/power while preserving coordination. Role-play fixation on airspeed so the candidate must coach attitude, coordination and warning recognition.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the approved configuration and briefed task condition. Explain how control response and power requirements change; demonstrate straight flight, a turn, climb and descent as applicable. Coach a learner attempt and return to the normal configuration using the aircraft checklist.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one short diagnosis of a deliberately small, safe deviation.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the distinction between slow-flight tasks, uses the appropriate warning/recovery criterion, and maintains applicable ACS tolerances with coordinated control.
errors: Treating the stall-warning condition as the same for every slow-flight task -> restate the selected task criterion.
Trying to climb with pitch alone -> compare the flight-path and airspeed indications, then make the approved power/attitude change.
steps.stop: Recover for an unbriefed stall indication, degraded directional control, traffic conflict or reaching the applicable recovery floor. Never continue merely to consume the block.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.A and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach the effect of drag, airspeed and configuration on OEI performance
steps.instructor: Have the candidate predict the effect of one approved configuration/airspeed change using actual aircraft data. Announce each change and keep the airplane in an authorized training condition; no low-altitude experiment is permitted.
steps.student: Demonstrate one change at a time and compare observed performance with the prediction. Explain propeller, gear, flap, sideslip and airspeed effects as applicable, then coach the learner to restore the best approved performance configuration.
steps.repetitions: Three approved comparisons, each followed by a reset; omit any unsupported configuration and carry its required demonstration to suitable equipment.
steps.success: Candidate distinguishes directional control from climb performance, explains the drag penalty and restores a safe aircraft-specific condition.
errors: Changing several variables at once -> reset and isolate one factor.
Assuming positive climb because controllability remains -> consult actual performance and assess terrain/landing options.
steps.stop: Stop for airspeed/control-margin loss, an aircraft restriction or inadequate altitude. Do not sacrifice stall or terrain margin to make the performance loss visually dramatic.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.C; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

courses.overview: The student in this route is the instructor candidate; the instructor is the qualified trainer who can role-play a learner. The candidate prepares and teaches a measurable preflight lesson, demonstrates while explaining, supervises practice, diagnoses errors and assesses the result. Timing is an adjustable plan. Aircraft inspection/preparation, parked briefing and debrief are separate from the flight block; flight includes taxi, departure/transit, practice and safe return. Repeat or defer tasks until proficiency is demonstrated, and meet actual regulatory experience/endorsement requirements independently.
entryRequirements: Hold an existing instructor certificate/rating and verify pilot multiengine qualifications and applicable 61.191/61.195 authority/experience with the recommending instructor.
Use the correct existing-rating column of the current ACS additional-rating table, then apply every referenced area note; confirm all selected tasks before the final assessment.
Prepare runway-incursion avoidance (II.C), records/endorsements (II.K), OEI performance (II.P) and actual aircraft systems; review prior instructor competencies where needed.
Confirm aircraft-authorized OEI/VMC/feathering procedures and safe practice/landing options; never perform intentional spins in a multiengine airplane.

Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Teach multiengine systems, performance and normal control
steps.instructor: Require aircraft-specific systems, fuel, propeller, gear and engine-control briefs and performance calculations before dispatch. Observe the candidate teach a normal control transition from the instructor seat and identify workload/scan differences without inventing model-specific settings.
steps.student: Teach the approved preflight/start/taxi/checklist procedures. In the practice area demonstrate level flight, turns, climbs and descents, explaining the aircraft systems/configuration cues. Coach a learner sequence and monitor both engines and the outside environment.
steps.repetitions: One integrated normal-flight demonstration and one coached sequence; ground/start/taxi teaching occurs in the separate preflight and taxi phases.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the specific aircraft’s normal procedures and common flight tasks while maintaining applicable standards and clear control responsibility.
errors: Moving engine/propeller controls as an undifferentiated group -> identify the control and approved purpose before movement.
Focusing on the extra engine instruments while losing attitude/traffic scan -> prioritize flight path and integrate the scan.
steps.stop: No dispatch without verified aircraft procedures and performance. Stop for asymmetric indications, a control misunderstanding, aircraft limit or loss of situational awareness.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F and VIII.A-D; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach normal pattern operations and crosswind judgment
steps.instructor: Let the candidate brief pattern entry, wind correction, runway choice, stabilized approach criteria and a positive control-transfer plan. Act as a learner who overlooks a checklist or misjudges spacing; use a verbal prompt instead of creating an unsafe approach.
steps.student: Teach a normal/crosswind departure and approach using the actual airport procedures. Demonstrate one approach, coach the next, explain workload management and make a planned go-around. Make the landing/go-around decision early enough to preserve options.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration circuit, one coached circuit and one planned go-around as traffic/ATC permit; no forced pattern count.
steps.success: Candidate keeps the airplane within task standards while teaching runway alignment, energy, spacing, communication and a timely go-around.
errors: Talking through final while losing airspeed/alignment -> shorten instruction, regain a stabilized approach or go around.
Treating an ATC instruction as permission to exceed a limit -> request an alternative and protect the aircraft margin.
steps.stop: Go around or discontinue for an unstable approach, unsafe spacing, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or unclear control responsibility. Touch-and-go operations require aircraft/airport authorization.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.A-B and VII.A-B,N; AFH chapters 6, 8-9

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.

steps.title: Teach coordinated steep turns and workload control
steps.instructor: Ask the candidate to brief the applicable bank target, entry speed, power and limitation from the ACS/aircraft documents. Demonstrate a safe learner tendency to lose altitude by discussing it or making only a small recoverable deviation.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the entry condition; demonstrate a coordinated turn in each direction. Explain attitude, back-pressure, power and trim management, then coach a learner through a turn and rollout to the starting heading.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration each direction; one coached attempt in the weaker direction; reset between turns.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable commercial/instructor task standard and diagnoses the cause of altitude/airspeed deviations while retaining coordination and lookout.
errors: Adding more bank to correct an altitude loss -> diagnose the load/attitude problem before the correction.
Rolling out late while explaining -> lead the rollout and divide attention between instruction and the flight path.
steps.stop: Stop for aircraft load/speed limit, loss of coordination, significant flight-path deterioration or traffic conflict. The instructor takes control before the learner error becomes unsafe.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 IX.A; AFH chapter 10

steps.title: Teach slow flight and configuration effects
steps.instructor: Have the candidate name the selected ACS slow-flight task, its configuration and recovery criterion before changing configuration. Demonstrate changing drag/power while preserving coordination. Role-play fixation on airspeed so the candidate must coach attitude, coordination and warning recognition.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the approved configuration and briefed task condition. Explain how control response and power requirements change; demonstrate straight flight, a turn, climb and descent as applicable. Coach a learner attempt and return to the normal configuration using the aircraft checklist.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one short diagnosis of a deliberately small, safe deviation.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the distinction between slow-flight tasks, uses the appropriate warning/recovery criterion, and maintains applicable ACS tolerances with coordinated control.
errors: Treating the stall-warning condition as the same for every slow-flight task -> restate the selected task criterion.
Trying to climb with pitch alone -> compare the flight-path and airspeed indications, then make the approved power/attitude change.
steps.stop: Recover for an unbriefed stall indication, degraded directional control, traffic conflict or reaching the applicable recovery floor. Never continue merely to consume the block.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.A and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach a power-off stall and its recovery
steps.instructor: Brief whether recovery is at the first indication or after a full stall, as applicable. Observe the candidate explain an approach-to-landing setup. Act as a learner who tries to hold the nose up during recovery; require prompt explanation of angle-of-attack reduction.
steps.student: Clear the area, verify recovery altitude and aircraft authorization, and establish the approved approach configuration. Explain the developing cues during entry. Recover using the aircraft procedure, regain controlled flight, clean up as appropriate, then coach one learner attempt.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached attempt; repeat only if the recovery remains controlled and the planned altitude margin is available.
steps.success: The candidate recognizes the briefed stall condition, reduces angle of attack promptly, maintains coordination, and explains the recovery while meeting the applicable ACS standard.
errors: Watching only the airspeed indicator -> identify aerodynamic and warning cues throughout entry.
Retraction or pitch changes that cause a second stall -> stabilize recovery and follow the approved configuration sequence.
steps.stop: Terminate for yaw/incipient spin, a recovery-floor threat, an unbriefed full stall, aircraft limitation, or a trainer intervention. Review the cause before another attempt.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.C and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach short-field takeoff planning and execution
steps.instructor: Require an actual performance calculation with the selected weight, weather, runway and obstacles. Ask the candidate to compare available distance with the approved takeoff/obstacle profile and to identify reject/continue decisions from the aircraft and conditions.
steps.student: Explain configuration, runway use, approved target speeds and obstacle-clearance path. Demonstrate or coach the assigned short-field takeoff; verify the flight path and checklist transition after obstacle clearance. Teach why a computed capability is not a reason to accept inadequate margin.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff with complete briefing; a second only if runway/traffic/time permit.
steps.success: Candidate uses correct aircraft-specific performance and configuration, achieves the applicable task standard, and explains reject/continue judgment clearly.
errors: Using a memorized generic speed -> locate and use the approved speed for this aircraft/loading.
Skipping the runway/performance comparison -> recalculate before departure.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway/obstacle margin or an unmet aircraft condition. Reject only by the briefed approved procedure; simulated failures must be separately authorized and safely bounded.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.E; AFH chapter 6

steps.title: Teach short-field landing and a safe go-around choice

steps.student: Brief and fly a stabilized short-field approach with the approved configuration and speeds. Explain the aim point versus touchdown point, coach the learner through roundout/landing, and apply approved stopping procedures only after maintaining directional control.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached attempt when traffic permits; any required go-around replaces the landing attempt.
steps.success: Candidate satisfies applicable task accuracy while making a safe approach/landing decision and teaching directional control and energy management.
errors: Stretching a glide to reach the mark -> correct the energy/path while options exist or go around.
Forcing the touchdown after an unstable approach -> go around; record why the original target was not met.
steps.stop: Go around for an unstable path, unsafe wind, runway conflict or inadequate remaining distance. Never force a landing solely to achieve a target mark.

steps.title: Teach engine-failure recognition and OEI maneuvering
steps.instructor: Brief simulation, the aircraft memory/checklist actions, approved speeds/zero-thrust condition, recovery margins and who touches each control. Begin at a suitable altitude with a real landing option; do not create an unannounced critical-engine event.
steps.student: Recognize the announced simulated failure, maintain control and use the approved aircraft sequence to identify/verify the affected engine and reduce drag. Teach aircraft-specific zero-sideslip/performance technique, then coach straight flight and turns with one engine simulated inoperative.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached OEI maneuvering sequence, with normal-power resets as briefed.
steps.success: Candidate teaches accurate identification/verification and maintains control/performance without confusing minimum controllability with climb capability.
errors: Acting on the wrong engine before verification -> maintain control, identify, verify and use the approved checklist.
Allowing airspeed to decay while troubleshooting -> restore the safe aircraft condition before further diagnosis.
steps.stop: Recover for loss of directional control, stall indication, speed/altitude-margin threat or incorrect critical-control selection. No intentional shutdown is included unless the separately briefed feathering gates are satisfied.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.A and Appendix 2; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach authorized feathering, securing and restart decisions
steps.instructor: Before any actual shutdown/feathering, verify the airplane permits the task, manufacturer conditions, applicable ACS altitude requirement, weather/terrain and a safe airport landing if restart fails. Otherwise use only the permitted simulation and carry required actual demonstration to a suitable opportunity.
steps.student: Explain identifying/verifying the affected engine and the approved feather/secure sequence. Under qualified supervision perform the authorized task or its permitted simulation, teach the loss of associated systems, and follow the manufacturer unfeather/restart procedure when applicable.
steps.repetitions: One fully briefed authorized sequence; a failed restart becomes an emergency, not a repetition opportunity.
steps.success: Candidate follows the aircraft-specific sequence, protects control/performance and can explain when an actual task is unsafe or cannot be completed.
errors: Assuming zero thrust equals a completed actual feather task -> state the demonstration status and record any unmet requirement.
Troubleshooting an unsuccessful restart while losing the landing option -> secure safe flight and treat the situation as an emergency.
steps.stop: No actual shutdown/feathering without all manufacturer/ACS safety conditions and a safe established-airport option. Abort a control error; treat inability to restart/unfeather as an emergency.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.A and Appendix 2; AFH chapter 13; POH/AFM

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.

errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.

steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.

steps.title: Teach VMC demonstration and first-cue recovery
steps.instructor: Require the exact aircraft-authorized entry/configuration, applicable ACS recovery limits and a stall-versus-controllability briefing. Explain that published VMC is condition-dependent and is not a safe target for routine engine-out flight. Observe a controlled demonstration only after baseline OEI proficiency.
steps.student: Clear the area and establish the authorized demonstration condition. Explain the developing directional-control or stall cues and recover at the required first cue using the approved power/attitude procedure. Teach how density altitude/configuration may cause a stall cue before directional-control loss.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration; one coached explanation/reset. A second demonstration only with adequate margin and a clear training need.
steps.success: Candidate recognizes the first limiting cue, recovers promptly and explains why the demonstration does not establish a universal operational speed.
errors: Insisting on reaching the published red line -> recover at the applicable first cue instead.
Allowing a stall while searching for yaw -> prioritize the first stall/control warning and terminate the demonstration.
steps.stop: Immediate recovery for stall warning, loss of directional control, an aircraft/ACS limit or declining recovery margin. Never deliberately pursue an uncontrollable condition or apply a generic power/configuration value.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.B and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach the effect of drag, airspeed and configuration on OEI performance
steps.instructor: Have the candidate predict the effect of one approved configuration/airspeed change using actual aircraft data. Announce each change and keep the airplane in an authorized training condition; no low-altitude experiment is permitted.
steps.student: Demonstrate one change at a time and compare observed performance with the prediction. Explain propeller, gear, flap, sideslip and airspeed effects as applicable, then coach the learner to restore the best approved performance configuration.
steps.repetitions: Three approved comparisons, each followed by a reset; omit any unsupported configuration and carry its required demonstration to suitable equipment.
steps.success: Candidate distinguishes directional control from climb performance, explains the drag penalty and restores a safe aircraft-specific condition.
errors: Changing several variables at once -> reset and isolate one factor.
Assuming positive climb because controllability remains -> consult actual performance and assess terrain/landing options.
steps.stop: Stop for airspeed/control-margin loss, an aircraft restriction or inadequate altitude. Do not sacrifice stall or terrain margin to make the performance loss visually dramatic.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.C; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach a simulated engine failure before takeoff commitment
steps.instructor: Brief runway/performance, the authorized simulation point, ACS simulation restriction, reject action and who manipulates controls. Prefer ground discussion or an approved device until the candidate is proficient; any airplane event is planned and safely bounded.
steps.student: Teach how the aircraft’s takeoff plan establishes a reject decision. In an authorized, prebriefed low-speed simulation, maintain directional control and use the approved stop procedure. After stopping, teach why an attempted airborne continuation could be unsafe.
steps.repetitions: One complete reject briefing; one authorized simulation if conditions permit; verbal decision cases otherwise, with the required flight task carried forward.
steps.success: Candidate makes the correct briefed decision, maintains control and explains the performance/runway limits without inventing a universal commitment speed.
errors: Continuing because the engine loss was expected -> apply the actual reject/continue plan.
Making an unbriefed asymmetric power change -> stop the exercise and rebrief control authority.
steps.stop: Never surprise the candidate or simulate outside the applicable ACS/aircraft restriction. Stop for directional-control loss, inadequate runway, traffic or any real abnormality.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.E and Appendix 3; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach the after-liftoff engine-failure decision safely
steps.instructor: Require actual takeoff/OEI performance, obstacles, landing options and the manufacturer response. Rehearse the low-altitude decision verbally first. steps.student: Teach aircraft control and approved speed/configuration priorities, verify the simulated affected engine, and explain whether available performance supports continued flight. Coach the decision among appropriate landing options; distinguish actual aircraft capability from a generic engine-out script.
steps.repetitions: Two verbal takeoff cases with different performance margins; one authorized airborne simulation when appropriate.
steps.success: Candidate maintains control, uses actual performance/terrain to justify the decision and teaches the approved procedure without a universal return altitude or guaranteed climb assumption.
errors: Treating VMC as proof of climb capability -> compare controllability with actual OEI performance.
Following a memorized return-after-takeoff height -> evaluate the aircraft, wind, terrain, obstacles and landing options.
steps.stop: No engine-failure simulation below the applicable ACS/aircraft limits. Recover for stall/control-margin loss or actual malfunction. This guide does not authorize a turnback or a fixed return gate.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.F and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 13

lessons.timingLabel: Original SUAREZ.CFI pacing proposal; no publisher target or regulatory minimum. Repeat/extend for proficiency.

steps.title: Teach normal taxi, runway boundaries and checks
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate teach the aircraft start/checklist and airport route. Use a verbal learner error about a hold-short point, control positioning or system indication; avoid creating a real incursion or control error.
steps.student: Candidate explains the diagram/clearance and wind-control positioning; uses the actual checklist, monitors the two-engine systems, maintains directional control and stops before uncertainty turns into movement.
steps.repetitions: One actual taxi/check sequence; brief aircraft start/preflight outside the logged flight-time block.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the reason for checks and runway boundaries, not merely a memorized route; airport movement stays safe.
errors: Doing checklist/programming with inadequate lookout -> stop before the head-down task.
Assuming the next runway crossing is authorized -> verify clearance and markings before moving.
steps.stop: Stop for unclear crossing authority, abnormal indications, unsafe distraction or directional-control concern.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V.A-D,F; VI.A; current airport diagram; aircraft checklist

steps.title: Teach the briefed takeoff, climb and transit
steps.instructor: Have the candidate state runway/wind/performance and the approved departure/reject plan. Observe aircraft control and concise instruction; any learner-error role-play remains within a safe envelope.
steps.student: Candidate explains the approved configuration/speeds and departure path, teaches the selected takeoff, completes climb checks and navigates to the safe practice area with a traffic scan and clear control exchanges.
steps.repetitions: One assigned takeoff and transit; return reserve takes precedence over adding another maneuver.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the aircraft-specific departure correctly and reaches the practice area with control, checklist and traffic awareness intact.
errors: Using a generic target speed/configuration -> identify the approved aircraft value before departure.
Long explanation during a critical flight-path change -> shorten instruction and fly first.
steps.stop: Do not depart with inadequate performance/runway margin. Stop the exercise for traffic, weather, aircraft limit or loss of clear control responsibility.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VII.A,E,N as applicable; aircraft takeoff/climb checklist

steps.title: Assess normal operations and landing judgment
steps.instructor: Assess without coaching new technique. Select appropriate preflight/start/taxi teaching and at least the required takeoff/landing tasks for the applicant’s class and rating status. Include a stabilized-approach/go-around decision. Record pilot performance, teaching accuracy, learner-error diagnosis and risk decisions separately. Intervene immediately for safety; intervention ends that assessed attempt.
steps.student: Candidate briefs the task, demonstrates while explaining, supervises the trainer acting as learner, identifies the scripted error and states a justified assessment/correction. Maintain checklist discipline, control transfers and outside/flight-path scan throughout.
steps.repetitions: One assessed demonstration and one learner-error case for each selected task; unobserved items remain unobserved.
steps.success: Candidate meets the applicable task standards, provides effective instruction and identifies a safe learner error without prompting; selected ground tasks are assessed in briefing/preflight/taxi, not counted as airborne practice.
errors: Deviation outside the task standard -> record the evidence and assign remediation; do not coach it into a pass.
Inaccurate explanation or missed learner hazard -> record the teaching deficiency and stop before it becomes an aircraft-control hazard.
steps.stop: Stop for safety intervention, aircraft/clearance limit, traffic or unsuitable conditions. Record deferred tasks separately from unsuccessful tasks; the clock does not grant completion.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 V-VII

steps.title: Teach slow flight and configuration effects
steps.instructor: Have the candidate name the selected ACS slow-flight task, its configuration and recovery criterion before changing configuration. Demonstrate changing drag/power while preserving coordination. Role-play fixation on airspeed so the candidate must coach attitude, coordination and warning recognition.
steps.student: Clear the area; establish the approved configuration and briefed task condition. Explain how control response and power requirements change; demonstrate straight flight, a turn, climb and descent as applicable. Coach a learner attempt and return to the normal configuration using the aircraft checklist.
steps.repetitions: One demonstration sequence; one coached sequence; one short diagnosis of a deliberately small, safe deviation.
steps.success: Candidate teaches the distinction between slow-flight tasks, uses the appropriate warning/recovery criterion, and maintains applicable ACS tolerances with coordinated control.
errors: Treating the stall-warning condition as the same for every slow-flight task -> restate the selected task criterion.
Trying to climb with pitch alone -> compare the flight-path and airspeed indications, then make the approved power/attitude change.
steps.stop: Recover for an unbriefed stall indication, degraded directional control, traffic conflict or reaching the applicable recovery floor. Never continue merely to consume the block.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 X.A and Appendices 2-3; AFH chapter 5

steps.title: Teach engine-failure recognition and OEI maneuvering
steps.instructor: Brief simulation, the aircraft memory/checklist actions, approved speeds/zero-thrust condition, recovery margins and who touches each control. Begin at a suitable altitude with a real landing option; do not create an unannounced critical-engine event.
steps.student: Recognize the announced simulated failure, maintain control and use the approved aircraft sequence to identify/verify the affected engine and reduce drag. Teach aircraft-specific zero-sideslip/performance technique, then coach straight flight and turns with one engine simulated inoperative.
steps.repetitions: One candidate demonstration and one coached OEI maneuvering sequence, with normal-power resets as briefed.
steps.success: Candidate teaches accurate identification/verification and maintains control/performance without confusing minimum controllability with climb capability.
errors: Acting on the wrong engine before verification -> maintain control, identify, verify and use the approved checklist.
Allowing airspeed to decay while troubleshooting -> restore the safe aircraft condition before further diagnosis.
steps.stop: Recover for loss of directional control, stall indication, speed/altitude-margin threat or incorrect critical-control selection. No intentional shutdown is included unless the separately briefed feathering gates are satisfied.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIII.A and Appendix 2; AFH chapter 13

steps.title: Teach system-failure recognition and checklist discipline
steps.instructor: Choose two aircraft-applicable scenarios and state which indications are simulated. Require the candidate to distinguish an indication failure from a physical aircraft failure and to justify any checklist selection.
steps.student: Explain the indications, control/flight-path consequences and appropriate aircraft checklist. Teach a role-play learner to prioritize the aircraft, verify the diagnosis, request assistance and decide whether to continue, divert or land.
steps.repetitions: Two verbal/simulated scenarios with no unsafe system disablement; candidate leads one and coaches one.
steps.success: Candidate selects applicable procedures without unsupported memory actions, maintains safe flight and teaches a reasoned landing/diversion decision.
errors: Choosing a checklist from one alarming indication -> cross-check and identify the actual problem.
Pulling a breaker or moving a critical control without authorization -> stop simulation and use the approved aircraft procedure.
steps.stop: Do not create a real malfunction to simulate one. Stop for actual abnormal indications, a prohibited equipment action, workload saturation or loss of flight-path control.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XII.C; AFH chapter 18; aircraft POH/AFM

steps.title: Teach return, final landing and safe runway exit
steps.instructor: Require the candidate to choose an appropriate airport/pattern entry, wind/runway and landing plan. Observe concise teaching and a timely go-around decision; keep the final landing independent of a maneuver repetition count.
steps.student: Candidate teaches arrival/pattern communication and spacing, uses the approved descent/landing checklist, flies a stable approach, makes a safe landing/go-around decision and controls rollout/runway exit.
steps.repetitions: One final landing or safe go-around/alternative; pattern module repetitions occur within their own allocated blocks.
steps.success: Candidate maintains the applicable landing standard and supervises the learner without sacrificing spacing, runway alignment or energy control.
errors: Rushing the return to meet the timer -> maintain a safe return/landing reserve and defer incomplete practice.
Unstable approach or runway conflict -> go around rather than force completion.
steps.stop: Go around/choose a safe alternative for unstable approach, runway conflict, wind/aircraft limit or inadequate landing margin.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 VI.B,VII.B,F,N as applicable; aircraft landing checklist

steps.title: Teach after-landing, shutdown and postflight findings
steps.instructor: Observe the candidate wait until clear of the runway to teach noncritical checks, then supervise the actual parking/shutdown/secure sequence. Ask what equipment discrepancy or learner issue needs follow-up.
steps.student: Candidate announces runway-clear status, teaches the approved after-landing actions, taxis/parks safely, completes the shutdown/secure procedure and reports aircraft discrepancies before debrief.
steps.repetitions: One actual after-landing/taxi/parking sequence; discussion after shutdown belongs to the separate debrief.
steps.success: Aircraft is secured by its checklist; candidate teaches workload timing and identifies unresolved equipment/safety concerns.
errors: Starting a noncritical checklist on the runway -> exit safely first.
Calling the flight complete without reporting a discrepancy -> document/report the issue through the operator’s process.
steps.stop: Stop movement/checks for a taxi conflict or real abnormality; no instruction takes priority over aircraft control and safe parking.
steps.reference: FAA-S-ACS-25 XIV.A; aircraft after-landing/shutdown checklist

completion: Candidate performs the selected applicable tasks to the current certificate/rating skill standard while giving accurate, effective instruction.
Candidate recognizes and diagnoses learner errors, intervenes before unsafe flight and provides a justified performance assessment.
Task mastery is based on observed performance; completing the time block or reading the checklist alone does not complete the lesson.

Observed task outcome: Candidate meets the applicable task standards, provides effective instruction and identifies a safe learner error without prompting; selected ground tasks are assessed in briefing/preflight/taxi, not counted as airborne practice.
debrief: Candidate first explains which flight/teaching outcome was strongest and identifies one error with its cause.
Compare trainer evidence with candidate self-assessment; distinguish pilot performance from explanation, learner supervision and risk judgment.
Review the lesson-specific carry-forward item and choose the next practice or assessment before dispatch.
Use the first task block’s error/recovery evidence to explain whether the candidate’s next learner lesson should repeat, simplify or progress.
carryForward: Patch any documented coverage gap before the mock assessment; review prior instructor knowledge as needed without pretending the added-rating table prohibits evaluation of other topics.
